rows.key_quote: Revenue of $35.1 million beat the high end of guidance and grew 34% year-over-year, driven by record orders of $49.4 million including a record $23.9 million in back-end semiconductor orders. Gross margin expanded to 47.7%, exceeding guidance due to favorable product mix, while operating expenses remained flat sequentially. Management raised the full-year 2026 tax rate expectation to approximately 20% and provided Q4 revenue guidance of $34-$36 million.

KLX Energy Services reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $186 million, beating the high end of guidance and up 11% sequentially, while Adjusted EBITDA reached $25 million (13.4% margin), in line with guidance. The company successfully closed a backstopped rights offering that converted $88 million of debt to equity and raised $37 million new equity, reducing net leverage to approximately two times. Management highlighted strong sequential growth across all three segments, particularly in the Rockies where Adjusted EBITDA doubled.

Orion Properties reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues of $35.4 million, a decline from $37.1 million in the prior year quarter, alongside a net loss of $3.3 million compared to a profit of $69 million last year. Management raised the 2026 Core FFO guidance range to $0.75-$0.78 per share from the previous $0.72-$0.77, citing strong leasing activity despite a smaller portfolio and higher strategic review costs. The company maintained its dividend at $0.02 per share and improved its Net Debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio to 5.6x.

Oklo reported a year-to-date net loss of $123.3 million and cash used in operating activities of $110.9 million for the first nine months of FY2026. Management highlighted significant progress at Aurora-ID, including PDSA approval by the DOE and structural steel installation, while Groves-1 remains operational. The company raised its capital position with $2.3 billion raised via ATM offerings, bringing total cash and marketable securities to $3.1 billion.

Nutex Health reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $217.6 million, a 19.7% decrease from the prior year period, driven by higher collections in 2025 and normalization of revenue per visit after initial IDR process success. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $63.9 million for the quarter and $211.4 million for the first nine months versus 2025, while net income dropped to $40.2 million in Q3 despite a strong balance sheet with $249.9 million in cash. Management noted stabilization of revenue trends but declined to provide specific guidance for the remainder of 2026 or 2027.

NOG reported record quarterly results with Adjusted EBITDA up 15% year-over-year and total production rising 19% YoY, driven by a 39% increase in natural gas volumes. Management raised full-year 2026 production guidance to 147,000-150,000 BOE per day and updated cost guidance based on improved realizations. The company ended the quarter with $1.6 billion in liquidity and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.45 per share.

MTD reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $1.1 billion (up 6% in USD and local currency) and adjusted EPS of $12.57 (up 13%). Management raised full-year 2026 local currency sales growth guidance from 4-5% to approximately 5%, while providing initial 2027 guidance for roughly 5% sales growth and adjusted EPS between $52.50-$53.50.

MSC Income Fund reported Q3 FY2026 results with an annualized return on equity of 9.7% and NAV per share increasing to $16.56. Adjusted net investment income (ANII) was $0.34 per share, while total dividends for the upcoming quarter are set at $0.36 per share. The fund's private loan portfolio saw a net decrease of $11 million due to slower investment activity in a subdued market environment.

MSDL reported Q3 FY2026 net investment income of $0.48 per share, an increase from $0.45 in the prior quarter, though total investment income declined due to mark-to-market losses and lower non-recurring revenue. The board approved a fee reduction effective January 1, 2027, and declared a quarterly supplemental dividend alongside the regular distribution. NAV declined to $18.76 from $19.50 in the prior period driven by realized losses on the restructuring of BrightPet and unrealized depreciation.

Moderna reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.3 billion, representing a 29% year-over-year increase and generating $200 million in net income. Management raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to a range of 15%-25%, exceeding the prior framework of up to 10% growth. The quarter was highlighted by FDA approval for mFLUSIVA, positive Phase III data for Intismeran in melanoma showing a 42% reduction in recurrence or death risk, and the successful completion of a $3 billion convertible debt financing.

Total revenue increased 7.5% to $208 million in the third quarter, driven by growth in Middle Market and larger transaction segments, while Private Client Market revenue rose 4%. Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly to $8.2 million from $6.9 million a year ago, though net income remained low at $1 million due to talent retention expenses. Management noted that interest rate volatility remains a significant headwind causing deal delays and repricing, leading them to remain measured in near-term expectations for Q4.

Mercer International reported Q3 FY2026 operating EBITDA of -$3 million, an improvement from -$21 million in the prior quarter, driven by a lower non-cash inventory impairment of $8 million compared to $29 million previously. The company executed a pre-packaged Chapter 11 restructuring agreement reducing senior note debt by approximately 88% and injecting liquidity via a new rights offering, with completion expected by the end of 2026. While pulp sales realizations remained flat due to soft demand and maintenance downtime, management noted that supply constraints are beginning to balance market weakness.

Main Street Capital reported Q3 FY2026 results with Net Investment Income (NII) of $142.5 million, a 1.9% increase year-over-year but a 4.7% decrease quarter-over-quarter. Distributable Net Investment Income (DNII) before taxes per share was $0.98, which was in line with prior guidance and slightly lower than the prior year and quarter. NAV per share increased to a record $34.22 driven by net fair value appreciation of $40.9 million in the lower middle market portfolio.

Consolidated net revenue declined 3.2% year-over-year to ARS 270.1 billion, driven by a 6.3% drop in cement volumes and a 23.2% fall in concrete revenues due to soft activity and adverse weather. Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 74 basis points to 20.1%, while the railroad segment turned negative at -11%. Management noted that September's volume rebound suggests demand is responsive to weather, but bagged cement recovery remains uncertain pending real economy improvements.

Third quarter sales increased 3% to $499 million driven by volume growth in Performance Chemicals and Class I crossties, but Adjusted EBITDA fell 18% to $58 million due to higher raw material and logistics costs. Management revised the full-year 2026 earnings outlook lower to reflect these persistent cost pressures that outweighed benefits through September. While year-to-date free cash flow hit a record $92 million, pricing actions to recover absorbed costs are not expected until January 2027.

Kingstone reported a record Q3 with net income of $17.6 million ($1.19 EPS), representing a 62% increase year-over-year driven by a 14.5% rise in direct premiums written to $86.8 million and an underlying loss ratio improvement of 10.6 points to 33.5%. Management raised full-year 2026 diluted EPS guidance to $2.70-$2.90 from the prior range of $2.20-$2.90, while narrowing the combined ratio outlook to 79%-83% and updating premium growth expectations to approximately 16%. The company noted that California expansion is significantly below initial plans due to market reopening and competitive pressure, though it remains on track for its $500 million direct written premium goal by year-end 2029.

PAGP reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $711 million, reflecting benefits from operating efficiencies and the sale of its Canadian NGL business. Management narrowed full-year 2026 guidance to a range with a midpoint of $2.88 billion, implying approximately $700 million for Q4, which is down roughly $10 million from Q3 due to market conditions and transition costs associated with the Silver Creek acquisition. The company successfully optimized its balance sheet by raising $1.5 billion in junior subordinated notes and redeeming preferred securities.

KBDC reported Q3 FY2026 net investment income of $0.46 per share, up from $0.42 in the prior quarter, with a dividend coverage ratio of 115%. The company declared a regular quarterly dividend of $0.40 per share for Q4 and maintained its commitment to sustain this base dividend through 2026 despite NAV declines driven by idiosyncratic credit losses. Management highlighted that SOFR expectations rising above 4% provide a tailwind, while new originations averaged 538 bps over SOFR.

IAMGOLD reported Q3 FY2026 attributable production of 186,900 oz and adjusted net earnings of $237 million ($0.42/share), driven by a strong gold price environment averaging over $500 above guidance assumptions. The company remains on track to meet full-year consolidated guidance while executing significant capital return initiatives, including the repurchase of 50% of its gross margin royalty at Côté for approximately $525 million and continued share buybacks funded by cash from Essakane. Management expressed confidence in Q4 production strength led by Côté and noted that unit costs are trending down as operations stabilize post-contractor crushing.

Third quarter revenue increased 2% sequentially to $827 million, but Adjusted EBITDA returned to positive at only $6 million after narrowing losses from the prior quarter. Management noted that revenue was slightly below expectations due to shipment timing issues, customer delivery delays, and component availability constraints. The company announced a major restructuring program targeting $100 million in annual cost reductions by 2029, alongside the discontinuation of hydrogen solutions and electric terminal tractor programs.

Humana raised its full-year adjusted EPS outlook from at least $9 to at least $9.50 based on Q3 performance that exceeded initial expectations. Management highlighted strong execution in Medicare Advantage membership and CenterWell growth, alongside a significant one-time tailwind from Bonus Year 2028 Stars results exceeding Top Quartile goals. The company expects to utilize some of this tailwind for investments while passing the remainder to shareholders, though specific quantification is pending further data.

Helios Technologies reported record third quarter sales of $230 million, exceeding the high end of its August outlook by $8 million. Adjusted diluted EPS increased 11% to $0.80, beating the high end of guidance, while gross margin expanded 10 basis points to 33.2%. Management raised full-year 2026 sales guidance to a range of $895-$902 million, citing improved second-half demand and contributions from recent acquisitions.

HHH reported Q3 FY2026 with Vantage delivering $76.6 million of net pre-tax profit and real estate generating strong same-store NOI growth of 9%. Consolidated results included a non-cash GAAP loss of $105 million from the sale of municipal utility district receivables, which generated $177 million in net cash proceeds. Management raised guidance for the asset-light transition, expecting significant progress on joint ventures and capital redeployment by year-end.

HEI reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP net income of $35.5 million ($0.20/share), driven by a $64 million pre-tax gain from watching American Savings Bank shares and unrealized gains, which masked a core earnings decline to $23 million ($0.13/share) due to storm-related expenses. Consolidated liquidity stands at approximately $1.3 billion, with management planning to finance the remaining wildfire settlement payment via debt or convertible debt rather than equity. The company is awaiting a Public Utilities Commission decision on rate rebasing expected in mid-to-late April 2027.

Total revenue of $972 million beat the high end of updated guidance by approximately $7 million, driven by political advertising revenue of $198 million which exceeded its range and set a new record. Management raised full-year 2026 political guidance to $630-$640 million and provided Q4 political guidance of $319-$329 million. The company announced plans to reduce debt by an additional $175-$200 million in the fourth quarter using political cash flow.

Gran Tierra reported a net loss of $42 million in Q3 FY2026 compared to $25 million income in the prior quarter, driven by $30 million in stock-based compensation and $29 million in derivative losses. Adjusted EBITDA declined to $68 million from $85 million sequentially due to lower realized prices in South America (Brent down ~$5.40) and wider discounts. The company generated positive free cash flow of approximately $1 million, but production fell 4% sequentially to 39,904 bpd due to asset dispositions and a joint venture adjustment.

GSBD reported Q3 FY2026 net investment income of $35.3 million, a decline from the prior quarter's $42.2 million, driven by a smaller portfolio size and investments placed on non-accrual status. The company reduced its net debt to equity ratio to 1.21x from 1.35x and executed share repurchases of approximately $15 million. Management noted that while new deal activity remained light due to softer M&A volumes, they continue to deploy capital selectively at attractive spreads.

Granite Ridge Resources reported a strong Q3 FY2026 with Adjusted EBITDAX rising 35% sequentially to $107.3 million and oil volumes growing 16%, driven by an 8% increase in average daily production and a recovery in Waha gas basis. Management raised full-year production guidance to a range of 34,000-35,000 BOE per day with a higher oil mix, while also authorizing a new $35 million share repurchase program. The company highlighted the successful transition to free cash flow positivity and the addition of Arete Creek Resources as a third operated partner in the Permian.

Gogo reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $213.2 million, down 5% year-over-year and 4% sequentially, driven by the expected transition from legacy ATG to next-generation products. While Galileo shipments hit a record 172 units (up 59% sequentially) and military/government revenue grew 36% year-over-year, total service revenue declined 4% due to lower ATG volumes. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue of $870-$895 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $175-$185 million, noting that the revised range includes reduced litigation expenses following a court ruling.

Global Partners reported a significant beat in Q3 FY2026 with net income of $52.4 million versus $29 million in the prior year and adjusted EBITDA of $122.9 million versus $98.8 million. Management raised full-year maintenance CapEx guidance to $65-$75 million from a previous range, while maintaining expansion CapEx estimates unchanged. The company highlighted strong execution across its integrated model, with wholesale product margins increasing $33.4 million and retail station operations holding steady despite lower fuel volumes.

PAA reported strong Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $711 million, reflecting benefits from operating efficiencies and the sale of its Canadian NGL business. Management narrowed full-year 2026 guidance to a range with a midpoint of $2.88 billion, implying approximately $700 million for Q4, which is down roughly $10 million from Q3 due to lower market opportunities and transition costs associated with the Silver Creek acquisition. The company successfully optimized its balance sheet by raising $1.5 billion in junior subordinated notes and redeeming preferred securities.

Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported record quarterly Adjusted EBITDA of $52.4 million and adjusted net income of $33.6 million in Q3 FY2026, driven by a 31% year-over-year increase in TCE rates to $20,414 per day. Terminal revenue surged 73% year-over-year due to new port operations, while the company generated $57 million in operating cash flow and completed a refinancing that lowers borrowing costs. Management expressed confidence in firm market fundamentals for 2027 but declined to provide specific guidance on terminal growth or Q4 results.

Fluor reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $3.7 billion (up from $3.4 billion YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.77 (up from $0.68 YoY). The company delivered record new awards of $10.9 billion, raising backlog to $34.3 billion, while maintaining full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $500-$525 million despite a potential $2 billion scope reduction on one reimbursable project. Management expressed confidence in the pipeline and reiterated plans for continued share repurchases.

Starwood Property Trust reported Distributable Earnings (DE) of $0.31 per share for Q3 FY2026, excluding realized gains and losses from commercial lending resolution which were $0.41 per share. The company increased its CECL reserves by approximately $337 million to $822 million due to higher interest rates, while resolving $254 million of non-accrual and REO assets including the sale of two multifamily properties. Management noted that the stock price implies a significant discount to book value relative to their diversified business mix.

Under Armour reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.2 billion, a 7% decline year-over-year, with adjusted operating income meeting expectations despite the miss on top-line growth. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance at a mid-single-digit decline but lowered the gross margin outlook by 50 basis points due to elevated supply chain costs and inventory actions. The company emphasized a strategic shift toward simplifying its product assortment and improving marketing efficacy to stabilize North American demand.

Under Armour reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.2 billion, a 7% decline year-over-year, with adjusted operating income meeting the lowered outlook but missing prior expectations due to macro headwinds and inventory actions. Management maintained full-year guidance for mid-single-digit revenue declines while narrowing the gross margin outlook range, citing extended Middle East conflict costs and higher freight expenses. The quarter highlighted strategic shifts including a 50% SKU reduction and a transition of the youth apparel business to an expanded licensing model.

Canopy Growth reported Q2 FY2027 consolidated net revenue of CAD 81.4 million, a 22% year-over-year increase driven by a 30% rise in cannabis revenue and a 141% surge in international business. Adjusted gross margin held firm at 31%, while Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to CAD 2.9 million despite the absence of Q1 tariff refunds. Management raised expectations for the back half of the year, citing seasonality in Storz & Bickel and full-year impact from cultivation yield improvements expected in FY2028.

Franklin Templeton reported strong Q4 FY2026 results with adjusted operating income increasing 17.6% to $598.6 million and adjusted operating margin expanding 380 bps to 31.8%. The company ended the quarter with $1.8 trillion in AUM, driven by record inflows across ETFs, Canvas, and private markets, while maintaining positive long-term net flows for the 11th consecutive month. Management raised fiscal 2029 targets for private markets fundraising, ETFs, and Canvas, citing a diversified business model and strong momentum ahead of plan.

Ziff Davis reported Q3 FY2026 revenues of $289.3 million and adjusted EBITDA of $82.2 million, both broadly in line with prior guidance but representing declines from the prior year period. Management noted that while organic Google referrals declined approximately 37% year-over-year, revenue declines were narrower due to portfolio diversification and sequential margin improvements driven by cost discipline and AI efficiencies. The company highlighted strong performance in specific areas like IPVanish growth and Humble Bundle volume, but acknowledged persistent headwinds from search traffic disruption and a weak gaming ad market ahead of GTA VI.

Third quarter revenue was $76.2 million, up from $44.8 million in the prior quarter, driven by HPC lease revenue of $63.0 million representing 83% of total revenue. GAAP net income swung to a profit of $709.9 million compared to a loss in Q2, primarily due to non-cash fair value adjustments and gains on asset sales. Management reaffirmed cost guidance for the WULF Compute project at approximately $8.9 million per megawatt, within the original range, while highlighting robust demand and secured financing structures including Google credit support.

Wheaton Precious Metals reported Q3 FY2026 production of 231,000 gold equivalent ounces (GEOs), a 13% year-over-year increase driven by the BHP Antamina stream and new assets like Koné and Kurmuk. Revenue reached $772 million, up 62% year-over-year due to higher sales volumes and realized prices, while net earnings rose 12% to $410 million. Management maintained its full-year 2026 production guidance of 860,000-940,000 GEOs and reaffirmed the long-term target of 1.2 million GEOs annually by 2030.

rows.key_quote: Vistra delivered record adjusted EBITDA of $2.378 billion in Q3 FY2026, representing a more than 50% increase year-over-year driven by higher realized prices and capacity revenue. Management narrowed its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range to $7.1-$7.5 billion with a higher midpoint than originally provided, while also introducing new 2027 guidance of $7.7-$8.5 billion. The company successfully closed the Cogentrix acquisition and reaffirmed its capital allocation priorities including share repurchases and dividends.

VEON reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.31 billion (up 17.2% YoY) and EBITDA of $577 million (up 10.1% YoY), driven by a 46% surge in digital services revenue. Management raised the lower end of full-year 2026 guidance, projecting revenue growth of 16%-18% and EBITDA growth of 10%-12%. Operating cash flow increased 47% year-to-date to $1.3 billion, while leverage improved to 1.05x.

Consolidated service revenue declined 1% year-over-year to CAD 4.5 billion, while adjusted EPS fell to CAD 0.16 from CAD 0.24 due to a non-cash goodwill impairment of CAD 800 million in TELUS Health. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for flat-to-negative revenue and negative EBITDA growth, citing lower Digital results and one-time items from the prior year. The company announced a transformation strategy targeting CAD 900 million in annualized cash savings by 2028 to fund debt reduction and organic growth.

Interface reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $366.7 million, a slight miss on the low end of guidance due to timing shifts in retail billings and softer European demand. Adjusted earnings per share of $0.68 beat expectations, driven by margin expansion that offset higher input costs from tariffs and energy prices. Management reaffirmed full-year earnings guidance but lowered the net sales outlook to reflect the challenging macro environment in Europe.

TDS reported a decline in total operating revenues of 3% and Adjusted EBITDA missed expectations due to legacy revenue pressures and higher costs associated with fiber expansion. Consequently, management lowered its full-year 2026 guidance for both telecom revenues ($990M-$1.01B) and Adjusted EBITDA ($290M-$310M). While TDS Telecom achieved record fiber address delivery of 76,000 in the quarter, Array Digital Infrastructure maintained its full-year outlook unchanged despite the withdrawal of the proposed merger with TDS.

Suzano reported Q3 FY2026 results with combined EBITDA down 14% quarter-over-quarter due to operational challenges at the Pine Bluff mill and higher SG&A/logistics costs, though pulp sales volumes remained solid. Management updated full-year 2026 cash cost guidance from BRL 800/ton to approximately BRL 825/ton citing persistent Middle East conflict impacts on energy/commodities and a stronger USD. The Arbex acquisition is integrated with Q3 results in line with plans, but the company remains focused on deleveraging and efficiency capture rather than new capital allocation.

Strawberry Fields REIT reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $40 million, a modest increase of $0.3 million year-over-year, while net income declined to a loss of $14.8 million due to a one-time $24.6 million foreign currency transaction loss on bond redemptions. Management highlighted the completion of a Kansas City acquisition and the pending closing of an Indiana deal, with a pipeline of approximately $123 million expected to close before year-end. Excluding the FX loss, underlying earnings grew by roughly 11% compared to the prior year period.

Pembina reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of CAD 1.128 billion, a 9% year-over-year increase driven by premium propane prices in Asian markets and higher NGL margins. The company updated its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range to CAD 4.45-4.55 billion (raised from the prior CAD 4.35-4.55 billion) and stated it is trending toward the upper end of this range. Management highlighted strong execution on new assets like RFS IV and Greenlight, with nearly CAD 3 billion in projects sanctioned since April.

The E.W. Scripps Company reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $546 million ($373M Local Media + $173M Networks), which was up 19% YoY primarily due to record political advertising revenue of $81 million in Local Media, while core advertising revenue declined 13%. Segment profit surged to $151 million compared to $50 million a year ago. Management provided Q4 guidance expecting Local Media revenue growth in the low-to-mid-40% range and Scripps Networks revenue down in the high single-digits due to soft direct response markets, noting that core advertising will be displaced by the election cycle.

SiriusPoint reported a strong Q3 FY2026 with core gross written premium growing 14% to $991 million and net earned premiums up 19%. The company achieved a core combined ratio of 90.1%, resulting in underwriting income of $76 million, while operating earnings per share rose 19% year-over-year to $0.88. Management announced a Loss Portfolio Transfer (LPT) agreement with RiverStone to remove legacy runoff exposures, which is expected to free up over $200 million in capital and increase the BSCR ratio by approximately 20 points upon completion.

Sylvamo reported Q3 FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $128 million (20% margin) and Adjusted Operating Earnings of $1.33 per share, driven by favorable price/mix and operational improvements despite higher input and transportation costs. Management announced a binding offer to watch its Europe business for approximately EUR 50 million in working capital and EUR 35 million net cash, with closing expected by Q1 2027. While the company remains focused on North America and Latin America, it noted that annualized input and transportation costs are up approximately $50 million compared to 2025 levels.

Skyward Group reported Q3 FY2026 gross written premiums up 9% to $803 million and fee-generating gross written premiums up over 18% to $517 million. Diluted operating earnings per share increased 22% to $1.28, with a consolidated combined ratio of 89.9%. Management reaffirmed full-year premium guidance near the upper end of the original range of $2.65 billion-$2.8 billion.

Sunstone Hotel Investors reported Q3 FY2026 Adjusted EBITDAre of $54.5 million (up 9% YoY) and Adjusted FFO per share of $0.20 (up 18% YoY), driven by total portfolio RevPAR growth of 11.4%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for rooms RevPAR to a range of 9.5%-10.5% and total RevPAR to 8.5%-9.5%, citing strong group booking velocity in Orlando and recovery at Wailea Beach Resort. The company repurchased nearly $200 million of stock year-to-date, reducing the share count by nearly 6.5% and increasing NAV.

SABESP reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net revenue of BRL 6 billion (organic growth of 9%) and adjusted EBITDA of BRL 3.6 billion (up 14% YoY), driven by a 7.7% price contribution and 2.1% volume gain, partially offset by higher refunds and mix effects. Cash generation remained solid with operating cash flow at BRL 2 billion, while CapEx accelerated to BRL 4.5 billion in the quarter. Management provided no specific revenue guidance for the full year due to high uncertainty regarding El Niño rainfall impacts on consumption volumes.

RGA reported Q3 FY2026 pre-tax adjusted operating income of $736 million ($8.49 EPS), driven by strong investment income and favorable claims experience across all regions. Management highlighted a robust pipeline in the U.S. PRT and U.K. longevity markets, with new business momentum continuing globally. The company returned $139 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends while fully deploying Ruby Re capital.

Ring Energy reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $102.3 million, down 2% sequentially despite a 12% decline in realized oil prices, supported by improved natural gas and NGL realizations. Adjusted EBITDA rose 5% to $57.1 million with margins expanding to 56%, while adjusted free cash flow increased 7% to $50.4 million due to deliberate capital acceleration. Management raised full-year 2027 production guidance, projecting oil volumes of 13,200-14,300 bpd and total sales volumes of 21,000-23,000 boe per day.

Regency Centers reported exceptional Q3 FY2026 results with same-property NOI growth of 5.1% in the quarter and 4.4% year-to-date, driven by record occupancy levels reaching 97% leased and strong rent spreads averaging 12%. Management raised its full-year 2026 guidance for same-property NOI growth to a midpoint of 4.25% or higher and increased Core Operating EPS guidance to 5.7%, citing robust demand and a disciplined capital allocation strategy.

Ready Capital reported a GAAP loss of $0.40 per share and a distributable loss of $0.53 per share for Q3 FY2026, driven by $53.9 million in realized losses from asset resolutions. While recurring revenue improved to $20.7 million and operating expenses declined to $47.6 million, the company reduced its dividend to $0.01 per share following the completion of a liquidity plan that repaid $649 million of debt. Management targets breakeven distributable earnings in early 2027.

Q3 FY2026 QPU-related services revenue grew 53% YoY to EUR 3.1 million, but total revenues declined to EUR 3.3 million from EUR 5.7 million in the prior year due to a lack of QPU sales and lower government grants. Management explicitly stated that the quarter was not strong on reported financials, noting that order book levels remained stable rather than growing significantly.

Third quarter revenue was $7.3 million, up 67% year-over-year, driven by a shift toward PSQ Payments and credit originations while operating expenses were cut in half to $5.5 million. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance of $32 million in revenue and positive non-GAAP operating income, noting that the fourth quarter is expected to be the largest in company history due to seasonality and new integrations. Operating cash burn decreased to $1.7 million for the quarter, excluding one-time costs.

PPL reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS of $0.49 and adjusted earnings from ongoing operations of $0.54, beating the narrowed full-year forecast range of $1.92-$1.96 with a midpoint target of $1.94 for the nine months ended. Management raised the long-term annual EPS growth target to 7%-9% through 2030 and extended the capital plan to $25 billion from 2027-2030, driven by strong data center pipeline conversion in Pennsylvania and Kentucky. The company announced a collaboration with QTS for approximately 2 GW of generation capacity in Pennsylvania via Invitium Energy, providing meaningful upside potential.

FNF reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net earnings of $352 million ($1.32/share), missing the prior year's $439 million due to lower investment income and a sale of an F&G subsidiary, while GAAP net earnings were boosted by $29 million in recognized gains. Title segment revenue grew 11% YoY but margins compressed to 17.1% from 17.8% as the company invested heavily in recruiting (adding ~300 people) and acquisitions ahead of productivity ramp-up. Management noted a sequential decline in purchase orders driven by high mortgage rates and seasonality, with expectations for margin pressure in Q4 before potential recovery in 2027.

Galiano Gold reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $172 million and adjusted EBITDA of $93.3 million, driven by production of 40,922 ounces (up 19% from Q2) and an average realized gold price of $4,247/oz. Operating cash flow strengthened to $57 million compared to $40 million in the prior year quarter. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 AISC guidance between $2,300 and $2,600 per ounce, noting Q3 costs of $2,346/oz were within this range.

FTAI Infrastructure reported a record quarter with Adjusted EBITDA of $95.3 million, driven by strong railroad performance and terminal growth. The company closed the sale of Long Ridge Power & Gas for approximately $1.5 billion in proceeds to repay debt, significantly reducing leverage. Management raised full-year guidance expectations citing double-digit revenue and EBITDA growth driven by organic volume/rate gains, the USD acquisition closing mid-November, and Repauno phase two completion.

F&G reported adjusted net earnings of $96 million ($0.74 per share) for Q3 FY2026, which was in line with expectations but missed the prior year due to lower alternative investment returns and a one-time actuarial assumption adjustment. Gross sales reached a record $3 billion in the quarter, driven by core retail sales of $2.1 billion (up 24% YoY), while AUM before reinsurance grew 7% to $76.2 billion. Management maintained its long-term return expectations for alternative investments at 12% despite Q3 volatility and reaffirmed its disciplined capital allocation strategy.

Baytex reported Q3 FY2026 production of 71,600 BOE/d (up 5% YoY) and generated CAD 139 million in free cash flow while returning CAD 165 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends. Management raised the full-year 2026 exploration and development expenditure guidance from CAD 625 million to CAD 665 million, citing improved Duvernay performance and heavy oil activity. The company accelerated its Duvernay commercialization plan, now targeting 25,000 BOE/d by late 2028 (1.5 years earlier than previously planned), supported by a three-year outlook of 8%-10% annual production growth.

Total revenue declined 7.5% year-over-year to BRL 123.3 million in Q3, driven by lower client activity and reduced capital market issuances due to election-related volatility. Management adopted a conservative balance sheet stance, reducing securities warehousing and leverage, while announcing an interim dividend of BRL 0.12 per unit. Forward guidance remains muted with expectations for deal delays rather than mortality, pending a resolution in the macroeconomic and political landscape.

Q3 FY2026 U.S. comparable restaurant sales grew 190 bps while traffic declined 180 bps, with average check rising 370 bps driven by pricing partially offset by mix headwinds. Adjusted diluted EPS was a loss of $0.17 compared to a smaller loss last year, and adjusted operating margin contracted 50 bps due to higher restaurant expenses from turnaround investments and COGS inflation. Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $0.97-$1.02 from the prior $0.90-$1.00 range but tightened Q4 comp sales guidance to 0%-1% citing holiday calendar shifts, a decision to delay pricing actions at Outback and Bonefish, and avoiding dilutive traffic.

Third quarter Adjusted EBITDA of $124.3 million met expectations and grew 12% YoY, while RevPAR growth of 7.5% fell short of the anticipated 8.2% due to slower occupancy growth during the summer watching season. Management lowered full-year 2026 guidance for Adjusted EBITDA to $495-$502 million and RevPAR growth to 7.4%-7.9%, citing the occupancy miss, a fire at a Mississippi community, and increased marketing spend as key factors. The company continues its portfolio optimization strategy, having sold 23 owned communities and acquired 17 previously leased ones, with ownership expected to reach approximately 80%.

Brookfield Infrastructure Partners reported FFO of $717 million ($0.91 per unit) for Q3 FY2026, representing the third consecutive quarter of meeting its 10% FFO per unit growth target driven by organic growth and asset commissioning. Management reiterated confidence in closing the year with strong performance and achieving the full-year 10% FFO growth target, while noting that corporate simplification is expected to close on November 19th. The company deployed approximately $1.8 billion of equity year-to-date across new investments and organic projects.

Banco de Chile reported Q3 FY2026 net income of CLP 288 billion and a return on average equity of 19.9%, driven by a 4.4% net interest margin and contained cost of risk at 0.96%. Management raised full-year guidance for profitability to 22% ROAC and efficiency ratio to 36%, while adjusting loan growth expectations to 5%-6% due to the current economic slowdown. The bank maintained its strongest capital position with a CET1 ratio of 14.1% and regained market share in commercial loans.

BBDC reported a stable quarter with NAV per share of $10.92, largely unchanged from the prior period, and net investment income of $27.2 million which fully covered the $0.26 quarterly dividend. The company addressed its largest near-term refinancing risk by pricing a $400 million CLO financing to repay maturing notes ahead of schedule. While non-accruals ticked up modestly to 1.1% of the portfolio, excluding assets covered by a credit support agreement, they remained below 1%.

Brookfield Asset Management reported Q3 FY2026 fee-related earnings of $864 million ($0.54/share) and distributable earnings of $763 million ($0.47/share), both up 15% year-over-year. Fee-bearing capital grew 13% to $682 billion, driven by record fundraising including $25 billion in the quarter and approximately $50 billion in infrastructure commitments over the past year. Management noted that reported earnings were modestly below early-year expectations due to a timing shift in fee recognition for the flagship infrastructure fund and the deferral of BBU performance fees, rather than underlying business weakness.

Aura Minerals reported record Q3 FY2026 results with production of 96,000 gold equivalent ounces (up 27% QoQ) and revenues of $386 million. The company reiterated its full-year guidance for production between 340,000 and 390,000 ounces and sustaining cash costs below $2,000/oz, citing strong performance in Borborema and Apoena alongside the ongoing turnaround at MSG. Management highlighted a recurring free cash flow of $124 million, which funded dividends, buybacks, and expansion CapEx.

Third quarter adjusted net EPS increased to $0.11 from $0.09 last year, driven by favorable weather and new rates, though GAAP earnings missed due to wildfire insurance costs and higher OpEx. The company remains on track to meet its full-year 2026 adjusted net EPS guidance of $0.35-$0.37 per share. Management reaffirmed the 2027 guidance range of $0.38-$0.42 per share while noting that the recent sale of Suralis was largely neutral for 2026 due to tax impacts.

Pro forma consolidated revenue declined 1.5% year-over-year to a net loss of $2.1 billion for the quarter, driven by a one-time franchise impairment charge of approximately $6.3 billion at Legacy Charter and lower residential revenue. Adjusted EBITDA declined 4% year-over-year, excluding transition expenses related to the Cox acquisition which closed mid-quarter. Management announced a new operating model focused on returning to growth and efficiency, targeting an additional $2 billion in annualized run-rate cost savings over the next 18 months.

Apple Hospitality reported Q3 FY2026 comparable hotels RevPAR growth of 7.3% and total revenue growth of 8.2%, driven by a shift toward higher-rated business travel and group bookings. Management raised full-year guidance for RevPAR growth to a midpoint of 5.6% (up 235 bps) and Adjusted EBITDA margin to 35.25% (up 105 bps), citing strong October performance and limited new supply. The company sold three hotels for approximately $72 million, bringing total dispositions since early 2025 to $154 million.

Anika reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $30.6 million, a 10% year-over-year increase driven by 17% growth in the commercial channel and 5% in the OEM channel. Gross margin expanded to 62% from 56% last year, though it was sequentially lower than Q2 due to product mix impacts including the reintroduction of Hyalomatrix. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 6%-10% and adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to 15%-17%, while reaffirming flat-to-5% growth for 2027.

Alpha Metallurgical Resources reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $29.4 million and shipped 3.9 million tons, an increase from the prior quarter's 3.5 million tons. Management provided full-year 2027 guidance for shipments between 14.3 million and 15.7 million tons and costs between $104-$110 per ton. The company highlighted a two-year timeline to replace a damaged stacker reclaimer at DTA, noting that while logistics flexibility exists, the asset remains a constraint.

AirSculpt reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $31.9 million, an 8.7% year-over-year decline driven by a 9.6% drop in case volume and higher customer acquisition costs due to Google AI Overviews. Management lowered full-year 2026 guidance for both revenue ($144M-$146M vs $151M-$157M) and adjusted EBITDA ($9M-$10M vs $12M-$14M), assuming Q3 trends will persist into Q4. The company successfully refinanced its term loan to 2031, ending the quarter with approximately $20 million in total liquidity.

AHR reported Q3 FY26 total same-store NOI growth of 13.8%, with SHOP segment NOI accelerating to 28.2% YoY and Trilogy at 15.7%. The company raised full-year 2026 NFFO per diluted share guidance to $2.23-$2.26 (up from $2.15-$2.19) and increased same-store NOI growth guidance to 12%-14%.

Assured Guaranty reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted operating income of $86 million ($1.94 per share), down from $124 million ($2.57 per share) in the prior year quarter, primarily due to a lack of recovery benefits on U.S. RMBS exposures compared to last year. The company generated $280 million of PVP in the first nine months of 2026, representing a 44% increase from the same period in 2025 and only $6 million less than total full-year 2025 production. Management raised its full-year 2026 financial guaranty PVP guidance to more than $400 million, citing strong pipeline and growth in shorter-duration structured finance.

Ameren reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $2.17 per share, beating the prior year's $2.17 and GAAP EPS of $2.42 versus $2.35 last year. Management raised its 2026 EPS guidance range to $5.35-$5.55 from $5.25-$5.45 and issued new 2027 guidance of $5.70-$5.90 per share. The company outlined a five-year capital plan of $38.1 billion (up >20% YoY) to support 13.3% compound annual rate base growth through 2031.

TDS and Array reported Q3 FY2026 results where TDS Telecom delivered a record 76,000 fiber addresses but total operating revenues declined 3% YoY due to legacy pressures and divestitures. Consequently, management lowered its full-year 2026 guidance for telecom revenues ($990M-$1.01B) and adjusted EBITDA ($290M-$310M), while increasing CapEx guidance by $100M to support accelerated fiber builds. Array reported strong organic growth in cash site rental revenue but noted the withdrawal of TDS's acquisition offer, with its own full-year outlook remaining unchanged.

ACRE reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP net income of $10 million ($0.18 EPS) and Distributable Earnings of $6.7 million ($0.12 EPS), driven by a $300,000 realized gain on the sale of a North Carolina office REO property. The company ended the quarter with available capital of $116 million and a net debt-to-equity ratio of 1.9x, while fully repaying a term loan subsequent to quarter-end. Management maintains a cautious stance focused on resolving risk-rated four and five loans totaling approximately $160 million in carrying value.

CGBD reported Q3 FY2026 net investment income of $25 million ($0.36 per share), which was in line with expectations and fully covered the declared Q4 dividend of $0.35 per share. Total investment income rose to $63 million from $62 million, driven by higher JV dividends, while expenses remained flat at $38 million. The company maintained a resilient portfolio of $2.3 billion despite muted origination volume due to macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty.

Atmus reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $510 million, a 14% increase year-over-year driven by organic growth and the Koch Filter acquisition, with adjusted EPS of $0.77 beating the prior year's $0.69. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $2.01 billion-$2.035 billion (midpoint +15% vs 2025) and raised adjusted EPS expectations to $2.90-$3.05, while maintaining the EBITDA margin guidance of 19.75%-20.25%. The company returned $25 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends and paid down $100 million in debt.

Calumet reported an exceptional Q3 FY2026 with $347 million of Adjusted EBITDA and a record $80 million from Montana Renewables in its first full quarter. The Specialty Products segment delivered $248 million of Adjusted EBITDA, more than tripling the prior year's $80.2 million, driven by specialty material margins exceeding $108 per barrel. Management highlighted strong demand durability and a completed Shreveport turnaround, while noting that Performance Brands margins are lagging due to input cost lags.

Devon Energy reported Q3 FY2026 results with oil and total production within guidance, reaching all-time highs, while beating cash cost guidance by 2%. The company generated $3.5 billion in discretionary cash flow and $2 billion in free cash flow, accelerating buybacks to nearly 9 million shares ($414 million) alongside a quarterly dividend of $0.32 per share. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 production and cost guidance while providing an initial 2027 outlook assuming the Eagle Ford divestiture closes early next year.

Total revenue increased 8.6% year-over-year to $622.1 million, driven by a 4.9% rise in patient visits and higher revenue per visit. Adjusted EBITDA grew 17.9% to $140.2 million with an expanded margin of 22.5%. Management raised its full-year 2026 guidance for both revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, citing strong performance across all regions and end markets.

Fidus reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted NII of $0.54 per share, driven by a 24% increase in interest income from larger average loan balances and fee income from True Environmental repayments. The company maintained its portfolio at $1.4 billion fair value with no debt investments on non-accrual. Management expects M&A activity to lift in Q4 due to improved deal flow, though equity realizations are expected to remain limited.

Essent Group reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $163 million ($1.82 EPS), down from the prior quarter's $2.08 EPS, driven by a higher provision for loss and lower investment income. Insurance in force grew modestly to $250 billion while persistency declined to 83% amid high mortgage rates affecting refinancing volume. Management raised guidance for the effective tax rate to approximately 17-18% and maintained a constructive long-term view on housing demand despite near-term flatness.

EOG delivered record oil, NGL, and natural gas production in Q3 FY2026 with total per-unit cash operating costs and DD&A coming in below guidance midpoints. The company raised its regular dividend by 8% to an indicated annual rate of $4.40 per share for 2027 and returned approximately $1.5 billion to shareholders via dividends and buybacks. Management remains constructive on oil fundamentals, anticipating low single-digit oil production growth in 2027 while maintaining a pristine balance sheet.

Enbridge reported strong operational and financial performance for Q3 FY2026, with Adjusted EBITDA increasing by CAD 167 million compared to the prior year quarter. Management reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance, expecting results to finish at the midpoint of the range despite lower liquid market access contributions and higher financing costs. The company also announced significant strategic transactions, including a CAD 3 billion equity offering and acquisitions of Tallgrass's crude transportation business and Salt Creek Midstream's crude gathering assets.

Elanco reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.265 billion, an 11% increase on a reported basis and 9% organic growth driven by volume (5%) and price (4%). The company significantly outperformed guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS ($0.27), leading to a full-year guidance raise with organic revenue growth updated to approximately 8% and adjusted EPS raised by $0.06 at the midpoint to $1.17-$1.20. Gross margin expanded 300 basis points to 56.1%, while net leverage improved to 2.9x.

VAALCO Energy reported Q3 FY2026 results with NRI production increasing over 20% quarter-over-quarter to 18,454 barrels per day and adjusted EBITDAX reaching $71.1 million, driven by the restart of Côte d'Ivoire and drilling in Gabon and Egypt. Management raised Q4 sales volume guidance to a range of 21,000-22,800 NRI barrels per day (approx. 18% higher than Q3 actuals) while maintaining full-year CapEx guidance despite expanding the Egyptian budget. The company highlighted strong pricing premiums in Gabon and Côte d'Ivoire, though noted $22 million in realized hedging losses.

Edenor reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of ARS 1,123 billion, up 14% year-to-year in real terms driven by tariff adjustments and a 1.3% increase in customers to 3.42 million. Distribution margin rose 5% year-to-year to ARS 434 billion, while EBITDA for the first nine months reached ARS 506 billion (excluding a one-off gain). The company highlighted successful debt normalization with CAMMESA and an upcoming acquisition of MetroGAS.

Emera reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of CAD 0.85 and year-to-date adjusted EPS of CAD 2.90, representing a modest 3% decrease in quarterly earnings compared to last year but remaining on track for its 5%-7% compound annual growth target through 2030. Management introduced an updated five-year capital plan of CAD 21.5 billion, approximately 5% higher than the prior plan, which excludes asset sales and relies more heavily on equity funding via DRIP and ATM programs. The company reaffirmed its commitment to affordability while investing in reliability, data center growth, and renewable generation across Florida and Nova Scotia.

DraftKings reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.33 billion, a 16% year-over-year increase driven by strong Sportsbook and new Predictions growth. However, the company lowered its full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $175 million-$275 million from the prior range of $700 million-$900 million, primarily due to increased investment in the Predictions business which resulted in Q3 Adjusted EBITDA of -$317 million. Management remains confident in the core business's trajectory and the long-term value of the Predictions cohort despite regulatory uncertainties.

Delek US reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $1.13 billion ($18.22 EPS) and adjusted EBITDA of $1.28 billion, driven by strong refining margins and a $60 million Enterprise Optimization Plan (EOP) contribution. Management raised 2026 EBITDA guidance to $530-$560 million and increased the quarterly dividend by 18% to $0.30 per share while executing $50 million in buybacks. The company expects approximately $425 million in proceeds from Small Refinery Exemptions (SREs) in Q4.

Dauch Corporation reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $2.91 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.22, missing the prior year's adjusted EPS of $0.30 due to lower production volumes on Ram heavy-duty programs (down ~15% YoY) and GM downtime. Adjusted EBITDA was $358 million (12.3% margin), down from 13.0% last year, reflecting inflationary pressures and one-time commercial settlements. Management updated full-year guidance to a sales range of $10.8-$10.875 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $1.35-$1.375 billion, tightening the outlook from the prior $10.6-$10.8 billion and $1.36-$1.425 billion ranges respectively.

Docebo reported a strong Q3 FY2026 quarter with EBITDA growing approximately 34% while top-line revenue grew 12.8% in Q4 (guidance), following sequential growth of 12.4% in Q3. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to a midpoint of 14%, citing a rebound year and strong pipeline, particularly in the government vertical which exceeded expectations. The company announced an approximate $60 million one-time special dividend funded by remaining debt capacity, leaving a net debt position of approximately $108 million.

CareTrust REIT reported Q3 FY2026 normalized FFO per share of $0.54 and normalized FAD per share of $0.53, representing a 20% increase over the prior year quarter. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance for normalized FFO per share to a range of $2.08-$2.09 and normalized FAD per share to $2.04-$2.05. Management highlighted record investment activity totaling approximately $2.9 billion year-to-date, including the acquisition of 23 LNT homes for $733 million.

Camden Property Trust reported Q3 core FFO of $1.71 per share, beating the $1.69 midpoint guidance, driven by higher third-party construction fees and interest income. Management lowered full-year same-store revenue growth guidance from 0.5% to 0.0% due to greater-than-anticipated seasonality in September, while maintaining the core FFO midpoint at $6.75 per share. The company also canceled two planned acquisitions and paused development projects in Nashville and Denver to preserve liquidity.

DKL reported Adjusted EBITDA of $143 million in Q3 FY2026, which was in line with the prior year period and met expectations. Management raised full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $530-$560 million. The company completed its first sour gas compressor station and AGI well at the Libby Complex, driving an increase in Gathering and Processing EBITDA to $88 million.

Chesapeake Utilities reported a strong third quarter with adjusted net income up 12% and adjusted EPS rising 9% year-over-year. Adjusted gross margin expanded 9% to approximately $149 million, driven by interim rate recognition of $2.7 million for the Florida City Gas case and contributions from transmission expansion projects. The company remains on track for its full-year capital guidance of $550-$600 million after investing $413 million year-to-date.

Rigel reported Q3 FY2026 net product sales of $72.3 million, up 13% YoY, driven by $6.6 million from newly launched VEPPANU (six weeks of availability) on top of TAVALISSE $46 million (+3%), REZLIDHIA $9.9 million (+20%), and GAVRETO $9.8 million (-11%). Total revenues were $80.9 million with net income of $13.2 million, down from $27.9 million a year ago on higher costs and expenses of $63.8 million. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was narrowed to $290-$295 million from $285-$295 million, while the non-VEPPANU product sales range was trimmed to $255-$260 million from $255-$265 million and contract revenue raised to $35 million. Management struck an upbeat tone on the VEPPANU launch (100+ patients in six weeks, 88% PA approval) and reiterated R289 dose selection and registrational trial initiation plans for 2027.

Research Frontiers reported Q3 FY2026 fee income of roughly $77,000 versus roughly $359,000 a year earlier, with the prior-year period including non-recurring government contract royalty revenue, and a net loss of about $510,000 versus just under $300,000. Cash at September 30 was about $645,000 with roughly $538,000 in working capital. Management said it does not expect material royalty recovery until after Q4 2026, tied to Gauzy's court-approved Israeli settlement, October financing, and initial payments toward restarting emulsion production in Israel and film coating in Germany. The company also disclosed NASDAQ listing notices on bid price and market value of listed securities, with a board decision on a hearing request possible in December.

Riley Permian reported Q3 FY2026 oil production of 25.4 MBbl/d, up 20% QoQ and 38% YoY, with total production of 42 MBOE/d, up 23% sequentially, despite wells turned to sales coming in below the low end of guidance. Cash flow from operations was $111 million, up 75% QoQ, and debt was reduced by $28 million to $245 million. Management did not provide formal 2027 guidance but previewed 30%-40% YoY oil and total production growth with a two-rig program and added ~90 net San Andres locations at Red Lake, while Q4 CapEx is expected to rise and full-year CapEx guidance increases. The quarter showed strong production conversion, but the soft well count and higher CapEx, plus withheld formal guidance, temper the read.

Royal Gold reported record revenue of $465 million (up 84% YoY) on record volume of 109,000 GEOs, with record adjusted net income of $238 million ($2.80/share) and record operating cash flow of $344 million (up 98% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA margin increased to 84%, and the company fully repaid its revolver to become debt-free after quarter end. Management raised full-year guidance for other metals and expects silver and copper at or above the top end of ranges, while gold sales remain on track around the midpoint; Kansanshi copper guidance was narrowed and Andacollo guided to the low end. Portfolio developments include a Kinross buyback of 25% of the Great Bear royalty (~$43 million) in Q4, RIGI approval at MARA, and a temporary production suspension at Antamina following a fatality.

Regenxbio reported Q3 2026 cash, equivalents, and marketable securities of $251 million versus $241 million at year-end 2025, driven by a $100 million AbbVie NAAVIGATE milestone and $108 million in net proceeds from a July public offering; the total excludes a $39 million October Sarepta settlement payment. Royalty revenue came in slightly above one analyst's model on Itvisma pickup as U.S. Zolgensma IP has expired, though no explicit revenue or EPS figures were disclosed. Management guided to cash runway into late Q4 2027, spanning sura-vec wet AMD top-line data this quarter, a Q1 2027 RGX-202 BLA filing (switched from rolling to a single submission), and a 2027 sura-vec regulatory submission, with RGX-202 potential U.S. approval in H2 2027. No hard revenue, EPS, or margin results were reported, leaving the quarter defined by pipeline milestones rather than financial performance.

Perimeter Group reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $223.5 million, up 20% YoY, on net sales of $389.9 million, which fell 24% (prior-year sales included a large one-time item). Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.85 versus $0.82, and GAAP net income was $304.5 million ($1.74/diluted share). Fire Safety EBITDA rose 14% to $201.6 million at a 64.5% margin, essentially flat YoY despite the federal retardant pricing step-down, while Specialty Products EBITDA more than doubled to $21.9 million from $9.1 million. Management guided Q4 Specialty Products EBITDA only modestly below its year-to-date quarterly average despite near-zero PDI contribution, and reiterated unchanged long-term cash flow assumptions, with net debt leverage down to 2.7x from 3.1x.

Q3 FY2026 total revenues were $33 million, down $244.8 million year-over-year, driven by a $128.6 million unrealized Babcock & Wilcox loss versus a $30.2 million prior-year gain, producing a net loss of $243 million and diluted LPS of $6.04; Adjusted EBITDA was negative $219.1 million while Operating Adjusted EBITDA was $2.9 million. Service and fee revenues fell $58.2 million to $112.5 million on lower ATM/private placement/underwriting fees and lower SpaceX carried interest, partly offset by $6.3 million higher M&A and advisory fees. The capital markets segment posted negative $90.2 million of revenue and a $120 million segment loss; communications income rose to $13.2 million and Targus lost $4.3 million. Management gave no formal guidance beyond calling Operating Adjusted EBITDA 'on plan' for the year, citing up to $50 million in expected SpaceX cash inflows to fund the $164 million December senior note redemption and the pending Sangoma acquisition, which is targeted to close in January 2027 and add $35-40 million of EBITDA.

RLJ reported comparable RevPAR of $153, up 9.7% YoY, on ADR +6.4% to $203 and occupancy +230 bps to 75.4%, with each month beating expectations. Hotel EBITDA rose 17.5% to $93.9 million at a 26.5% margin (up 190 bps), adjusted EBITDA was $85 million (+17.3%), and adjusted FFO per share was $0.34 (+25.9%). Full-year comparable RevPAR guidance was raised to 5.75%-6.25% (up 200 bps at the midpoint), and corporate adjusted EBITDA guidance rose $9 million at the midpoint to $352-$358 million. The company also sold seven Chicago Midway hotels for $110 million at a 14x 2026 forecasted EBITDA multiple.

Q3 FY2026 revenue fell 1.1% to $506.5M as attendance dropped 4.7% (~320,000 guests) on weather, calendar and international headwinds, partly offset by total revenue per capita up 3.8%. Adjusted EBITDA declined $11.2M to $205.1M and net income fell to $80.0M from $89.3M; nine-month revenue was down 1.6% and Adjusted EBITDA down $31.4M. Management gave no formal 2026 or 2027 guidance, declining to commit to Q4 EBITDA growth given continued weather disruption, but cited a positive paid pass base (+0.3% through October), 2027-specific pass products up over 15%, deferred revenue up 4.9%, and a new $40M-$50M 2027 gross cost-savings target on top of the $50M 2026 program. The company bought back ~$218M of stock (~12% of shares) year-to-date but made no Q3 purchases due to cash flow timing.

First quarter as Real REMAX Group: revenue $728M up 28% YoY (pro forma combined ~$770M, +20%), Adjusted EBITDA $34M up 66%, but GAAP operating loss of $72M and net loss of $67.2M driven by $78.7M of non-recurring acquisition costs. Management introduced 2027 guidance of $2.6-2.8B revenue and $175-190M Adjusted EBITDA on assumptions of 5-10% lower existing home sales and 3-4% lower prices, and Q4 revenue of $575-625M with $32-38M EBITDA. Cost actions exceeded plan — $40M+ gross savings actioned and 2027 synergy target lifted above $30M versus the original $30M — but North American RE/MAX agent count fell 3% and management off-boarded over 1,000 agents, with Tamir calling 2027 'another very challenging year.'

Adjusted operating revenues rose 8% to $902 million and diluted adjusted operating EPS rose 7% to $6.77, but adjusted net operating income grew only 2% to $209 million on a smaller remeasurement gain ($9 million vs $23 million prior year). The investments business set records, with total ISP sales up 19%, variable annuities up 29%, managed accounts up 27%, AUM up 10% to $140 billion, and $407 million of net client flows. Term life was the weak spot: issued policies fell 7%, premiums fell 5%, and recruiting declined 10% year-over-year, with management guiding full-year 2026 issued policies down 8%-10% and year-end sales force down about 3%. Q4 guidance points to term life issued policies down low-single-digits and ISP sales up mid-single-digits.

Reforation reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue up 19.1% YoY to $173.6 million, its 22nd consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with DTC up 16.7% to $152.8 million and wholesale up 40.8% to $20.8 million. Gross margin expanded 250 bps to 60.4% (200 bps excluding ~$800,000 of tariff refunds) and adjusted EBITDA rose 64.2% to $23.1 million at a 13.3% margin, though GAAP swung to a $1.1 million net loss ($0.02/share) on $10.5 million of IPO-related stock comp and a 165.9% effective tax rate. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $610-612 million (20-21% growth, above the mid-to-high teens algorithm) and put adjusted EBITDA margin at ~14.2%, the high end of the prior range. Q4 is framed as prudent given a back-half-weighted holiday and a dynamic macro backdrop.

Q3 FY2026 net sales were $202.1M, down 1% YoY but up 32.5% sequentially from $152.5M, with net income of $29.9M ($1.30/diluted share) versus $1.20 a year ago. Gross margin expanded to 29.7% from 23.9% YoY, though that included a $3.8M tariff refund worth ~188 bps, and operating income was a record $40.9M (20.2% margin); operating cash flow was $40.9M and net cash reached ~$34M. Management raised its second-half outlook to net sales above 2H 2025 (prior: roughly in line), but guided Q4 gross margin down from Q3 on the non-recurring tariff refund plus a modest mix-driven further decline, and said it is not predicting a specific data center revenue level. Oil and gas softness continued (Power Systems sales down $6.2M YoY), partly offset by data center demand, and a new $220M three-year revolver cut borrowing spread 80 bps to SOFR+180.

Q3 revenue grew 5.4% YoY to $109 million but declined sequentially, with defense tech revenue down YoY (~16% per Q&A) on UAS shipment timing while space rose over 30% organically. Gross margin hit a record 32.3% (vs 16.3% a year ago), backlog rose 14.3% sequentially to a record $619.7 million on 1.73 book-to-bill, but the quarter still showed a $23.2 million net loss and negative $5.3 million Adjusted EBITDA. Management reaffirmed the full-year 2026 revenue range of $450-500 million, citing backlog and $46.8 million of WIP/finished goods inventory now up $10.6 million sequentially, and attributed near-term lumpiness to milestone and delivery timing.

Radian reported Q3 2026 revenue of $624 million, more than double year-over-year with Inigo included, adjusted pre-tax operating income of $254 million, and adjusted net operating income of $1.44 per diluted share, up 25% YoY, with operating ROE of 16% versus roughly 13% a year earlier. Mortgage insurance generated $206 million of adjusted pre-tax operating income at a 37% combined ratio on record $286 billion primary insurance in force, while specialty net premiums earned fell 3% YoY to $311 million but produced an 80% combined ratio aided by $43 million of favorable prior-period development and benign catastrophe activity. Full-year buybacks of $379 million, or 8% of beginning shares, far exceeded the prior $200-$250 million guide, and the Q4 dividend from Radian Guaranty of $145 million lifts the 2026 total to $660 million versus initial $600 million guidance. No explicit forward EPS or combined-ratio guidance was raised; management flagged a more competitive specialty market and reiterated a low-90s normalized specialty combined ratio.

AVITA Medical reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $26.1 million, up 53% year-over-year and 20% sequentially, led by U.S. RECELL revenue of $22.4 million (up ~20% QoQ) on 3,196 units. Gross margin expanded 270 bps to 84%, operating expenses held flat at $24.6 million, net loss narrowed to $6.2 million ($0.20/share), and net cash use fell to ~$600,000 from $3.2 million in Q2. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance for the second consecutive quarter to $92-$94 million from $86-$89 million and reaffirmed Q4 cash flow breakeven, while noting Q3 likely benefited by roughly $1 million from summer burn seasonality. The going concern doubt was alleviated and the remaining $10 million Perceptive tranche was drawn.

Q3 FY2026 revenue fell to $212,000 from $552,000 a year ago, with nine-month revenue of $814,000 versus $2 million; gross margin was 35% for the quarter and 39% year-to-date. Full-year revenue guidance was reiterated at approximately $1 million, while adjusted OpEx guidance was lowered to $87 million or less from $98 million and total cash usage to $87 million or less from $93 million. Adjusted operating expenses were $18.2 million versus $21.4 million a year ago and declined sequentially, with roughly $12 million in annualized savings from the August restructuring; net loss narrowed to $22.3 million from $35.7 million. Proteus remains on track for a Q2 2027 launch, but AI-driven demand is lengthening lead times on certain components, prompting earlier orders and incremental working capital, with cash of $149.4 million funding operations into Q4 2028.

Q3 revenue was $9.1 million, up 233% year over year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 74.6%. Bookings were $98 million in the quarter and roughly $104 million year to date, with full-year bookings expected above $120 million. Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $31-$34 million from $28-$32 million and reiterated greater than 100% revenue growth for 2027 off the higher base. Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $80.5 million from $45.3 million as R&D rose to $97.5 million, and the company ended with over $1.9 billion in cash and no debt.

Q3 global system-wide sales fell 5.6% in constant currency to $1.15 billion, revenue dropped 10.5% to $455 million, and adjusted EBITDA fell $10 million to $38 million. North America comps and international comps (down 1.8%) both declined, with management citing an intensely promotional environment and soft new-customer acquisition; full-year guidance was cut to roughly -5% system sales, ~-8% North America comps, and approximately $175 million adjusted EBITDA, and Q4 is implied similar to Q3. CEO Penegor conceded top line came in below expectations and introduced the 'Unbox Better' strategy alongside a franchisee marketing framework approved by 98% of votes, a supply-chain margin reduction to 4%, and a tech-fee cut to 1.5%. Free cash flow was $19 million YTD versus $59 million last year; guidance assumes no improvement in the consumer environment and no benefit from Unbox Better.

Palvella reported no product revenue for Q3 FY2026, with R&D rising to $10.8 million from $6.5 million and G&A to $11.9 million from $3.6 million year over year, producing a net loss of $24.6 million, or $1.70 per share. Cash and equivalents/short-term investments were $236.7 million at quarter end, down from roughly $250 million at Q2, and full-year 2026 cash expenses are expected below prior guidance with Q4 as the largest investment period. The key event was FDA acceptance of the QTORIN rapamycin NDA in microcystic lymphatic malformations with Priority Review and a PDUFA date of February 28, 2027, alongside plans to initiate Phase III studies in cutaneous venous malformations and Phase III in DSAP this quarter. Management declined to provide 2027 revenue guidance, pointing to a launch phase in which revenue and demand are expected to be decoupled during payer and access ramp.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 7% to $194.1 million with same-restaurant sales up 1.4% (2.1% check, -0.7% transactions) and Adjusted EBITDA up 23.7% to $26.5 million, 13.6% margin. Restaurant-level Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps to 20.7%, with labor 60 bps favorable. Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $98-$101 million, but the company will close a mid to high single-digit number of underperforming non-Chicago restaurants, mostly in Q4, with material charges. 2027 plan includes 4-6 openings and 2%-3% annual same-restaurant sales.

Privia raised its 2026 outlook above the high end of initial guidance across all key financial metrics: implemented providers ~6,000 (11.5% growth), practice collections +13.1% at the midpoint, care margin +16.3%, and adjusted EBITDA +23.9% to a midpoint above the prior high end. Year-to-date practice collections rose 12% to $2.91 billion and adjusted EBITDA grew 21.9% to $114.7 million, or 28.8% of care margin, with $446.3 million of cash and no debt. Management is exiting the Montana Surgery Partners partnership (~$23 million annual practice collections, 69 providers) effective January 2027 with no material EBITDA impact, and announced the ~$36 million cash acquisition of Cano Health's American Choice MSSP ACO (~36,000 attributed lives). Cash flow conversion guidance was trimmed to ~70% of EBITDA from the prior 70%-80%, citing MSSP payment timing and full cash taxpaying status.

PRA Group reported Q3 2026 revenues of $286 million, portfolio income up 5% to $271 million, net income of $15 million, and cash collections of $536 million, 1% above internal expectations. TTM adjusted EBITDA grew 9% to $1.4 billion, adjusted operating expenses fell 6%, and net leverage declined to 2.6x for an eighth straight quarter of deleveraging. Guidance was largely unchanged: portfolio purchases remain on track for $1 billion-$1.3 billion, 2026 cash growth is expected to moderate versus 2025, and legal collection costs are expected to peak and decline in 2027. The main change versus the prior period was a sharp moderation in curve-adjustment revenue to $14 million after Q2's $349 million European write-up, shifting more revenue toward recurring portfolio income.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $9.8 million, up 86% YoY, split $5.7 million capital and $4.1 million recurring (disposables/service); gross margin rose to 78% from 74% on favorable mix and price discipline. Net loss improved 3% to $7.7 million ($0.21/share vs $0.26), and operating cash use fell to $5 million from $11.3 million sequentially and $9.6 million a year ago. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance improved to at least $25 million (from approximately $25 million) with gross margin of 70% or higher. Installed base reached 98 systems globally (~70/30 US/international), qualified pipeline was $79.2 million, and management disclosed new Cook Medical distribution and Telix education agreements plus a CEO transition effective January 14, 2027.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 1.9% to $215.9 million with net income of $44.4 million ($0.70 diluted) versus $39.9 million ($0.60), and adjusted operating income grew 8.4% to $66.1 million with adjusted EPS of $0.77, up 18.5%. Total enrollments increased 1.6%, with AIU System up 7.5% to 10,830 and St. Augustine revenue up 9.8% to $41.7 million, while CTU enrollments were roughly flat at 31,870. Full-year 2026 adjusted operating income guidance was set at $260-263 million versus $237.9 million in 2025, with Q4 adjusted EPS guided to $0.68-0.72 versus $0.59. The company declared a $0.17 quarterly dividend and repurchased 610,000 shares for $19.9 million, and announced a definitive agreement to acquire South University (~10,500 students) expected to close as early as April 2027.

Total revenue was $32.9 million, up 1% YoY and in the top half of guidance, while non-GAAP operating income of $4.9 million beat the high end of the range. However, management lowered Q4 revenue guidance to a decline of 8%-15% YoY due to a significantly deteriorating macro environment with refinance volume down roughly 60%. The company highlighted strong Autopilot adoption and new deals but warned that 2027 growth will rely on converting this pipeline rather than market volume.

Permian Resources reported Q3 FY2026 oil production of 208,000 bbl/d (up ~10,000 bbl/d QoQ, ~8,000 organic) and total production of 458,000 BOE/d, with record free cash flow of $0.98 per share. Controllable cash costs fell 6% QoQ to a company-low $7.05/BOE (LOE $5.11/BOE, cash G&A $0.73/BOE), and gas revenue swung from -$90 million in Q2 to over +$50 million. The company raised full-year oil guidance to a 202,000 bbl/d midpoint (7% above February guidance) and now expects ~$300 million (~$0.35/share) more free cash flow than its original plan, while announcing $1.15 billion of acquisitions including Ridge Runner. Q4 oil is guided to more than 210,000 bbl/d, and cash CapEx was updated to a $2.025 billion midpoint.

Puma reported Q3 FY2026 net product revenue of $54.1 million, a sequential increase driven by inventory drawdowns and higher supply revenue to international partners, though underlying U.S. net sales declined quarter-over-quarter. Management lowered full-year 2026 guidance for both net NERLYNX product revenue ($205M-$208M vs prior $205M-$209M) and royalties ($18M-$19M vs prior $20M-$23M) due to generic competition in China and higher Medicaid gross-to-net adjustments. The company remains debt-free with positive net income guidance for the full year.

Onity Group reported Q3 FY2026 results with improved financial performance driven by rising interest rates boosting servicing income, which offset declining origination income. Adjusted pre-tax income more than doubled to $30 million and adjusted ROE reached 19%, while net income available to common stockholders improved to $3.5 million. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged from the prior quarter, citing a balanced business model that navigates market volatility effectively.

Third quarter revenue was $203 million, a decrease of $22 million year-over-year primarily due to the normalization of recovery services following a significant environmental event in 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $36 million with a record margin of 17.7%, and full-year 2026 guidance remains unchanged at the midpoint implying approximately 150 basis points of margin expansion compared to 2025.

Third quarter revenue was $1 billion, up 12% year-over-year, while Contribution Profit rose 70% to $34 million despite a weaker housing market. Contribution Margin declined sequentially to 3.3% from Q2's 5.8% due to watching spring acquisitions into a difficult market and deeper price cuts for clearance. Management expects margins to decline again in Q4 as the company continues clearing inventory and increases marketing spend.

rows.gics_industry: Independent Power and Renewable Electricity Producers
rows.key_quote: Ormat reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $275 million (up 10.2% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $153.8 million (up 11.1%), driven by a 145% surge in energy storage revenue to $49.9 million. Management raised the full-year revenue guidance midpoint to $1.17-$1.20 billion and Adjusted EBITDA to $640-$650 million, citing strong momentum in storage and electricity segments despite a temporary Puna outage impact.

Net product revenue declined 70% year-over-year to $45.5 million in Q3 FY2026, driven by a contraction in the skin substitute market following CMS policy changes and discarded product comments. Operating loss widened to $29.5 million compared to income last year due to lower revenue and reduced gross margins (52% vs 76%), though operating expenses decreased significantly by $55.2 million year-over-year. Management updated full-year 2026 guidance to a net revenue range of $179-$200 million, representing a decline of 65%-68%, which is slightly wider than the prior guidance of 62%-68%.

Oscar Health reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5.1 billion (up ~70% YoY) and earnings from operations of $178 million, driven by a 24% larger member footprint and favorable risk adjustment. Management raised full-year 2026 earnings from operations guidance to $850-$950 million, citing disciplined execution and AI-driven efficiencies that pushed the SG&A expense ratio down to a record low of 14%. The company expects stable membership in 2027 despite CMS integrity reviews, with pricing increases of ~14% reflecting medical cost trends and market morbidity.

OTF reported Q3 FY2026 net investment income of $0.29 per share, a modest decline from the prior quarter's $0.30 due to lighter deployments and a new non-accrual, while NAV increased to $16.62 driven by portfolio valuation recovery and $55 million in share repurchases. Management maintained its guidance to cover the dividend by mid-next year via approximately $1.2 billion of net deployment and leverage increasing toward 1.15x, citing improved market sentiment and wider spreads as tailwinds.
