The company raised $900 million in debt financing during the quarter, ending with significant liquidity and a conservative portfolio structure.

Consolidated revenues grew 9% YoY to $145M OIBDA (up 6%) and $103M AFFO (up 5%), driven by strong 20% growth in transit and mid-single-digit growth in billboard. Management raised full-year AFFO guidance to approximately 25% growth compared to the prior year, citing robust Q4 bookings and continued investment in AI-enabled sales tools. The quarter included roughly $50M of incremental FIFA World Cup revenue, with management expressing high confidence in sustaining momentum into 2027.

Pan American Silver reported Q3 FY2026 attributable free cash flow of $377 million and net earnings of $357 million ($0.86/share), though silver production of 6.1M ounces missed the quarterly outlook range due to sequencing at Juanicipio and Cerro Moro, and gold production was impacted by delays at Timmins and Shahuindo. Management revised full-year gold production guidance downward to 660k-680k ounces and raised full-year gold all-in sustaining cost guidance to $2,000-$2,150/oz due to lower production, increased development costs, and El Niño weather impacts. While silver segment costs came in below expectations at $11.21/oz, the company faces operational headwinds including a 40-day downtime at Huaron for mill repairs and ongoing remediation work at Jacobina affecting 2027 production.

PAR reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $137.1 million (up 15% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $17.1 million, exceeding the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $532.5-$536.5 million from the prior $516-$523 million range, citing strong ARR growth and multi-product adoption. The company delivered record free cash flow of $17.7 million and improved non-GAAP subscription margins sequentially.

PDF Solutions reported record Q3 revenue of $68.3 million, representing a 20% year-over-year increase and an 11% quarter-over-quarter rise. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance for 20% annual revenue growth and maintained its long-term target gross margin model of 77%. Gross margins expanded to 77% from 73% in the prior quarter, driven by reduced eProbe costs and controlled personnel spending.

Pennant reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $302.3M, up 32% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $24.7M (+42.4%), adjusted EBITDA prior to NCI of $26.1M (+44%), and adjusted EPS of $0.35 (+16.7%). Home Health and Hospice segment revenue rose 38.2% to $239.8M with adjusted EBITDA of $38.1M (+42%), while Senior Living revenue grew 12.6% to $62.4M but segment adjusted EBITDA was roughly flat YoY due to integration challenges and elevated benefits costs. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance but called out higher-than-anticipated employee benefits costs (about 50 bps of revenue in Q3 and expected similar in Q4) and softness in two senior living markets; the home health final rule provided a 2.1% net increase (1.5% on Pennant claims).

PENN reported record Q3 FY2026 retail revenue of $1.5 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $502 million, representing a 5% YoY increase in revenue and 7.7% in Adjusted EBITDA. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for retail revenue to $5.89 billion and Adjusted EBITDA to $1.973 billion, citing strong performance from new development projects like M Resort and Hollywood Columbus. Interactive segment revenue was $348.4 million with a loss of $18.3 million, though margins expanded significantly due to iCasino mix improvements.

Perma-Fix reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $17.9 million and a net loss of $3.5 million, representing a decline in profitability compared to the prior year quarter due to lower gross profit in the treatment segment. Management noted that while backlog grew 25% to $19.6 million and pricing increases began implementation, full operations were delayed until September by customer-directed protocol changes and scheduled maintenance. The company expects revenue recognition from the Hanford DFLAW waste stream to continue ramping up over the next few months.

Park Hotels & Resorts reported Q3 FY2026 results with RevPAR increasing 8.4% year-over-year to $201 and hotel adjusted EBITDA rising 8% to $135 million. Management raised full-year guidance, updating the RevPAR outlook midpoint by 200 basis points to a range of 5.5%-6.0% and increasing adjusted EBITDA guidance by approximately $13 million at the midpoint to $635-$645 million. The quarter was driven by broad-based strength across the portfolio, including record performance at Orlando Bonnet Creek and significant recovery in Hawaii despite weather disruptions.

Park-Ohio reported record Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenues of $459 million, a 15% year-over-year increase and 4% sequential growth, alongside a gross margin expansion of 120 basis points to 9.5%. Management raised full-year sales guidance to $1.75-$1.77 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $3.35-$3.50 per share, citing strong demand in aerospace, defense, semiconductor, and AI data center markets. The company expects Q4 free cash flow to be significant as working capital levels normalize.

Consolidated revenue grew 9% to $31.7 million, driven by Honey Birdette (up 12%) and China licensing (up nearly 40%). Operating income nearly tripled to $4 million as the company achieved its seventh consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA. Management announced an agreement to acquire a Miami Beach property for a private members club, choosing this capital deployment over share repurchases.

Palomar Holdings reported a strong Q3 FY2026 with gross written premium increasing 28% year-over-year to $767 million and adjusted net income growing 47% to $81.3 million. Management raised full-year adjusted net income guidance to $280-$285 million from the prior range of $270-$280 million, citing strong execution and business evolution. The company also initiated a dividend of $0.45 per share and repurchased $8.9 million of stock during the quarter.

Planet Fitness reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $360 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $146.2 million (up 3.9% YoY), driven by a 1.5% system-wide same-club sales growth that beat expectations. Management raised its full-year guidance for same-club sales growth to 1.5%-2% from the prior range of 1%, while also increasing the unit opening outlook to 190-195 clubs following the acquisition of Be-Fit in Portugal. The company executed a $10 Classic Card promo test which provided regional pricing insights but confirmed no nationwide rollback, with Black Card price increases planned for Q2 2027.

Gibraltar reported Q3 FY2026 Residential net sales of $399M (up 73% on OmniMax inclusion, +3.1% organic) with adjusted EBITDA of $84M (up 62.3%) and adjusted EPS of $1.01, which included a $21.5M net interest impact. Each segment came in below management expectations: shingle shipments fell 13% YoY and 22% sequentially, Agtech pushed more than $40M of revenue out of H2 on permit delays, and Infrastructure sales fell 7.8% on fiber seal pilot delays. Full-year 2026 guidance for continuing operations was cut to sales of $1.64-1.66B, adjusted EPS of $2.25-2.40 (from $3.92 in 2025), and free cash flow of roughly 1% of sales, versus prior expectations of residential down ~5% in H2 now assumed down ~15%. OmniMax integration synergies were raised to a $36.5M annualized run rate, and the D.S. Brown/Infrastructure sale ($208M) was signed for expected Q4 close.

Pulse Biosciences reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $395,000 versus $86,000 in the prior year period, with GAAP net loss widening to $23.1 million from $19.4 million and non-GAAP net loss to $17.5 million from $13.5 million. The company completed NANOPULSE-AF pivotal enrollment at 169 evaluable patients (189 total) in under six months, three months ahead of plan, and ended the quarter with $189.2 million in cash and marketable securities after raising $95.8 million through its ATM during the quarter. Management guided future quarterly non-GAAP costs and expenses to rise 15%-25% above the Q2/Q3 average of approximately $20 million, citing persistent AF IDE, additional studies, and manufacturing build-out; no revenue guidance was provided.

Playtika reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $673.8M, down 7.8% sequentially and essentially flat year-over-year, with record adjusted EBITDA of $252.1M (up 15.9% YoY, 37.4% margin) and net income of $40.4M. Guidance was reaffirmed, not raised: full-year revenue of $2.75B-$2.85B and adjusted EBITDA of $750M-$790M, now expected around the midpoint of both ranges versus last quarter's cautious second-half view. The quarter was driven by DTC revenue of $275.1M (40.8% of total, up 31.4% YoY), June's Journey up 12.1% and Slotomania stabilizing, offset by Bingo Blitz down 18.2% and Disney Solitaire down 21.9% sequentially. The board concluded its strategic review, opting to remain independent, with refinancing of upcoming maturities the stated priority.

RenovoRx reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.07 million, up ~17% sequentially and more than fourfold from $266,000 a year ago, with gross margin of 82% (85% excluding zero-margin device conversions) and a net loss of $3.6 million, or $0.08 per share. Active commercial cancer centers rose to 26 from 21 at Q2, leaving a commercial funnel of more than 65 centers against a year-end 2026 target of 36. Management maintained (did not raise) full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $3.75-$4.25 million, and operating loss narrowed to $3.2 million from $3.4 million in the prior quarter. Cash of $10.4 million is expected to fund operations into the second half of 2027, and the phase III TIGeR-PaC trial has completed enrollment with top-line data expected in the second half of 2027.

Runway reported Q3 FY2026 total investment income of $40.6 million (up from $37 million in Q2) but net investment income fell to $15.9 million from $18.2 million, with NII per share of $0.38 including roughly $0.06 of net one-time benefit ($0.08 prepayment fees partly offset by $0.02 debt costs), implying a core run rate near $0.32 versus the $0.33 base dividend. NAV per share was $11.94 versus $11.91, and the portfolio shrank to $1.1 billion from $1.2 billion on $140 million of liquidity events (including the $72.3 million 3PL/Extensiv repayment) against only $8.5 million of deployments. Management guided that Q4 prepayments could match or exceed Q3, that net portfolio growth may take a while, and declined to commit to 2027 dividend coverage beyond stating they expect to cover the base dividend next quarter and full year; the board expanded the buyback to $30 million through September 2027.

Omada Health reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $91 million, a 34% year-over-year increase and its highest quarterly revenue ever, driven by strong enrollments and a mix shift toward higher-value diabetes and hypertension programs. Gross margin expanded significantly to 78% on a non-GAAP basis (up from 68% a year ago) as the company achieved record net income of nearly $7 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $12 million. Management raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $344-$346 million and Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $32-$34 million, citing strong execution and operating leverage.

Total revenue was $21.9M, down 7% YoY but above the high end of guidance and consensus, with AI customer revenue up 7% to $14.4M (66% of total) and AI customer ARR up 11% to $54.5M (74% of SaaS ARR). Non-GAAP EPS of $0.09 and adjusted EBITDA margin of 12% both beat guidance, but GAAP net income fell to $1.6M ($0.06/share) from $2.6M a year ago and operating cash flow dropped to $1.8M from $10.4M on federal payment timing. Full-year guidance was reiterated ($84.5-86M revenue, AI customer revenue up 8-10%) while Q2 guidance implies a GAAP loss of $0.02 to income of $0.01 and adjusted EBITDA margin of 0-2%, as sales and marketing steps up and legacy runoff accelerates. Total SaaS ARR fell 4% to $73.4M, total RPO fell 18% to $71M, and AI-customer net retention held at 104% versus 117% a year ago.

NFG reported Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.22 (GAAP $1.02), flat versus the prior year, capping FY2026 adjusted EPS of $7.55, up 9% YoY; full-year Seneca production of 419.5 Bcf came in just below the low end of the already-revised guidance range. Initial FY2027 guidance is $6.00-$6.40 per share, well below FY2026, driven by a $2.85/MMBtu natural gas price assumption ($0.80 lower NYMEX) and flat production of 400-435 Bcf. Offsets include newly in-service Tioga Pathway and Shippingport Lateral projects (~$30 million incremental annual revenue), the closed Ohio utility acquisition doubling utility rate base, and anticipated operating income doubling in the utility segment. Management flagged 2027 as a transitional year with one-time separation costs and modest dilution from acquisition financing.

Rockwell reported Q4 FY2026 core organic sales growth of 7% (reported +1%), adjusted EPS of $3.88 up 16%, and enterprise operating margin of 24.5% up 320 bps, though the margin included 130 bps of tariff-refund benefit and reported sales were cut ~$85 million by customer refunds. Intelligent Devices organic sales rose 5%, Software & Control +15% with Logix up 25%, and Lifecycle Services +2%; full-year core sales grew 9%, adjusted EPS $13.42 up 27%, and free cash flow conversion was 113%. FY2027 guidance calls for 6%-9% organic growth (7.5% midpoint), ~23% enterprise margin (up ~100 bps), and adjusted EPS of $14.50-$15.50 ($15.00 midpoint), with ARR growth expected to improve to 7% from 5%. Key soft spot was ARR, which management acknowledged 'did not meet our expectations' primarily due to project delays and scaled-back rollout scopes in Lifecycle Services.

Q1 FY2027 GMV grew 34% and the RLTC take rate came in at 4.3%, with funding costs at 6% of on-balance-sheet loans. Management set a full-year FY2027 growth floor of at least 30% (a 'three handle'), noting Q2's first month is growing at a high-30s rate, and flagged a new transformer-based underwriting model that improved approval separation roughly twofold. Provision expense rose on September-dated approval experiments kept on balance sheet and GAAP operating margin guidance landed below Street on heavier warrant expense tied to new-user growth in the U.K. launch; DTC and wallets drove about half of volume.

Revenue came in at $177.8 million, up 4.3% sequentially but down 2.6% year-over-year, slightly above the midpoint of guidance, with non-GAAP gross margin up 150 bps to 25.2% and a non-GAAP loss of $0.07 per share versus $0.13 loss last quarter. Advanced Computing grew over 50% sequentially and 80% year-over-year to nearly 23% of revenue, while traditional PC revenue fell roughly 30% sequentially and consumer was down 22.9% sequentially. December guidance is approximately $180 million plus or minus $10 million with non-GAAP gross margin of 25.7% plus or minus 1%, implying slight sequential and roughly 10% year-over-year growth despite continued PC weakness. Management flagged elevated memory costs and component shortages as a persistent headwind and said it does not expect a near-term PC recovery.

Q1 FY2027 core revenue was $316.4M, up 14% YoY, with a non-GAAP operating margin of 39% (up 900 bps sequentially) and non-GAAP net income of $119.1M, up 70% YoY. Management called the quarter a beat, with TPV exceeding expectations by ~250 bps, AP/AR take rate of 16.2 bps, core ARPU up 4.1% YoY, and GAAP net income of $60M. FY2027 guidance reiterates core revenue of $1.28B-$1.31B (11%-14% growth) and ~33% non-GAAP operating margin, while GAAP profit guidance was raised to more than $180M and non-GAAP EPS guidance implies ~47% YoY growth. Management flagged Q2 as a growth trough (core revenue growth of 10%-13%) tied to a tough prior-year compare and continued restructuring adjustments, with improvement expected in the back half.

Cardinal Health reported Q1 FY2027 revenue up 5% to $67.5 billion, gross profit up 12% to $2.6 billion, and operating income up 17% to $1 billion, with diluted EPS up 28% to $3.26. Management raised FY2027 EPS guidance to $12.80-$13.00 from $12.40-$12.60, lifted pharma segment profit growth guidance to 10%-12% from 8%-11%, and raised the 'other' segment revenue and profit outlook. Offsets include GMPD segment profit trending toward the low end of its $200-$220 million range on high petroleum costs, and a 400 bp revenue headwind from IRA WAC reductions. The largest positive change was the CVS Health contract renewal through June 2032, complemented by renewals covering nearly two-thirds of enterprise revenue over the last 12 months.

Organic net sales rose 0.6% excluding EABL (1.4% including), with volume -0.1% and price/mix +0.7%; reported net sales were up 1.2% to $4.9 billion. North America organic sales fell 3.6% (U.S. -3.7%) on weakness in Don Julio, Casamigos and Crown Royal, partly offset by Johnnie Walker and double-digit Guinness and Smirnoff Ice. Asia-Pac grew 4.1%, LAC 4.8%, India 3.4% and EMEA 2.4%. FY2027 guidance was reiterated unchanged: broadly flat organic net sales, low-to-mid-single-digit organic operating profit growth, and free cash flow of around $2 billion.

Q1 FY2027 consolidated revenue fell 11.1% to $171.4 million from $192.7 million on a continuing-operations basis, with E-Commerce down 12.3%, wholesale and other down 10.7%, and BloomNet down 3.6%; a Hebron, Ohio fire cost roughly 1% of revenue. Gross margin contracted 120 bps to 34.1% on lower volume, fuel surcharges, and promotional testing, and Adjusted EBITDA loss was essentially flat year-over-year at $31.9 million versus $31.7 million. Net Order Demand on primary websites improved to an 8% decline from 12.6% a year ago, while other websites fell 36%; management issued FY2027 guidance of revenue down 2%-5% and Adjusted EBITDA of $10-15 million, reflecting the completed PersonalizationMall and Things Remembered divestitures. The two-site sale closed at roughly $45 million, with $22 million applied to the term loan lowering it to $111.3 million, and a Jacksonville facility sale for about $10 million is pending.

MACOM reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $424.8 million, up 62.7% year-over-year and 24.1% sequentially, with adjusted EPS of $2.09 versus $1.40 in Q3 and adjusted operating margin of 38.2%. Data center revenue reached a record $188.1 million (up ~37% sequentially), I&D $164.6 million (+23%) and telecom $72.1 million (+1%); Q4 book-to-bill was 1.4:1 and the company ended the year with record backlog on a full-year book-to-bill of 1.5:1. Q1 FY2027 guidance is $450-460 million in revenue, 62-63% adjusted gross margin and $2.21-2.29 adjusted EPS, with data center expected up ~15% sequentially and telecom flat to slightly down. Management said data center growth should exceed FY2026's 74% (base case ~80%) and I&D growth could top 30%, and flagged operating margin above 40% during FY2027.

IBEX reported record Q1 FY2027 results with revenue of $175.2 million (up 16% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $25.2 million (up 29% YoY). Management raised full-year guidance for revenue to $720M-$735M and adjusted EBITDA to $96M-$99M, citing strong momentum from new logos and the Sierra partnership. The company maintained a robust outlook with double-digit organic growth expected to continue.

AI Cloud revenue nearly tripled to $200 million in Q1 FY2027, while total revenue reached $228 million and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 29%. Management noted a delay in the Horizon 1 delivery to Microsoft, pushing the target from December to January or potentially February due to customer-requested design changes and supplier timing. Despite this specific delay, management expressed strong confidence in demand, citing new contracts with leading frontier AI labs and investment-grade counterparties.

IRSA reported a net loss of ARS 6.3 billion for Q1 FY2027, driven by fair value adjustments on investment properties due to inflation outpacing currency devaluation in Argentina. Despite the headline loss, rental EBITDA increased 20% in dollar terms and reached a record $205 million over the last 12 months. Management raised the dividend yield to 11% (ARS 211 billion) and guided CapEx for the full year at approximately $150 million.

Net sales reached $391 million, representing a 7% year-over-year increase and a 5% sequential rise, driven by organic growth in medical (14% YoY) and automotive segments. Management reiterated full-year fiscal 2027 guidance with sales expected at the high end of the range ($1.535 billion-$1.560 billion), citing strength in medical and Helvoet integration progress. Gross margin remained flat at 7.9% as higher material costs offset favorable mix, while adjusted operating income was $17 million.

BrasilAgro reported Q1 FY2027 net income of BRL 81 million and Adjusted EBITDA of BRL 95 million, driven by a BRL 50 million gain from farm sales and BRL 37 million in financial effects from soy price rallies. Management highlighted that operational results fell short of the BRL 150 million target due to lower corn sales volume compared to the prior year and tight sugarcane margins caused by low ATR prices. The company reduced its net debt/EBITDA ratio to 1.05x following the farm sale but noted that high interest rates are currently hindering further expansion or purchases.

Lesaka reported Q1 FY2027 net revenue of ZAR 1.58 billion (up 8% YoY) and adjusted EPS of ZAR 0.72, beating the top of guidance while meeting all three measures. Group Adjusted EBITDA was ZAR 220 million at the midpoint of guidance, though down 17% YoY due to exceptional items in merchant and higher group costs. Management reiterated full-year guidance for net revenue (ZAR 7-7.7 billion) and adjusted EPS (ZAR 7.50-8.50), noting that Bank Zero completion is expected by end of January 2027.

LSI reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $226 million, a 44% year-over-year increase driven by the Royston acquisition and strong C-store/grocery verticals, while lighting sales declined 6%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 41% to $22.2 million with improved margins across all brands, supported by cost synergies and pricing discipline. Management noted continued softness in QSR and lighting markets due to customer budget delays but highlighted a new 3,000-store QSR award and positive momentum from the NACS trade show.

Q4 net sales fell 1.1% to $376.5 million (Water Flow -3.0%, Water Management +1.4%), adjusted EPS was flat at $0.38, and adjusted EBITDA rose 4.0% to $95.5 million with margin up 130 bps to 25.4%. Full-year net sales grew 3.2% to ~$1.5 billion, adjusted EBITDA rose 14.1% to a record $372.2 million (25.2% margin, +240 bps), and adjusted EPS rose ~20% to $1.57 with $207.3 million of free cash flow. FY2027 guidance is net sales of $1.44-$1.47 billion (flat to +2.5% ex-metering) and adjusted EBITDA of $378-$388 million, a ~26.3% margin at the midpoint, down from $372.2 million on an absolute basis only slightly higher and reflecting the metering exit. The company also announced the transition of its metering business to ZENNER USA, with ~$40 million of metering sales at a negative EBITDA margin, ~$26 million of one-time FY2027 expenses, and a 100-140 bps annualized margin benefit. Additionally, the board authorized a $300 million buyback increase and a 14.3% dividend raise to $0.08 per quarter.

Kura Sushi reported Q4 FY2026 total sales of $88.9 million versus $79.4 million a year ago, but comparable sales fell 5.7% on an 11.5% traffic decline, partially offset by 5.8% price/mix. The quarter swung to a net loss of $0.3 million (-$0.02 per share) from net income of $2.3 million ($0.18), with adjusted net income of $0.9 million ($0.08) versus $2.5 million ($0.20), and restaurant-level operating margin contracted to 19.1% from 19.8%. FY2027 guidance calls for total sales of $376-381 million, 17 new units, G&A of ~11.5% of sales, and restaurant-level margin of ~19%, with management guiding to flat-to-slightly-positive comps at the high end and negative comps at the low end. Management also said it will take no pricing to offset the 3.5% that rolled off in November, and Q1 comps to date are -3.1%.

Revenue increased 4% to $219.4 million and gross margins expanded 150 bps to 8.2%, driven by improved execution and overhead absorption. The company reported its third consecutive quarter of profitability with positive EPS of $0.22, while liquidity remains strong at $222 million. Management noted that award activity will pick up in the second half of the fiscal year, though current awards primarily solidify revenue for fiscal 2028.

Xeris reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $107.2 million, up 44% year-over-year and 16% sequentially, with net product revenue of $106.3 million (+43%). Recorlev drove the quarter at $71.5 million (+93% YoY, +26% QoQ), Gvoke fell to $21.7 million from $25.2 million on a $4 million one-time Medicaid gross-to-net adjustment despite 5% Rx growth, and KEVEYIS contributed $13 million (+9%). Adjusted EBITDA rose 77% to $30.8 million and GAAP net income was $11.3 million versus $0.6 million; full-year revenue guidance was raised to $395-$405 million (~37% growth) and the 2030 outlook lifted to over $1 billion from $750 million. R&D growth guidance was trimmed to ~$15 million from ~$25 million while SG&A growth was raised to ~$60 million from ~$50 million.

Q3 FY2026 total revenue was $263M, up 17% YoY and $1M above the high end of guidance, with subscription revenue also up 17% to $246M. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 18.3%, 85 bps above the high end of guidance and up 560 bps YoY, while non-GAAP EPS of $0.72 (up from $0.46) reflects a newly applied 22% non-GAAP tax rate. Full-year revenue guidance of $1.041-1.044B and ~19% subscription growth remain essentially intact, with the non-GAAP operating margin outlook raised 25 bps at the midpoint to 18.2%-18.3%; management flagged that FX and sustainability tailwinds have subsided, contributing to a Q4 revenue guide that does not fully pass through the Q3 beat. CRPO grew 17% YoY (18% in constant currency), and the >$300K contract cohort grew 31%.

Willdan reported Q3 FY2026 contract revenue of $215 million (+18% YoY) and net revenue of $112 million (+18%), with organic net revenue growth of 12% and 17% growth in the energy segment. Adjusted EBITDA rose 22% to $28.3 million, a 25.2% net revenue margin up 80 bps, while Adjusted EPS was essentially flat at $1.20 versus $1.21 on a higher tax rate and stock comp. Management raised FY2026 targets to net revenue of $435-445 million, Adjusted EBITDA of $109-111 million, and Adjusted EPS of $5.15-5.25, and introduced preliminary 2027 targets of $1 billion contract revenue, over $500 million net revenue, and more than $140 million EBITDA. The $120 million Mantis Innovation acquisition closed October 30, adding roughly $75 million in net revenue for 2026.

Q3 revenue was $244.7M, up 10.4% and within guidance, with retail +12.4% and e-commerce +4.8%; adjusted gross margin 54.6% (+40 bps) and adjusted EBITDA $28.6M at 11.7% of revenue (+10 bps). Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $966-976M (11%-12% growth) and now includes up to 1 point of Intelligent Eyewear contribution, with adjusted EBITDA of $117-119M; Q4 revenue guided to $243-253M (15%-20% growth) on a much larger marketing and launch spend. Active customers grew only 3% and management flagged softer September trends, weak category units, and pressure on cash-pay consumers, offset by eye exams +30%, insurance +22%, and the Nov 12 Intelligent Eyewear pre-order launch. Guidance was nudged with a new product contribution rather than raised on the core business.

Total revenue of $601 million rose 6% YoY and beat the $585 million outlook; adjusted EBITDA of $234 million topped the $232 million guide at a 38.8% margin, and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.29 versus $0.25 prior year. FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $2.34 billion and net CAPEX to $400 million, but adjusted EBITDA guidance was held at $920 million as higher Q4 activations, transfers and D&I mix dilute flow-through. Modular units on rent inflected up 1.2% YoY, the first growth in five years, and the modular order book is up over 20% YoY, supporting initial 2027 views of low single-digit organic revenue and mid-single-digit organic EBITDA growth.

Watts reported Q3 sales of $728 million, up 19% reported and 12% organic, with adjusted operating margin expanding 240 bps to 20.9% and adjusted EPS of $3.40, up 36% YoY. The company raised full-year organic sales growth guidance to 11%-12% (two points at the midpoint) and lifted adjusted EBITDA and operating margin outlook by 25 bps at the midpoint, while Q4 revenue guidance of 11%-14% reported with organic 9%-12% was below the Q3 organic rate. Growth was led by data centers, notably in APMEA (+30% organic) and Americas (+12% organic), offsetting continued weakness in residential and non-institutional new construction.

Q3 FY2026 revenue fell 11% YoY to $152.9 million as behavioral subscription revenue dropped 22% to $113.9 million, partly offset by clinical revenue up 48% to $38 million (about 25% of total). Adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to $51.7 million at a 33.8% margin (vs 24.9%), net income was $15.1 million, and operating cash flow was $32.3 million. Total subscribers were about 2.3 million, with behavioral down 26% YoY to 2.1 million while Core+ grew to 546,000 (16% YoY growth, fourth straight sequential gain) and clinical fell sequentially to 174,000 from 197,000. Full-year guidance was narrowed: revenue $625-630 million (from $620-635 million) and adjusted EBITDA $110-115 million (from $105-115 million), with adjusted gross margin now about 74% versus prior expectation of above 72%.

Wynn reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted property EBITDA of $158.8 million in Las Vegas (27.6% margin) on $575.2 million of revenue, $50.1 million in Boston (25.8% margin) on $194.7 million, and $255.3 million in Macau (27.8% margin) on $919.2 million. Las Vegas results absorbed just under $24 million of unfavorable hold plus a soft summer market, partially offset by 3% RevPAR and ADR growth and retail lease revenue up 8%; Macau VIP hold added just under $12.3 million. October trends were strong across Vegas (drop, ADR, RevPAR and retail tenant sales all up), while Macau volumes declined into month-end after a Golden Week in line with last year. Capital return continued with $58.1 million of buybacks, a $0.25/share dividend, and a $150 million Macau interim dividend (up from $125 million), and the Al Marjan Island budget and timeline (Sept 2027) were unchanged.

Xponential reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $62.3 million, down 21% from $78.8 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $24.3 million, down 27% or $9.2 million year-over-year. Same-store sales fell 7.5% overall and 5.6% at Club Pilates, while North America systemwide sales of $424 million declined 2%. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $250-260 million and systemwide sales of $1.70-1.75 billion were unchanged, but adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered to $91-94 million and net new studio openings cut to 124-130. Management cited a softer Q4 consumer backdrop, a tighter real estate environment, and continued merchandise logistics disruption, while announcing a new CFO and reiterating an ongoing strategic alternatives review.

BD reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $5.3 billion, up 5.6% FX-neutral (high single digits ex-Alaris prior-year comparison), with adjusted EPS of $4.15, up 27.3%. Adjusted gross margin was 56.8% (up 180 bps) and adjusted operating margin 28.6% (up 280 bps), while full-year adjusted EPS of $12.70 grew 6.7% on 3.9% revenue growth to $19.5 billion. FY2027 guidance calls for low single-digit revenue growth (including an ~200 bps Alaris capital comparison headwind, roughly mid-single digit ex-Alaris), flat adjusted operating margins, and adjusted EPS of $13.10-$13.30, with Q1 EPS of $2.32-$2.37 at the low end due to Alaris and an APM system cutover. Full-year free cash flow rose 42% to $2.9 billion, conversion improved to 74%, and BD announced its 55th consecutive dividend increase.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $836 million, down 7.6% as reported and 7% in constant currency, with adjusted EPS of $0.29, down $0.13 year-over-year; adjusted EBITDA margin fell 110 bps. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was cut to $1.20-$1.30 from $1.40-$1.50 (excluding a $0.17 one-time tariff refund gain), and net sales guidance narrowed to approximately $3.5 billion from $3.5-$3.6 billion. Roughly three-fourths of the EPS reduction was attributed to EMEA underperformance and the Middle East conflict, with tax rate and strategic investments the balance. Gross margin nominally rose 190 bps, but included a $39 million pre-tax accounting-estimate benefit that management said reflects a multi-year period and is not expected to recur; excluding Byte, ~$10 million dealer inventory reductions and discrete items, revenue declined 3.8% in constant currency.

Q3 FY2026 Nareit FFO was $0.50/unit and Core FFO $0.75/unit, with outpatient medical same-store cash NOI up 1.6% YoY, described as consistent with expectations set at the start of the year. Cash G&A of $5.3M included $1.2M of severance/transition costs, leverage stood at 41% and net debt to adjusted EBITDAre at 7.1x. No formal guidance was updated; management declined to give timing or valuation on the legacy outpatient medical disposition but said pricing has eroded 25-50 bps on the backup in Treasuries. Seniors housing lease-ups are early — The Riviera at 25.6% average occupancy and The Pinnacle (closed in October) at 31% — with targeted yield-on-cost above 7% in 2028/2029.

Yelp reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue down 1% YoY to $371 million, $1 million above the high end of its outlook, with adjusted EBITDA down 6% to $92 million (25% margin) and net income down 12% to $35 million ($0.63 diluted). Advertising weakened further: services ad revenue fell 2% to $238 million and RR&O ad revenue fell 13% to $99 million, with ad clicks down 8%, partially offset by other revenue up 82% to a record $34 million. Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $347-$352 million implies continued pressure, and the full-year revenue range was updated to $1.455-$1.46 billion while adjusted EBITDA was narrowed to the high end at $320-$325 million. Management said it does not expect the local advertising market to turn anytime soon and disclosed it paused buybacks to pay down its revolver, with repurchases expected to resume in 2027.

Total revenue was $108.2 million in Q3 2026, with net product revenue up 2% sequentially as the China commercial business stabilized; the text gives no YoY growth figure and no EPS. Management reiterated that China remains profitable and expects a return to year-over-year product revenue growth only in 2027, with R&D and SG&A roughly flat versus the prior year. The cash position was $659.7 million at September 30, 2026, plus about $250 million raised in October equity at no discount. Forward narrative centered on zoci (81.8% confirmed ORR in first-line SCLC, 6-month PFS 81.9%, grade 3+ zoci-related AEs 9.1%) and a potential U.S. BLA in 2027 with launch as early as 2028.

Zoetis reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.4 billion, down 1% on both reported and organic operational bases, with a 1% price decline and flat volume, adjusted EPS up 1% to $1.75 on a lower share count, and adjusted net income down 7% organically. Companion animal fell 5% to $1.6 billion, led by a 16% drop in key dermatology to $396 million (US down 13%), with US segment revenue down 6% to $1.2 billion while international grew 4% to $1.1 billion. Livestock rose 7% to $797 million and diagnostics rose 13% to $122 million. Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $9.22-9.32 billion (organic decline of 2% to 1%), while adjusted net income was raised to $2.6-2.64 billion and adjusted EPS to $6.25-6.35; for 2027 management said it will not assume macro improvement or easing competition and expects limited launch contribution.

Air Products reported FY2026 adjusted EPS of $13.45, up 12%, on 8% sales growth, with operating margin up 70 bps to 24.4% and ROC up 100 bps to 11.9%; Q4 EPS rose 6%. FY2027 EPS guidance of $14.15-$14.50 implies 5-8% growth, including a ~2% non-operating headwind from higher interest expense and a 19% tax rate, flat equity affiliate income, and no buybacks assumed. The industrial gas backlog rose to $3.3 billion from ~$3 billion, with over $2 billion in electronics project wins in the last 12 months, while FY2027 CapEx is targeted at $3-3.5 billion and management expects positive net cash flow. Full-year results came in above original FY2026 guidance, but the FY2027 EPS growth guide decelerates versus the 12% delivered in FY2026.

Atmos reported fiscal 2026 diluted EPS of $8.49, marking the 24th consecutive year of EPS growth, with FY2026 results including $175 million of pre-tax Rule 7.7102 deferrals (up $149 million year-over-year). Capital spending rose 17% to $4.2 billion, rate base grew 15% to roughly $25 billion, and O&M was flat at $875 million. FY2027 EPS guidance was initiated at $9.05-$9.25 with 6%-8% annual growth off the midpoint through FY2031 ($12.35-$12.55), and the board raised the indicated FY2027 dividend 9% to $4.36. Management noted APT through-system spreads returned to historical norms in Q4 and are assumed to stay there in FY2027.

Net sales increased 29.9% to $252.9 million driven by Saxdor and Cobalt growth, though this modestly missed the guided range due to a softer ski/wake category. Adjusted EBITDA rose 21.7% to $14.3 million at the low end of guidance, while legacy adjusted EBITDA declined as Malibu volumes fell. Management provided updated guidance for the transition period (July-Dec) with net sales expected between $489M-$501M and adjusted EBITDA between $27.3M-$29.3M.

OpenText reported Q1 FY2027 total revenue of $1.237B, within the expected outlook range, with Core revenue of $864M up 2.4% year over year (2.7% constant currency) and Core Cloud revenue of $339M up 11.2% (11.7% cc). Adjusted EBITDA margin was 35.8%, down 50 bps year over year but above the 32%-33% outlook range, and non-GAAP diluted EPS was $1.05, flat year over year. Q2 revenue guidance is $1.26B-$1.29B with adjusted EBITDA margin of 33%-34%, and full-year FY2027 outlook ranges were maintained on all metrics, with growth investments weighted to the second half. The quarter was in line with the company's own outlook, with Content Cloud growing 20.7% while ITOM and cyber declined double digits and $116M of products were reclassified from Core to non-Core.

Rayonier reported Q3 GAAP EPS of $0.41 on net income of $123 million, including $91 million of income from the ~36,000-acre Washington disposition; excluding that and $7 million of merger costs, EPS was $0.13 and adjusted EBITDA was $145 million, up sharply YoY on PotlatchDeltic contributions. Southern Timber adjusted EBITDA rose 23% to $52 million on 56% higher harvest volumes with delivered sawlog prices down 5% and pulpwood down 15% YoY (both up low-single digits sequentially), while Northwest Timber EBITDA jumped to $32 million from $6 million on doubled volumes and 29% higher sawlog prices. Wood Products EBITDA of $27 million was the best since Q3 2022 at $528/MBF lumber realization, but management guided Q4 realizations lower with quarter-to-date prices ~6% below Q3 and the Random Lengths composite 12% lower. Real Estate Q4 EBITDA is guided to $60-70 million, implying full-year toward the upper end of the $180-200 million range, buybacks totaled $60 million in Q3 with a $300 million authorization increase, and more timberland dispositions are planned over 12-18 months.

Sony reported record Q2 FY2026 results with sales up 10% YoY to JPY 3,429.4 billion and operating income up 45% to JPY 622.3 billion, with net income up 44% to JPY 449.6 billion. Full-year guidance was raised across all three metrics: sales +4% to JPY 13 trillion, operating income +9% to JPY 1,870 billion, and net income +10% to JPY 1,330 billion. Segment guidance was lifted for G&NS (OI +6% to JPY 700 billion), Music (+6% to JPY 445 billion), Pictures (+33% to JPY 200 billion), and I&SS (+7% to JPY 450 billion), while ET&S was unchanged. Offsets include a JPY 16 billion earthquake loss at Kumamoto, a JPY 30 billion Sony Honda Mobility loss, a ~20% YoY smartphone market decline, and a delayed God of War Laufey release.

National Grid reported H1 FY2027 underlying operating profit of GBP 2.6bn (+13% YoY) and underlying EPS of GBP 0.365 (+22%), with capital investment up 32% to a record GBP 6.7bn. Full-year capital investment guidance was upgraded to GBP 13.5bn and EPS growth guidance nudged up to 15%-16% from a prior 13%-15%, though operating cash flow growth guidance was cut to 15% from 20% on higher capex and interest. The interim dividend rose 3.8% to GBP 0.1697 per share and the five-year 8%-10% EPS CAGR and GBP 70bn capex framework were reiterated, with 80% of the programme now under supply-chain mechanisms and net debt up GBP 4.5bn to GBP 48.6bn.

Consolidated adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations rose 15% YoY to $192.4 million, with Water Solutions adjusted EBITDA up 17% to $178.3 million (93% of the total) on record produced water disposal of 3.45 million barrels per day, up 23% YoY. Management raised FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance by $10 million to $735-$745 million (second raise this fiscal year) and lifted FY2027 growth capex to roughly $250-$270 million from about $200 million. Water Solutions opex fell to $0.20 per barrel from $0.22, while Crude Oil Logistics adjusted EBITDA declined to $11.9 million from $16.6 million on Grand Mesa volumes of 64,000 bpd versus 72,000 bpd. Leverage is expected to reach about four times by fiscal year-end, with the credit agreement repriced 50 bps lower and the ABL accordion raised $50 million to $475 million.

Q2 FY2027 revenue rose 1.4% to $222.2M as expected, with product revenue down 5.1% to $89.9M on order timing pulled into Q1 while service revenue grew 6.4% to $132.3M. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.71 versus $0.62, operating margin expanded to 28.3% from 26.5% on 2.7% lower opex, and gross margin slipped to 80.9% from 81.4% on DDoS acquisition overhead. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue of $885-915M and EPS of $2.65-2.80, guiding Q3 revenue to $240-250M and EPS to $0.90-0.95 against a tough comparison with $15M pulled forward last year. Free cash flow was a $17.8M use tied to working capital, and the company repurchased about 2M shares for roughly $77M.

Q2 FY2027 revenue rose 9% YoY to $21.7 million from $19.9 million, with LED lighting up to $14.9 million from $10.7 million, offset by EV charging falling to $2.8 million from $4.8 million and maintenance to $4.0 million from $4.5 million. Overall gross margin contracted to 28.7% from 31.0% on mix shift within lighting, opex rose to $7.0 million from $6.4 million, and the net loss widened to $0.8 million ($0.20 per share) from $0.6 million ($0.17). Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $100-$102 million (recently raised from $95-$97 million) with positive adjusted EBITDA, and guided Q3 and Q4 to roughly even revenue near $26-27 million each with gross margin normalizing back above 30%. Backlog was $21.6-21.7 million at September 30, with firm POs for the $10-15 million retailer interior project received after quarter-end, implying a substantially higher October backlog that management declined to quantify.

Q2 FY2027 revenue of $336.3M grew 22.7% YoY but fell 1.6% organically, with the growth entirely driven by the first full quarter of Breathe Right and LaCorium; adjusted EPS rose ~6% to $1.13 and adjusted EBITDA margin was ~33.6%. Management lowered the FY2027 outlook to $1.28-1.29B revenue and $4.48-4.55 adjusted EPS, citing Clear Eyes production volatility that began in late September and continued into October with zero safety stock, plus slightly higher interest expense. Full-year Clear Eyes sales are now forecast below $20M with limited second-half improvement, while the ~$190M Breathe Right/LaCorium contribution and ~2% organic growth excluding Clear Eyes are unchanged. Adjusted free cash flow is now expected at least $265M, down slightly on updated revenue and interest assumptions.

ePlus reported Q2 FY2027 net sales of $667.9M, up 9.7% YoY, with product sales up 12.8% to $547.1M and record gross billings of $1.07B. Gross profit rose 11.2% to $180.3M, gross margin expanded 40 bps to 27%, operating income grew 15.8% to $56.5M, and non-GAAP EPS rose 19% to $1.82. Management raised FY2027 guidance to upper single-digit growth in net sales and gross profit, with adjusted EBITDA up low double digits. Open orders rose nearly $750M YoY to about $1.8B, driven by AI, data center, and cloud demand, while professional services revenue declined 11.3% on retail project delays.

Q2 constant-currency revenue rose 10%, above the prior mid-single-digit outlook, with Asia +28% (China +35%), North America +6%, and Europe +3%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 220 bps to 70.2% and operating margin 140 bps to 15.5%, with AUR +9%. FY2027 guidance was raised: revenue growth to ~6%-7% from 5%-6%, gross margin expansion to ~80-100 bps from 50-70 bps, and operating margin expansion to ~80-100 bps from 60-80 bps. Europe's outlook was trimmed to low single digits from low-to-mid single digits on weaker traffic and consumer confidence, and the company repurchased ~$250 million in shares in the quarter, completing FY2027 buyback plans.

STERIS reported Q2 FY27 revenue of $1.6 billion, up 9% as-reported and 8% constant currency organic, with adjusted EPS of $2.94 (+19%, +13% excluding tariff refunds) versus $2.47 last year. Adjusted gross margin rose 100 bps to 45.3% and adjusted EBIT margin 150 bps to 24.6%, both largely driven by ~$20 million of tariff refunds; underlying margins were down slightly as price was offset by inflation. FY27 EPS guidance was raised to $11.35-$11.55 from $11.10-$11.30 (including ~$0.18 of tariff refund benefit), while total revenue growth guidance was unchanged at 7-8% as-reported / 6-7% organic; AST was trimmed to 6-7% from 7-8% and Life Sciences raised to 9-10% from 6-7%. Free cash flow for the first half fell to $492.5 million from $527.7 million on lower working capital contribution, and a new restructuring plan with $45 million of charges and ~$9 million of annualized savings was approved.

Microchip reported September-quarter net sales of $1.622 billion, up 9.2% sequentially and 42.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.97 beating the guidance midpoint by $0.04; non-GAAP gross margin was 66.5% and operating margin 39.5%. About $53 million of infrequent, 100%-margin items (patent licensing, distribution price-protection catch-up, a $10 million customer contract) boosted the quarter and do not repeat. December-quarter guidance is down 3% to up 1% sequentially (midpoint -1%), with non-GAAP gross margin of 64%-65% and EPS of $0.87-$0.95; management frames this as 5%-7% above normal seasonality but below what it expected a quarter ago. Management cited supply constraints at foundries, OSATs and internal fabs, with lead times stretching to six to 32 weeks and unsupported high-margin backlog pushed to later quarters; bookings were strong and book-to-bill well above one.

StepStone reported fee revenues of $298 million (up 37% YoY) and FRE of $126 million (up 61% YoY), with a 42% core FRE margin, up 6 pts YoY, and adjusted net income of $0.66 per share versus $0.54 a year ago. Gross AUM additions were $11 billion in the quarter and a record $43 billion over 12 months, with fee-earning AUM at $158 billion and undeployed fee-earning capital at $42 billion. Management guided to a roughly 42% full-year cash compensation ratio (better than the prior 43% signal) and meaningful margin improvement versus last year, while cautioning that 42% is not a run rate and that G&A will be seasonally higher in fiscal Q3 and Q4. The company plans to retain cash to fund the private wealth profits interest watch-in, suspending the supplemental dividend while maintaining the $0.33 regular quarterly dividend, and a GAAP net loss of $71 million ($0.87 per share) reflected the change in fair value of that watch-in.

UHAL reported Q2 FY2027 earnings of $137 million ($0.71 per non-voting share) versus $106 million ($0.54) a year ago, on record total revenue with equipment rental revenue up $37 million and storage revenue up $16 million (~6%). Moving and storage Adjusted EBITDA rose $5 million to $548 million, but the Adjusted EBITDA margin fell about 90 bps as freight and shipping costs added just under $24.5 million. Same-store occupancy declined 110 bps to 89.5%, and management disclosed no formal forward guidance other than reiterating a projected ~$500 million net fleet CapEx reduction and describing the dealer-expansion catalyst as progressing slower than hoped.

Universal reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $622 million, down 18% YoY, operating income of $43 million versus $68 million, and net income of $13 million versus $34 million. Tobacco segment revenue fell 19% to $534 million and operating income fell to $44 million from $65 million on delayed shipment timing; Ingredients revenue fell 8% to $88 million and swung to a $2 million operating loss. Management maintained that full-year expectations are unchanged, with shipments and results heavily weighted to the second half, and reported uncommitted flue-cured and burley stocks down 45 million kilos to 134 million kilos (19% of inventory, within target range). Net debt rose $82 million YoY to $1.15 billion, with management citing plans to delever as working capital moderates.

Revenue rose 3% to $1.2 billion with DAT up 20% and Communication Services down 3%; net loss widened $68 million to $129 million and adjusted EBITDA fell 4% to $370 million. Full-year EBITDA guidance was cut to roughly flat versus prior year, while free cash flow guidance improved to over $225 million and CapEx was trimmed to $850-900 million. Management disclosed that recent airline announcements will ultimately affect 15%-20% of aviation revenue and guided FY2028 aviation revenue below FY2027, offsetting an awards pipeline that includes about $2 billion of DAT awards planned for FY2027 versus $1.6 billion last year.

Q2 FY2027 revenue rose ~5% to $889 million with Adjusted EBITDA of $287 million and a 32.2% margin, down from the record 34.1% first-half margin. Management cut full-year revenue guidance by 3% at the midpoint to $3.35 billion (Adjusted EBITDA down 1% to $1.015 billion), citing lower resin inflation rather than end-market deterioration, though residential demand also softened with rates near 7.5%. Pre-watch pulled into Q1 was revised up to $40-50 million from $25-30 million, and management pointed to a low-single-digit organic second half with pricing a dollar-for-dollar offset to materials and transport costs.

Merger-announcement call that also covered both companies' Q3 results. Array reported Q3 revenue of $330 million (including one month of AWM; $321 million excluding), adjusted gross margin of 22.8% including a 330 bps charge for a 45X rebate reserve, and adjusted EBITDA of $32 million (10% margin), with a record $2.6 billion order book up 42% YoY and book-to-bill of 1.6x. Shoals reported record revenue of $195.3 million, up 44% YoY, gross margin of 31.9% (up 160 bps QoQ), adjusted EBITDA of about $40 million (20.4% margin), and $186 million of new orders, with results above its guided range. The deal is stock-for-stock (1.6931 Array shares per Shoals share, Shoals holders owning about 65%), targets $100 million of annual synergies by year three, includes $161.3 million of preferred redemption within 90 days, and carries a preliminary 2027 outlook of $2.2-2.4 billion revenue and $410-480 million adjusted EBITDA against a $3.4 billion backlog.

H1 FY2027 operating income was JPY 2.2 trillion on sales of JPY 26.96 trillion, with net income of JPY 2.24 trillion; OI rose year-on-year as cost reduction, price revisions, value-chain profits and tariff mitigation offset Middle East disruption and material costs. Toyota revised full-year operating income guidance up JPY 500 billion to JPY 3.9 trillion, with revenue forecast at JPY 53.5 trillion on FX assumptions of JPY 157/USD and EUR 182. Consolidated vehicle sales fell 25,000 units YoY (but rose 26,000 ex-Hino), while Toyota/Lexus unit sales fell to 96% of the prior year on weak China demand and the Middle East, and the electrified ratio reached 55.6%. Shareholder returns were expanded: interim dividend of JPY 50 (up JPY 5), FY dividend of JPY 100, buyback authorization raised JPY 300 billion to JPY 1.3 trillion, and an additional 1 billion treasury shares cancelled.

Total Q2 revenue fell 5.5% YoY to $632M, described as favorable to expectations despite lower math capture rates, while Higher Ed was up slightly and K-12 fell 9.6% to $325M. Adjusted EBITDA was $251M at a 39.6% margin and gross margin held at 79.2%; first-half revenue was $1.2B, down 1.9%. FY2027 guidance was reaffirmed at $2.115B-2.175B revenue and $750M-790M adjusted EBITDA (~35.9% margin, up 50 bps), with the only change being a softer enrollment assumption of flat to down 1% versus 1% growth prior. Management pointed to FY2028 acceleration from the K-12 ELA super cycle, MCP/AI integrations, and a two-business-unit leadership change.

Microchip reported September-quarter net sales of $1.622 billion, up 9.2% sequentially and 42.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 66.5% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.97, $0.04 above the midpoint of guidance. However, roughly $53 million of the quarter was one-time (patent licensing, a distribution pricing effect, and a customer contract), so the underlying product growth was more modest. December-quarter guidance calls for revenue of down 3% to up 1% (midpoint -1%), non-GAAP gross margin of 64%-65%, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.87-$0.95, a step down sequentially, which management frames as roughly 5%-7% above normal seasonality after stripping the one-offs. Bookings were strong and book-to-bill remained above one, backlog built, and management cited supply constraints and stretched lead times of six to 32 weeks limiting shipments of high-margin products.

Phibro reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $386.8 million, up 6% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up 4% to $64.3 million and net income up 11% to $29.5 million. Growth came from Mineral Nutrition (+17%) and Performance Products (+16%), while Animal Health grew 3% and its adjusted EBITDA fell 1% on higher SG&A and a $5.2 million virginiamycin decline in Brazil. Fiscal 2027 guidance was maintained at $1.55-1.6 billion net sales, $258-268 million adjusted EBITDA, and $3.41-3.59 adjusted EPS, with management attributing the hold to expenses shifting from Q1 into Q2 rather than a raised outlook. Management described poultry producer margin pressure and inventory trimming as temporary but flagged soft near-term protein producer profitability; the CFO also cited excess inventory as a priority to reduce.

AMSC reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $94.0 million versus $65.9 million a year ago, up more than 40%, with Grid up 41% and Wind up 51%. Non-GAAP net income was $9.1 million, or $0.20 per share, flat with the year-ago $0.20, while GAAP net income fell to $3.0 million, or $0.06 per share, from $4.8 million, or $0.11, and gross margin compressed to 28% from 31% though it rose 190 bps sequentially. Q3 guidance calls for revenue above $80 million, net income above break-even, and non-GAAP net income above $7 million, or $0.15 per share, with management citing customer pull-ins that shifted projects into Q2 and a large semiconductor project that builds in Q3 but ships in Q4. Orders exceeded $95 million in Q2, first-half orders of about $230 million more than doubled year over year, and 12-month backlog of nearly $320 million rose 50% year over year.

Paylocity reported Q1 FY2027 total revenue of $451.7 million, up 11% YoY, with recurring and other revenue of $424.5 million up 12%, coming in $7.2 million above the top end of revenue guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $159.5 million at a 35.3% margin, $3.5 million above the high end of guidance. Management raised FY2027 total revenue guidance by $30 million at the midpoint to $1.910-$1.925 billion and increased adjusted EBITDA guidance to $711.5-$721.5 million, passing through more than the Q1 beat; the raise reflects stable demand, strong retention, and the September 25 bp rate hike. GAAP gross margin was pressured year-over-year on staffing timing ahead of year-end, which management characterized as timing rather than structural.

Prospect Capital reported September-quarter net investment income of $76 million, or $0.15 per common share, with NAV of approximately $2.9 billion, or $5.36 per share, and a net debt to total assets ratio of 25%. The board approved a $200 million common share repurchase authorization and monthly distributions of $0.035 per share for November, December, and January. Originations were $90 million against $257 million of repayments and exits, producing net repayments of $167 million, while non-accruals fell to 0.2% at fair value and 1.8% at cost. No guidance was provided and the Q&A session drew no questions.

Peloton reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $559 million, up 2% YoY and $4 million above the midpoint of guidance, its third consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth. Gross margin was 61.3% (up 975 bps YoY) and adjusted EBITDA was $168 million, both well above guidance, though roughly $25 million of the beat came from tariff favorability and lower recall costs; ex-those items adjusted EBITDA was $143 million, $3 million above the midpoint. Ending paid connected fitness subscriptions of 2.475 million hit the high end of guidance with 1.7% net churn. Full-year FY2027 revenue guidance of $2.3-2.4 billion (down ~4% at midpoint), ~54% gross margin, $475-525 million adjusted EBITDA and at least $350 million free cash flow were all unchanged from last quarter.

Hyperliquid Strategies reported Q1 FY2027 results dominated by treasury movements: net income of ~$621 million after a ~$172 million tax provision, driven by ~$803 million of unrealized HYPE gains as the token rose from $65.04 to $90.99. NAV rose ~82% to $3.4 billion, cash increased to ~$255 million with zero debt, and the company raised ~$911 million net, deploying $785 million into 9.1 million HYPE at an average $86.44 and $17 million into buybacks at $6.36. The company announced it is applying to form its own FCM as a neutral bridge for U.S. Hyperliquid customers, with a timeline of roughly three to six months and single-digit-million-dollar one-time cost; no formal financial guidance was provided and results are non-operating, driven by token price.

ScanSource reported Q1 FY2027 net sales growth of 30% year-over-year with reported net profits up 9%; non-GAAP net income was $17.7 million and non-GAAP EPS $0.86. Profitability was pressured by a lower-margin large-hardware mix (~110-120 bps of margin compression) and customer-specific bad debt reserves in Brazil tied to Oi S.A., which management characterized as largely confined to Q1. FY2027 guidance was raised to $3.8-4.0 billion net sales and $175-185 million adjusted EBITDA, now including the September 1 MicroAge acquisition, with free cash flow reaffirmed at least $85 million. Free cash flow was a $44 million use in Q1 on higher working capital, and share repurchases totaled $5 million with ~$116 million remaining on the authorization.

Atlassian reported Q1 FY2027 total revenue of $1.8B, up 24% YoY, with cloud revenue up 31% to $1.3B and subscription ARR up 22.5% to $6.8B; GAAP operating margin was 11% and free cash flow was $463M (26% margin, up 304% YoY). RPO grew 44% to $4.7B and gross margin rose to 85.2%, but management flagged that Q2 cloud guidance implies about 4 points of deceleration and that ARR growth will decline over the next three quarters on tougher comps and lapping the DX acquisition. The full-year guide was raised by less than the size of the beat, which management attributed to a prudent stance amid macro and geopolitical uncertainty, and no meaningful usage-based pricing revenue is assumed in FY2027. Cloud revenue was modestly reduced by hybrid Data Center deals that shifted some revenue to Data Center.

Tapestry reported Q1 FY2027 revenue up 12% pro forma to $1.9 billion, operating margin up 230 bps to over 23%, and EPS up 32% to $1.82, beating guidance by about $0.27. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $8.5-8.6 billion (6-7% constant-currency growth), operating margin above 24%, and EPS to $8.25-$8.35 from a prior $7.80-$7.90, with increased shareholder returns of about $2 billion including $1.7 billion in buybacks. Coach grew 16% constant currency with broad regional strength (North America +7%, Greater China +41%, Europe +27%), while Kate Spade declined 10%, in line with guidance, with gross margin up 190 bps. Gross margin expanded 220 bps to 78.7%, including a 70-bp tariff benefit, and Q2 revenue is guided up 5-6% constant currency with EPS of about $3.05.

Doximity reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $174.5 million, up 4% year-over-year and 2% above the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA of $89 million (51% margin) 9% above the high end. FY2027 revenue guidance was raised to $678-683 million (6% growth at midpoint, a $4.5 million midpoint increase), while adjusted EBITDA guidance of $317-325 million implies continued AI investment and a 47% midpoint margin. Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 88% from 92% last quarter on AI cost scaling, NRR slipped to 103% overall and 106% for top-20 customers, and Q3 revenue is guided to $195-196 million (6% growth).

Lightspeed reported organic revenue of $323.8M, up 15% and at the high end of the 12%-16% outlook, with software revenue up 9% (14% in growth engines), total GTV up 8% to $25.8B, gross margin of 44% vs 46% a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA of $22.7M (7.0% margin, up from $21.3M). Adjusted free cash flow was $4M versus a $4.5M outflow last quarter. Management left FY2027 guidance unchanged (revenue $1.225B-$1.265B, adjusted EBITDA $75M-$95M) and introduced Q3 guidance of $310M-$320M revenue and $25M-$30M adjusted EBITDA. The key change was a deliberate tightening of deal parameters: net new locations fell sharply to ~800 from ~2,000 in the prior-year quarter, but new locations carried 27% more software revenue, software ARPU rose 7%, and payments penetration reached 45%.

GHM reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $69.8M, up 6% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $10.3M (14.8% margin, up 64%) and adjusted EPS of $0.52 (up 68%). Gross margin expanded 650 bps to 28.2%, though this was partly due to lower material receipts versus an unusually high prior-year quarter; the company reaffirmed FY2027 revenue guidance of $285-295M and adjusted EBITDA of $35-40M, while raising its gross margin outlook by ~50 bps. Backlog hit a record $561M (up 12% YoY, seventh straight record), orders were $73.7M (1.1x book-to-bill), and space revenue grew 59% while energy and process fell 17%. The key change versus prior periods is the sharp margin improvement and the FlackTek contribution (revenue $9.5M), offset by softness in large capital projects.

Q2 revenue rose 5% to CAD 274 million with gross margin up 280 bps to 66.8%, but D2C comparable sales fell 7.5% and adjusted EBIT swung to a loss of CAD 22 million (margin -7.9% vs -5.5%), with adjusted EPS loss widening to CAD 0.20 from CAD 0.14. EMEA revenue fell 14% (D2C comps -27%) on softer demand and logistics-driven product delays, while Asia Pacific grew 21% and North America 8%. Full-year guidance was maintained at low single-digit revenue growth and 11%-12% adjusted EBIT margin, with the U.S. tariff impact now estimated at 100 bps versus the prior less-than-200-bps estimate; D2C comps remained negative in October.

GSI Technology reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $6 million, within guidance but below the midpoint, and a GAAP net loss of $7 million, or $0.18 per diluted share. Gross margin of 48.5% fell well short of the 53%-55% guidance range on higher wafer and assembly/burn-in/test costs, and Q3 guidance of $5-6 million revenue with gross margin of approximately 38%-40% implies further deterioration. Management cited insufficient inventory and extended lead times that delayed customer shipments and are also weighing on the Q3 outlook, with price increases on new orders and existing backlog (effective January 1) expected to support recovery beginning in Q4 FY2027. Operating expenses rose to $10.4 million from $6.7 million a year ago, including roughly $2 million of non-routine legal and professional fees tied to an internal assessment of vendor matters in foreign operations.

Haemonetics reported Q2 FY2027 organic revenue growth of 10% and adjusted EPS of $1.35, up 6%, with plasma up 18%, Blood Management up 7%, MedSurg up 6% and Interventional Technologies up 3% organic. FY2027 organic revenue guidance was raised to 6%-9% from 4%-7% (reported 8%-11% from 5%-8%) on apheresis strength, but adjusted operating margin expansion guidance was cut to 0-50 bps from 50-100 bps on investments ahead of CSL plasma share gains, performance-based comp and freight/energy inflation. Q2 adjusted operating margin fell 40 bps to 26.3% and gross margin of 61.9% (up 140 bps) included a ~200 bps tariff refund benefit. First-half operating cash flow rose 40% to $180 million and free cash flow rose ~57% to $143 million.

Q2 FY2027 net sales from continuing operations rose 24% to $1.43 billion at the high end of guidance, and Adjusted EBITDA of $455 million came in above guidance, with margin up 450 bps to 31.8% and adjusted diluted EPS up 68% to $0.42. However, management cut its market assumption, now expecting a mid-single-digit decline versus a prior low-single-digit decline, and full-year revenue guidance of $4.99–$5.133 billion was only reaffirmed, with the second half guided down slightly year-over-year. DR&A's 51% growth included roughly 21 points from distribution load-in and 16 points from channel normalization, leaving about 14% underlying growth. Full-year free cash flow guidance was raised to more than $650 million from $600 million or more.

Lionsgate Studios reported Q2 FY2027 revenue up 41% YoY to $669 million, with Adjusted OIBDA of $72 million, operating income of $29 million, and adjusted EPS of $0.07. Studio segment profit more than doubled to $110 million, driven by motion picture revenue up 30% to $359 million and TV revenue up 56% to $310 million (22 episodic deliveries vs. seven). Management reaffirmed confidence in its FY2027 forecast of strong Adjusted OIBDA growth and pointed to visibility into FY2028-2029, citing a $1.487 billion backlog (58% TV) and 10 of the next 15 wide releases being branded IP; no specific numeric guidance was raised, but leverage improved to 3.7x from 4.3x.

Dorian reported record quarterly results: reported TCE revenue per available day of just shy of $97,000 (highest in corporate history for a third straight quarter), Helios Pool spot/COA TCE of $115,163 and overall pool TCE of $99,915, adjusted EBITDA of $242 million including $63.6 million of gains on sale (or $178.4 million excluding them). The company declared a $1.25 per share regular dividend (21st in total) and held $578.8 million of free cash at quarter-end, rising to almost $785 million currently, with pro forma net cash of about $320 million after the Clermont and Captain John NP sales. Management gave no formal earnings guidance but guided forward cash cost per day to about $27,000 (up slightly on fewer vessel days), TCIN expense down to about $29,954 per day (~$13.8 million quarterly), and Q3 cash interest of ~$6.1 million with ~$9.8 million amortization; it added three Hanwha 90,000 CBM newbuilds ($338 million, 2030 delivery) and refinanced into a seven-year $368.4 million facility at SOFR+140. Key change versus prior quarter: record cash generation and continued fleet monetization into newbuilds, though U.S. Gulf loadings slowed to about 102/month from about 113.

Revenue rose to $26.6M from $25.3M in Q2 and $24.3M a year ago, but GAAP net income of $3.1M ($0.34/share) fell from $3.7M ($0.41) in Q3 2025 and Economic Earnings declined to $4.4M ($0.48) from $5.7M ($0.64) year over year, with $1.7M of severance and higher taxes offsetting revenue. Still, income nearly doubled sequentially from $1.5M ($0.17) and Economic Earnings rose from $3.0M ($0.33). Firmwide AUM/AUA was $17.1B, with AUM net outflows of $0.3B and market depreciation of $0.6B in the quarter. No formal guidance was issued; the board declared a $0.15 quarterly dividend, and management cited a robust pipeline, ETF assets of $430M at quarter-end (about $460M since), and roughly $30M of new private capital commitments.

Westrock reported record Q3 FY2026 consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $26.4 million, up ~14% YoY, with nine-month EBITDA of $73.7 million up 58%. Net sales of ~$300 million fell 15.4% YoY, driven by ~$26 million in tariff refunds recorded as a sales reduction, lower green coffee pass-through, and the prior single-serve customer loss; excluding tariffs, sales were ~$326 million. Operating profit swung to $3.2 million from an $8.6 million loss, and the company reaffirmed FY2026 EBITDA guidance of $90-100 million (current estimate $95 million, +36%) while initiating a 2027 outlook of ~$130 million EBITDA (+35% over the midpoint). It closed a $600 million upsized credit facility maturing 2031 and repurchased $40 million of convertible notes.

WES reported Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $708 million, up 12% YoY but down modestly sequentially, with DCF of $512 million and net income to limited partners of $325 million. Partnership-wide natural gas throughput hit a record 5.9 Bcf/d (up 8% sequentially, Delaware up 20%), and produced water set another Delaware record. Management now expects full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA above the midpoint of its already-raised $2.75-$2.95 billion range, with DCF and FCF guidance ranges unchanged and 2027 capex expected in line with 2026. The quarter's sequential softness came from West Texas contract mix and pricing, DJ Basin declines, lower NGL/skim oil, and seasonal O&M, partially offset by a full quarter of Brazos.

Normalized FFO was $43.8 million ($0.34/share), up 29.3% YoY, and Adjusted EBITDAre was $133.5 million, both above consensus; retained-hotel RevPAR rose 8.3% to $128.38 and Adjusted Hotel EBITDA grew 16.2% with 130 bps of margin expansion to 15.4%. Guidance was mixed: RevPAR outlook was raised for retained and Exit Hotels and a new $96 million (plus ~$13 million from CBRE-based RevPAR growth) operating upside plan targets ~20% retained-hotel margins, but the hotel EBITDA range high end was cut to $124-$134 million on a $3.8 million James Nautilus delay and Exit Hotel underperformance, and net lease NOI guidance fell to $373-$379 million. Full-year Normalized FFO is guided to $1.07-$1.22 per share and CAD turned positive on a rolling four-quarter basis from an $83 million deficit a year ago. The board unanimously rejected TKO LLC's unsolicited $2 billion hotel-portfolio proposal as significantly undervaluing the assets.

Total company revenue was $274.3 million with adjusted operating income of $39.2 million; the Sphere segment grew revenue 14% YoY to $198.9 million and segment AOI rose to $32.4 million from $17.1 million on 241 Wizard of Oz performances versus 220 combined prior-year showings. MSG Networks deteriorated sharply, with revenue down to $75.4 million from $88.4 million and AOI to $6.8 million from $19.3 million on a ~15.5% subscriber decline, prompting a non-cash goodwill impairment charge. No quantitative guidance was given, but management said it still expects growth in 2027, reaffirmed 3-4 Sphere Experiences by end-2027, and guided to a new venue announcement likely this quarter. The main negative changes were the MSG Networks impairment and the scrapping of the From the Edge concept.

Total revenue was $37.7 million versus $32.5 million in Q3 2025, including $33.4 million in U.S. neffy net product revenue, $2.6 million in ex-U.S. supply revenue, and $1.7 million in collaboration revenue. Total U.S. market share surpassed 5% (from 4% a year ago), end-user demand rose 42% year-over-year, and field-targeted account share improved to 9% from 6%. SG&A fell to $43.5 million, down more than 40% from the first-half 2026 quarterly average, and the company reaffirmed its path to cash flow breakeven by year-end 2027 on $138.4 million in cash. Net revenue growth lagged demand growth due to inventory timing, and gross-to-net remains around 50%.

Sempra reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS of $1.34 versus $0.12 a year ago and adjusted EPS of $1.40, up 26% from $1.11. Management guided to the high end of the 2026 adjusted EPS range of $4.80-$5.30, affirmed the 2027 range of $5.10-$5.70 and the 7%-9% long-term EPS growth rate, while flagging that pending regulatory outcomes could put 2027 results in the lower half of the range. Texas drove the quarter with $154 million of higher equity earnings, and Oncor plans a roughly 20% increase to its $47.5 billion capital plan in February 2027. A CPUC proposed decision denying the GRC petition for modification creates a $188 million revenue requirement headwind, limiting California earnings to the low end of its 2027 guidance range if not corrected.

Surf Air reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $36.5 million, within its $35.5-$37.5 million guidance range and up 25% year-over-year and 24% quarter-over-quarter, with an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $6.7 million inside the $4-$7 million guide and 36% better than Q2. Surf On Demand revenue more than doubled to $19 million (+121% YoY) and surpassed scheduled service revenue of $17.5 million, which fell 15% YoY on EAS route exits, while airline Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1.2 million. Full-year revenue guidance of $128-$138 million was reaffirmed, but the full-year Adjusted EBITDA loss outlook was widened to $32-$35 million from the prior range due to higher fuel prices (up ~37% per gallon YoY) and extended SurfOS implementation periods; SurfOS revenue was not material in the quarter. Q4 guidance was set at $36.4-$46.4 million revenue and a $2.4-$5.4 million Adjusted EBITDA loss, and no 2027 guidance or breakeven date was provided.

Stoneridge reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted revenue of $180 million, up 30% (nearly 26% core, excluding FX and $6 million Mexico contract manufacturing), the fastest organic growth in over three years, with adjusted EBITDA up over 40% YoY to $7.3 million (4.1% margin, +34 bps). However, adjusted gross margin fell 382 bps to 19.9% on inventory-related expenses and legacy warranty settlements ($3 million incremental), and reported results absorbed a ~$24 million non-cash pre-tax charge tied to a $25.5 million arbitration award on former Control Devices PM sensor claims. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $690-700 million ($37.5 million higher at midpoint), but adjusted EBITDA is now expected at the bottom of the $20-25 million range due to memory-chip inflation, unfavorable FX, and the legacy-matter costs. MirrorEye hit a record $37 million in sales (+48% YoY), and a new non-MirrorEye vision system win is expected to add ~$180 million through 2028, ramping from early 2027.

Starling Oncology reported record Q3 revenue of $169.8 million, up 24.3% year-over-year, with Adjusted EBITDA of $3.4 million (versus $0.2 million in Q2 and a $3.5 million loss a year ago) that exceeded the top end of the guided Q3 range. Specialty pharmacy revenue rose 44% to $109.3 million at a 24.2% gross margin, which management attributed partly to rebates and favorable drug price moves it does not expect to recur, guiding pharmacy margins to normalize to the high teens. Total gross margin expanded roughly 420 bps to 18.1%, and the MLR improved to 81% from 85.5% in Q2. However, the capitated revenue target for 2027 was cut to roughly $220 million from a prior $300 million after anchor Florida partners did not expand statewide, which analysts pressed on throughout; management reaffirmed 100% capitated revenue growth in 2027 versus 2026 and full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $4 million-$6 million.

Revenue was essentially flat at $320 million with adjusted operating income of $50 million (-2%), a 15.7% margin (down 30 bps), and adjusted EPS of $1.69 (+4%) driven by a lower share count; free cash flow rose 8% to $137 million through nine months. Strength in ETS (revenue +12% to $43 million, margin +80 bps to 42.5%) and healthcare enrollment (+9%, now 54% of U.S. Higher Education) was offset by Australia, where enrollment fell 9% and a $134 million non-cash goodwill/intangibles impairment was recorded. Management said full-year results will likely fall outside the notional outlook, guided 2027 revenue to roughly flat with negligible margin expansion, and plans ~$50 million in incremental growth investments. Australia's international visa approvals slowed sharply, at times down 80% year over year, and the government closed the onshore transfer market.

Savers Value Village reported Q3 net sales up 8.5% to $463 million (8.9% constant currency) with comps +4.2%, U.S. net sales +12.2% on a 5.9% comp, and Canada net sales +2.5% with comps +1.5%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 8% to $76 million (16.4% of sales), gross margin expanded 100 bps to 43.1% on COGS, GAAP EPS was $0.15 and adjusted EPS $0.16. Full-year guidance was updated to net sales of $1.77-$1.78 billion, comps of 3.5%-4.0%, and Adjusted EBITDA of $270-$275 million, with Q4 revenue roughly flat (up mid-to-high single digits excluding last year's 53rd week) and comps modestly below Q3 as the company laps an 8.8% U.S. comp. Management reiterated the 50-100 bps annual EBITDA margin expansion framework beginning in 2027, with 2027 at the low end (~50 bps), and disclosed ~$10 million of annualized labor savings from the new Autotagger upon full deployment by early 2028, requiring ~$40 million of CapEx.

SoundHound reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $62.4 million, up 48% year-over-year, including nearly one month (~26 days, ~$14 million) of LivePerson contribution following the September 4 close. Non-GAAP gross margin was 50.3%, down 9 percentage points year-over-year on new agentic AI ramp and higher cloud usage. FY2026 revenue guidance was narrowed and the midpoint raised to $250-260 million from $230-260 million, while FY2027 revenue guidance of $350-400 million was reaffirmed alongside a first-time target of sustainable positive adjusted EBITDA in the second half of 2027, supported by at least $120 million of identified annualized cost reductions ($80 million actioned before January 1). The key change is a shift away from point-in-time license revenue (cut to ~10% of revenue from ~33% in Q2) toward hosted recurring structures, which management says drives the ~$35 million reduction versus an additive ~$290 million 2026 base.

Molson Coors reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated net sales revenue of $2.9 billion, down 1.2% YoY, underlying pre-tax income of $349 million, down 17.4%, and underlying EPS of $1.46, down 12.6%. The company cut full-year 2026 guidance across all key metrics: NSR now expected -1% to -2% (vs. prior flat +/-1%), underlying pre-tax income -21% to -24% (vs. prior -15% to -18%), underlying EPS -16% to -19% (vs. prior -11% to -15%), and underlying free cash flow to $1 billion +/-10% (vs. prior $1.1 billion +/-10%).
