Management cited U.S. category softness (industry down more than 4%), increased U.K. promotional activity, elevated Midwest Premium and aluminum costs, and a tighter freight market, with Midwest Premium alone driving roughly $30 million of YoY cost increase in the quarter and expected to add approximately $130 million for the full year (about 10 points of pre-tax income impact, or more than $0.50 of EPS).

Adjusted net investment income was $0.15 per share against a $0.17 quarterly dividend, with total investment income of $28.5 million ($0.34/share). NAV fell $0.97 per share to $5.61, of which $0.68 came from the previously disclosed portfolio sale to a Pantheon-sponsored continuation vehicle. Non-accruals rose to 14.2% at cost and 3.4% at fair value from 7.4% and 1.6%, and net realized losses were $75.8 million ($0.91/share). Management declared a $0.17 Q4 dividend, kept $253 million in cash and 0.16x net leverage, and declined to give any timeline or detail on the KBW-assisted strategic review.

Total Q3 revenue fell 7.4% to $519.2 million (-5.8% same-store), adjusted EBITDA dropped 36% to $36.6 million, and digital advertising declined 13.9% on search-driven pressure in indirect programmatic revenue. Digital-only subscription revenue grew 5.3% to $46 million with record ARPU of $10.82 (+23%), and digital other revenue rose 24.8% to $21.3 million. Full-year same-store revenue guidance was cut to a mid-single-digit decline from a prior low-single-digit decline, with the 50% digital revenue mix target pushed to 2027 and full-year adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow now expected to decline versus 2025. Management implemented a $100 million annualized cost reduction program in late Q3 and guided to significant sequential EBITDA and free cash flow improvement in Q4.

Q3 revenue was $399 million at the high end of the outlook, recurring revenue $359 million also at the high end, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.70 beat the top of the range by $0.11. Total ARR grew 1% (2% constant currency) and cloud ARR grew 11%, while Q3 recurring revenue declined year-over-year against a first-half-skewed linearity comparison. FY26 revenue range was narrowed to the high end (-1% to 0%), recurring revenue to 1%-2%, and EPS guidance raised to $2.86-$2.90 with operating margin expansion now seen at ~200 bps versus 100 bps expected at the start of the year. Q4 guidance calls for recurring revenue down 2%-4% and total revenue down 4%-6% on upfront-recognition timing.

Q3 revenue was approximately $235 million, down 26% year-over-year, with ex-TAC gross profit of $93.5 million, down 28% and decelerating from a 6% decline in Q2. Enterprise ex-TAC gross profit fell 14% (North America -15%, EMEA weak in August, APAC +5%) while direct response/SME ex-TAC gross profit fell 50% on AI-summary and algorithm-driven page view declines of 20% to 60%. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $8.1 million, a $272 million non-cash goodwill impairment was recorded, and free cash flow before interest was -$1.4 million ($33 million total cash use including $31 million semi-annual interest). No formal guidance was given; management said early Q4 shows some recovery versus Q3 on operational improvements and seasonality, and that it is further scrutinizing costs and capital structure.

Teleflex reported Q3 2026 revenue of $567.8 million, up 0.2% GAAP and 3.0% pro forma adjusted constant currency, with adjusted operating margin of 25% (up 300 bps) and adjusted EPS of $2.63, up 39.2% year over year and ahead of expectations. Vascular grew 4.6% and Surgical 5.1%, while Interventional returned to positive growth at 0.2% as integration disruptions eased. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $7.50-$7.75 from $6.90-$7.20, including a $0.31 IEEPA tariff refund benefit, while pro forma constant currency revenue growth guidance was maintained at 3.5%-4.5%. The company repurchased about $350 million of shares since July 1, $100 million more than previously announced, and noted the Acute Care and Interventional Urology divestiture may slip into 2027 pending FTC review.

Taseko (TGB) reported Q3 F2026 revenue of CAD 342 million, up 100% YoY, with Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 161 million (a quarterly record) and cash flow from operations of CAD 122 million; consolidated copper sales were 37.4 million pounds. 2026 production guidance was raised by 5 million pounds to 115-120 million pounds, but management guided Q4 lower due to the transition to oxidized ore at Gibraltar, with recoveries averaging 77% and costs at $2.72/lb. Florence Copper produced 7 million pounds (up 35% QoQ) and C1 costs fell 25% to $3.54/lb, though sulfuric acid costs are expected to rise next year and leverage remains about 1x net debt/EBITDA.

SPG reported Q3 real estate FFO of $3.37/share, up 4.7% YoY, with domestic property NOI +6.6% and portfolio NOI +6.7%. Comparable mall and outlet sales rose 4.9% and occupancy reached 96.5%, the highest combined level since 2016, while initial new-deal rents jumped 17% YoY with tenant allowances down 10%. Management raised full-year 2026 real estate FFO guidance by $0.10 to $13.30-$13.40/share (about 5% growth at the midpoint) and declared a $2.30 Q4 dividend, up 4.5% YoY. Reported FFO of $3.09 was reduced by $0.27/share of non-cash mark-to-market and equity revaluation losses, and management flagged roughly $0.30 of interest expense headwind for 2027.

Solventum reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $1.95 billion, down 7% reported and 2.8% organic, as the reversal of $125 million in ERP-related advanced orders from Q2 created a ~630 bps organic headwind; normalized organic growth was ~4%. EPS was $1.45 including a ~$0.35 hit from the order reversal, gross margin rose 120 bps YoY to 57.1%, and operating margin fell 70 bps to 19.9% (~22.3% excluding the ERP timing). Management nudged FY2026 organic growth to the high end of the 2.5%-3% range, moved operating margin toward the high end of 22.2%-22.7%, and raised EPS guidance to $7.20-$7.30 from $7.10-$7.20 while maintaining $200-300M free cash flow. The renegotiated 3M supply agreement eliminated an anticipated 100 bps 2027 gross margin headwind, and separation is now more than 90% complete.

Wendy's reported Q3 FY2026 global systemwide sales down 5.9% and U.S. same-restaurant sales down 5.7%, with traffic falling 11.9% offset by average check growth of 6.2%; the U.S. comp improved 130 bps sequentially from Q2. Total adjusted revenue was $435.6 million (down 1.6%), adjusted EBITDA fell $24.6 million to $113.4 million, and adjusted EPS was $0.13, with G&A up $15.2 million including $11.9 million of Dave's Way investment and a $9.1 million doubtful-accounts charge for franchisee deferrals. Management gave no formal forward guidance beyond stating Q4 has started with early improvement and that trajectory details will come on the next call; net debt leverage was 5.2x. Key changes versus prior period: a location-optional breakfast strategy worth up to $200 million in restaurant-level EBITDA, an LOI to acquire up to 163 Meritage restaurants, and rejection of an unsolicited acquisition offer.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 2% to $176.0 million, but comparable sales fell 6.4% on a 4.9% traffic decline and 2.1% mix headwind, with restaurant-level margin contracting 270 bps to 10.4% and adjusted EBITDA a $6.8 million loss versus a $4.4 million loss a year ago. Management guided Q4 comps to about +4% (including a 150 bp gift card lap headwind) and Q4 restaurant margin to roughly 11%, with one-time costs of about 60 bps, and set the full-year outlook at comps down about 5.5%, restaurant margin of 11-11.5%, and adjusted EBITDA of -$23 million to -$20 million. October comps turned positive at about +5% with 4% transaction growth, and management sized roughly 150 bps of food-cost and a couple hundred bps of labor-efficiency opportunity for 2027 while cutting 2027 net new openings to about half the 2026 level.

Q3 revenue rose 3% YoY to $738 million, in line with expectations of flat to low single-digit growth, while normalized adjusted EBITDA grew 13% to $170 million, beating the $155 million guide by $15 million and expanding margin 200 bps to 23%. Air marketplace bookings fell 1% on a 300-400 bps Middle East conflict and fuel-price headwind, though total marketplace bookings were flat and management expects sequential improvement into Q4. Full-year pro forma EBITDA guidance was raised $10 million to approximately $610 million and FCF guidance improved, while revenue and bookings growth outlooks were reaffirmed. Reported free cash flow was negative $48 million, attributed to $15 million of refinancing fees and $40 million of accrued interest, absent which it would have been positive.

Clinical-stage biotech with no product revenue; Q3 FY2026 net loss widened to $22.3 million from net income of $45.4 million a year earlier, the prior-year figure inflated by a $58.1 million warrant fair-value gain versus $3.6 million other income this year. R&D rose to $18.1 million from $9 million and G&A to $7.8 million from $3.7 million, driven by SAFEGUARD trial costs and stock-based compensation. The company ended the quarter with $205 million in cash and projects funding through 2028, including $13.4 million of warrant exercise proceeds. Enrollment guidance is unchanged: SAFEGUARD adult and adolescent cohorts are fully enrolled, pediatric step-down was approved by the DMC in September, full enrollment is reaffirmed for Q4 with top-line data in 2H 2027; FDA granted Fast Track designation in October.

StandardAero reported Q3 revenue of $1.56 billion, up 4% year-over-year, adjusted EBITDA of $225 million up 15% with margins expanding 130 bps to 14.4%, and adjusted diluted EPS up 30% to $0.39. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance across the board: revenue to $6.525-6.645 billion (~9% growth vs prior 6%), adjusted EBITDA to $905-920 million (~13% vs prior 11%), and adjusted EPS to $1.57-1.62 (~26% vs prior 23%), while reiterating adjusted free cash flow guidance of $270-300 million. The quarter reflected margin expansion in engine services and continued profitability on LEAP and CFM56 DFW programs, partially offset by military component repair delays tied to Middle Eastern conflict outlays. Management also announced an increase in share repurchase authorization to $1.01 billion and a $350 million accelerated share repurchase.

SandRidge reported Q3 FY2026 production of 20.9 MBOE/d, up 10% YoY with oil up 8%, revenue of $54 million (up 37% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $39 million (up 44% YoY). Adjusted net income was $23.8 million, or $0.64 per share, versus $15.5 million, or $0.42 per share, a year earlier; GAAP net income of $31 million ($0.83 per share) included a ~$14 million deferred tax revaluation benefit. The $48 million Cherokee bolt-on closed intra-quarter and added only partial-period production, with management citing roughly a 10% incremental production uplift and about 5% to annual volumes. No explicit updated production or capital guidance was issued beyond reaffirming the 10-well program and $10-12 million adjusted G&A, while management flagged emerging service-cost inflation in rig rates, tubulars and pressure pumping.

SEG reported Q3 FY2026 total operating EBITDA positive for a second straight quarter at $362K, a $3.2M/113% swing from the $2.9M loss in Q3 2025, with hospitality and entertainment positive and landlord operations at a loss. Management said the quarter underperformed expectations due to record Las Vegas heat (110F July, 105F August game highs) and a NYC nor'easter that forced cancellation of two sold-out Pier 17 concerts; concert series revenue fell 18% and Las Vegas revenue fell 4%. Offsets included G&A down 65% to $6.2M (down 4% excluding prior-year leadership costs), adjusted EPS loss narrowing 60% to $0.23, a net cash position of $72.2M, and net proceeds of ~$7.2M from the 85 South Street sale. No formal revenue or EBITDA guidance was given; capital spending to stabilization is tracking toward the high end of the $35-55M range, and Flanker Kitchen + Sports Bar and Hidden Boot Saloon openings slipped to late Q1/early Q2 2027 on contractor delays.

Solaris reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $341M (up 55% sequentially) and record adjusted EBITDA of $136M (up 26% sequentially), with Power Solutions revenue of $284M up 79% sequentially and Logistics revenue of $57M. Adjusted pro forma net income was $43M, or $0.45 per diluted share. Management raised Q4 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $165M-$185M from $145M-$180M and Q1 2027 guidance to $220M-$260M from $200M-$240M, and signed a 15-year, 900 MW contract that lifts weighted average contract tenor to ~11 years. Contracted backlog exceeds $16B of revenue (>$1.6B annual run-rate adjusted EBITDA once deployed), though total expected capital through 2029 rose ~$600M and management acknowledged share-price pressure tied to data-center policy concerns, mostly in Texas where it has minimal exposure.

Serve reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.8 million, up over 300% year-over-year and ahead of expectations, and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $12 million from a prior $9-10 million (implying ~$3 million in Q4 and ~4.5x prior-year revenue). Gross loss was $7.6 million at a negative 266% gross margin, but this marked a third consecutive quarter of improvement, with fleet margin up over 100 percentage points sequentially and cost of revenues down 14%. GAAP net loss was $59.2 million (-$0.68/share), non-GAAP net loss $44.6 million (-$0.51/share), with non-GAAP opex down $1.2 million sequentially to $39.2 million and $198 million in cash and marketable securities. Management also launched Serve Physical AI Services and flagged a $20 million reduction in full-year non-GAAP opex expectations versus the start of the year.

Shake Shack reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $423.3M, up 15.2% YoY, with company-operated same-Shack sales growth of 2.5% (0.8% traffic, 1.7% price mix), and adjusted EBITDA of $62.8M, up 16%. Restaurant-level margin was 22.5%, down 30 bps YoY, as food and paper leverage (down 100 bps to 28.3% of sales) was offset by higher labor (25.4%, +50 bps) and other operating expenses (+90 bps) tied to delivery commissions. Guidance was maintained but skewed to the low end: full-year adjusted EBITDA toward the low end of $225M-$235M, G&A toward the low end of the 12%-13% range, and 60-65 company-operated openings; licensed openings now expected at the high end of 40-45. Management flagged a Q4 lap of last year's 1-3-5 value platform and Big Shack launch, plus ~20-50 bps of traffic headwind from new-Shack delivery transfer.

South Bow reported Q3 FY2026 normalized EBITDA of $248 million and DCF of $187 million (up 7% QoQ, aided by a one-time favorable tax adjustment), with management describing results as in line with expectations. Full-year 2026 DCF guidance was raised 4% to ~$690 million while 2026 normalized EBITDA guidance stayed unchanged at ~$1.04 billion. 2027 guidance was introduced: normalized EBITDA of ~$1.07 billion (±2%) and DCF of ~$630 million (±4%), the DCF decline reflecting higher current income taxes versus tax savings in 2026; a $0.50 quarterly dividend was declared and $320 million of notes were repurchased. Leverage stood at 4.3x with net debt ~$4.4 billion, and Prairie Connector remains targeted for mid-2027 FID pending permit durability.

Steven Madden reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $772.6M, up 15.7% YoY, with diluted EPS of $0.79 versus $0.43, up 85%. Gross margin expanded to 44.6% from 43.4% and operating income rose to $78.9M (10.2% of revenue) from $46.3M. Management raised FY2026 guidance to revenue growth of 12-13% (from 11-13%) and EPS of $2.15-$2.20 (from $2.05-$2.15). Kurt Geiger's full-year outlook was trimmed to low double digits from mid-teens as comps normalized to 6%, and Q4 wholesale is guided down 6-7% on shipment timing shifts.

Q3 FY2026 net revenue was $16.2 million, up 38% YoY, with implant unit volume up 34% and gross margin expanding to 78.5% from 76.2%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $68-70 million (44-48% growth) from a prior $67-69 million (42-46%). Net loss narrowed to $7.0 million from $8.7 million, and Adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $5.5 million, with cash of $92.3 million. Q4 is guided for similar gross margins but higher SG&A as a percentage of revenue and moderately increased cash burn.

SINTX reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.2 million, up 953% year-over-year from $208,000, and roughly double the high end of its prior $900,000-$1.1 million guidance, driven by aerospace and industrial technical manufacturing. Gross margin expanded to 62% from 45%, gross profit rose to about $1.4 million from $93,000, opex fell 13% to $3 million, and net loss narrowed 55% to $1.6 million. However, management withdrew visibility on Q4, stating it cannot offer an expectation on delivery of the remaining portion of the $3.2 million in June purchase orders relative to Q4 2026. Cash fell to $2 million from $4.1 million at year-end 2025, with $6.6 million used in operations year-to-date and continued operating losses flagged.

Q3 revenue of $69.2M came in at the upper end of the $65-70M guide but still declined 2.1% YoY, a sharp moderation from -7.8% in Q2. Adjusted gross margin rose ~380 bps to 71.8% (helped by a one-time ~$1M / ~140 bps tariff refund), adjusted EBITDA was $13.4M (19.3% margin, up ~50%), and GAAP operating income of ~$5M marked a second straight positive quarter; consumables returned to growth (+1.2%), equipment fell 9.9%. FY26 revenue guidance was trimmed at the bottom to $281-287M from $280-290M while adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $48-50M from $39-46M. The company also repaid its remaining $103.2M 2026 converts, ending with $112.4M cash; Q4 gross margin is expected to moderate as the tariff benefit laps and opex steps up.

Core FFO was $0.64/share vs $0.60 a year ago (+6.7%), driven by 4.2% same-center NOI growth and accretive acquisitions; other revenues rose 11%. Full-year 2026 core FFO guidance was raised to $2.49-$2.53 from $2.45-$2.52 (+8% at midpoint), and the low end of same-center NOI growth was lifted to 3.5% from 2.75% with the high end unchanged at 4.25%. Occupancy reached 97.3% (+70 bps from June), blended cash rent spreads were 11% on ~560 leases signed over 12 months, and TTM tenant sales were $487/sq ft (+2.5%), with the occupancy cost ratio steady at 9.7%. The board authorized a $0.3125 quarterly dividend, a 7% increase year over year.

NuScale reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $0.3 million versus $8.2 million a year earlier, with management attributing the drop to the absence of RoPower FEED Phase II work in the current quarter. Operating expenses fell to $65 million from $549 million in the prior-year period, and liquidity rose to roughly $1.9 billion from about $916 million. No revenue or margin guidance was issued; management said OpEx should stay fairly constant until an ENTRA1/TVA project ramps, and that margin clarity requires an OEM agreement. The key business development was a first-article manufacturing agreement with Doosan Enerbility, though TVA and RoPower commercial agreements remain unfinalized.

Same-store weighted occupancy reached 88.6% (+200 bps YoY), same-store RevPOR rose 4.6% to $5,413 and resident revenue grew 7.3% to $163.5 million, lifting same-store NOI 15.6% with 230 bps of margin expansion to 31.8%. Normalized FFO was $0.46 per share and Adjusted EBITDA rose 26.2% to $46.8 million, while total SHOP NOI margin of 29.1% was up 240 bps YoY but down 80 bps sequentially on Q3 seasonality. Net leverage rose to 8.1x from 7.8x at June 30, and formal 2027 guidance is deferred to the Q4 call, with management only indicating occupancy and rate growth should be consistent with recent years.

Tecnoglass reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $310.6 million, up 19.2% year-over-year, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $47.7 million from $79.1 million and gross margin contracted to 34.1% from 42.7%. The decline was driven by roughly 580 bps of peso impact (including an $8.4 million non-cash inventory revaluation), a 52% year-over-year rise in aluminum prices, Section 232 tariffs that added about $15.5 million of SG&A, and Colombia's 23% minimum wage increase. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $1.1-$1.14 billion, but adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $210-$220 million, reflecting the $8.4 million non-cash item; management said Q3 was the margin low point and expects sequential gross margin improvement in Q4 toward the high-30s, with 2027 margins better still.

TIC reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $640 million, up 12.5% year-over-year (13.0% constant currency, 8.4% organic), with adjusted EBITDA up 19% to $107 million and margin expanding roughly 90 bps to 16.8%. Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.18, up from $0.14 in Q2, and all three segments grew, led by C&E at +20.3% to a record $223 million and I&M returning to growth at +8.5%. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $2.24-2.27 billion from $2.15-2.25 billion and narrowed adjusted EBITDA to $342-350 million, raising the midpoint to $346 million. GeoVerra, WDI, and Core Group acquisitions were announced adding roughly $90 million annualized revenue; geospatial margins fell 330 bps on project mix and pass-through work despite revenue growth.

Millicom reported Q3 2026 service revenue of $2.1 billion, up 6.1% reported and 5.4% organically (fourth consecutive mid-single-digit organic quarter), with adjusted EBITDA at a record $1.1 billion, up 7.7% organically at a 48% margin despite ~$30 million of severance. Equity free cash flow reached $316 million, up ~30% YoY, bringing nine-month EFCF to ~$870 million and leverage down to 2.53. Full-year guidance was maintained at ~$1.1 billion EFCF and sub-2.5x leverage, though management flagged Q4 margin moderation in Ecuador and continued home subscriber pressure. Key changes versus prior periods include the completed Colombia brand consolidation with a four-year investment plan, an Ecuador brand launch, a Guatemala litigation settlement, and home net losses of 86,000 driven by the Colombia earthquake and the deliberate more-for-more pricing strategy.

Vontier reported Q3 sales of $737 million with ~6% core growth versus a 5% guide, and adjusted operating margin of just over 24%, up 300 bps versus an ~110 bps guide. Full-year revenue guidance midpoint was raised to ~$3.03 billion (~3% core), full-year margin expansion raised to ~180 bps, and adjusted EPS raised to $3.60-$3.64, above the prior high end. Q3 also included ~$4 million of favorable geographic/product mix that management said will not repeat, and Q4 core growth steps down to ~3% with Mobility Technologies flattish. Structural cost savings now track ~$20 million versus $15 million originally, and the company repurchased ~3 million shares for $80 million in the quarter.

Vericel reported Q3 revenue of $85.4 million, up 26% YoY and well above guidance, with MACI at $67.4 million (+21%) and burn care at a record $18 million (+52%). GAAP net income rose 179% to $14.2 million ($0.27 per diluted share), adjusted EBITDA grew 48% to $25.2 million at a 30% margin, and free cash flow was $16 million. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $344-346 million from $330-340 million, the third consecutive raise, with MACI raised to $290-292 million and burn care to approximately $54 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance lifted to approximately 28% from 27%.

Victory Capital reported Q3 revenue of $396.6 million, up 10% YoY and its second highest ever, with adjusted EPS of $1.98 up 21% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 53.5%, up 80 bps YoY and above the 50% long-term guide. Record long-term net inflows of $11.7 billion (13.8% annualized organic growth) and record gross flows of $30.5 billion drove total client assets to a record $355.5 billion, up 3% QoQ and 13% YoY. The 46-47 bps full-year fee rate guidance was reiterated (46.3 bps YTD) despite a Q3 dip to 44.8 bps from annual-fee timing, and the First Eagle deal remains on track to close by end-Q1 2027 with $280 million net expense synergy and 35% accretion targets unchanged. Management said Q3 flow momentum has continued into Q4.

First commercial quarter for TRUTAKNA generated $10.3M in net product revenue on a partial quarter following July 7 accelerated approval, with roughly 700 Patient Start Forms to date; management noted about half of Q3 sales were inventory stocking versus demand. Cost of sales was $3.3M, R&D fell to $41.3M from $56.5M on manufacturing capitalization, SG&A rose to $61.4M from $27.5M on launch investment, and net loss widened to $93.7M ($1.30/share) from $80.3M ($1.26). The company submitted an sBLA for full approval based on ORIGIN 3 final efficacy (76% risk reduction in kidney progression, HR 0.24) targeting a mid-2027 FDA decision, with an EU MAA planned for Q1 2027. Cash was $384M at quarter-end, rising to $459M pro forma after a $75M October draw, with up to $350M remaining under the facility.

Virtu reported Q3 FY2026 Adjusted Net Trading Income of $704 million ($11 million/day), Adjusted EBITDA of $438 million at a 62% margin, and Adjusted EPS of $1.77. Market Making ANTI was $9 million/day, down only about 4% sequentially despite U.S. equity volumes down mid-teens and realized volatility down more than 20%. Trailing-twelve-month ANTI per day of $11.3 million, Adjusted EBITDA of $1.8 billion, and Adjusted EPS of $7.69 were all-time highs. Management maintained the $0.24 quarterly dividend, cited a 23% cash comp ratio and 1.4x debt-to-EBITDA, and did not provide formal forward guidance.

Aurora Networks Q3 FY2026 net sales were $320 million, down 5% YoY, while adjusted EBITDA rose to $57 million (up 5%) and adjusted EPS rose 283% to $0.23, aided by lower variable compensation. Management lowered full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $180-200 million, citing customer amplifier order pushouts into 2027 and a roughly $40 million annual memory chip cost impact, with 2027 specifics deferred. The quarter included large capital returns: a $1.50/share special distribution (~$300 million), 28.9 million shares repurchased (~13% of shares) for $225 million, and a new $100 million buyback authorization. CEO Chuck Treadway also announced he will step down February 1.

VieMed reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $80.7 million, up 12.2% YoY and 3.3% sequentially, with net income of $4.6 million ($0.11 per diluted share) up 32% YoY and about 68% QoQ. Adjusted EBITDA was $17.1 million (21.1% margin), up 6% YoY and 24% sequentially but down from 22.4% a year ago as mix shifted toward lower-margin sales and services. Full-year revenue guidance was raised at the low end to $316-$320 million from $314-$320 million, but Adjusted EBITDA guidance was narrowed to $64-$66 million from $64-$68 million, cutting the top end. Ventilator rental revenue grew 7.4% YoY to $37.5 million and PAP patients rose 37.5% YoY, while free cash flow was only $4 million on AR timing and audit-related collection delays management expects to reverse in Q4.

Vivmark Residential's inaugural quarter reported Q3 Core FFO of $1.03/share, reflecting AVB as accounting acquirer before the Aug 17 merger close and the combined company after it. Full-year same-store revenue guidance was raised 20 bps to 2.2%, and projected gross synergies were lifted to $185M (net $135M) from $175M/$125M, with merger costs cut to $725M from $750M and run-rate accretion rising to ~3% from 2%. Q4 Core FFO guidance is $1.03/share at the midpoint, and 2027 building blocks include ~1% embedded same-store revenue growth, ~$70M incremental development NOI and ~150 bps of development contribution to Core FFO growth. Blended rate change was 3.1% in Q3 (up 150 bps YoY), occupancy just under 96%, and turnover fell 50 bps to 12.7%.

Verisk reported Q3 revenue of $809 million, up 5% GAAP and 7.4% on an organic constant-currency basis, with underwriting up 7.7% and claims up 6.7%. Subscription revenue grew 8.2% OCC (84% of total) while transactional revenue rose 3.2%, which management said was modestly ahead of expectations on data overages and Life Solutions services it does not expect to repeat in Q4. Total adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 90 bps to 56.7%, adjusted EPS rose 14% to $1.96, and GAAP net income fell 3% to $219 million on investment losses and higher interest expense. Full-year guidance was maintained (revenue $3.19-3.24B, EBITDA $1.79-1.83B, adjusted EPS $7.45-7.75) but management said results likely land toward the midpoint of the range.

TransMedics reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $203M, up 41% YoY (organic $194M, up 35%), the highest quarterly revenue in company history, with product revenue of $113M (+29%) and service revenue of $90M (+60%). Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.51 and adjusted operating margin 14.2%. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $764M-$774M from $737M-$757M (26%-28% growth), inclusive of ~$14M from PAD Aviation, while the adjusted operating margin range of 12.5%-14% was maintained and no contribution from ENHANCE Part B or DENOVO is assumed.

VSE reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $541 million, up 91% (about 17% organic), adjusted EBITDA of $107 million up 126%, a record 19.8% adjusted EBITDA margin (up ~310 bps), and adjusted diluted EPS of $2.01 up 49%. Free cash flow was ~$47 million versus $18 million a year ago, and adjusted net leverage fell to 2.3x from 2.4x. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 65%-66.5% from 61%-64% and adjusted EBITDA margin to 18.9%-19.1% from 18.7%-19%. Q4 revenue is guided lower sequentially on seasonality and a tough December 2025 comparison, and 2027 guidance is deferred to the December investor day.

Verastem reported Q3 FY2026 net product revenue of $24.0 million for the AVMAPKI/FAKZYNJA CO-PACK, up 114% year over year but with new patient starts moderating after significant Q2 growth, which management attributed to late-summer seasonality; refills drove the quarter. Adjusted net loss widened to $72.8 million ($0.72 per diluted share) from $39.1 million ($0.53) a year earlier on R&D of $68.8 million and SG&A of $26.5 million. No quantitative revenue or EPS guidance was given; the only stated financial outlook is that SG&A will remain roughly flat in Q4, and cash plus roughly $250 million raised in October is expected to fund operations into the first half of 2028. Development news dominated: the new blister-pack NDA was accepted with priority review (PDUFA February 2027), VS-7375 showed a 50% confirmed ORR in second-line PDAC, and the company plans to start the phase III TARGET-D 301 first-line PDAC trial by year-end 2026.

Subscription revenue rose 7.1% YoY in USD but only 0.2% FX-neutral, GMV grew 12.0% in USD and 4.5% FX-neutral, both decelerating sequentially on Brazil same-store weakness. Non-GAAP operating income grew 27.1% to $12.1 million (19.0% margin, below management's own expectation on higher AI R&D usage), while non-GAAP net income fell to $7.0 million from $10.6 million on mark-to-market losses; free cash flow rose 77.3% to $13.3 million. Q4 guidance calls for negative low-single-digit FX-neutral subscription revenue growth, and the full year is revised to roughly flat FX-neutral subscription revenue from prior expectations, reflecting further Brazil consumption weakening seen in October. Management attributed the revision to volume and macro, not churn, win rates, or pricing, and declined to extrapolate Q4 into 2027.

Viatris reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues of $3.75 billion, described as in line with expectations, with adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.71; North America grew ~7% and Greater China ~10%, while adjusted gross margin came in above expectations at 58%. Management narrowed and raised the midpoint of 2026 guidance across all key metrics (operational growth ~2% revenue, ~6% adjusted EBITDA, ~8% adjusted EPS), excluding Pacira. Offsets included ~$100 million of Q3 supply-constraint impact from Nashik (now OAI with manufacturing suspended) and an expected ~$100 million Q4 hit, while China growth is guided to slow below 10% in Q4 and toward low-to-mid single digits in 2027. The pending Pacira acquisition (tender launched October 30, close expected before end-November) is expected to be immediately accretive in 2027 and add >$1 billion of U.S. innovative medicines revenue.

Total revenue fell 20% to $539 million (down 3% excluding the hardware transition), with recurring revenue up just 1%, software up 3%, and services flat. Adjusted EBITDA was $120 million, down 2%, though margin expanded 410 bps to 22.3% on the hardware mix shift and was essentially flat ex-hardware; non-GAAP EPS rose 7% to $0.32. Management reaffirmed Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow guidance but now expects revenue at the low end of the prior range due to delayed hardware purchases and installation revenue, and flagged continued SMB restaurant pressure with restaurant revenue down 5% ex-hardware and payment sites down 1% to 8,400. The main positive was sales momentum: RCV rose 151% YoY to $440 million (up 54% sequentially) on 10 new VCP contracts, and Aloha Next went live at Bruster's.

WaterBridge reported record produced water volumes of 2.8 MMbpd (up 6% sequentially), record revenue of $240.2 million (up 10% sequentially), and Adjusted EBITDA of $124.2 million (up 7% sequentially) at a roughly 52% margin. Management raised full-year 2026 volume guidance to 2.65-2.75 MMbpd and Adjusted EBITDA to $465-485 million (midpoints up 2% and 4%), the third consecutive raise, while narrowing CapEx to $530-560 million (midpoint down 3%) on timing shifts into 2027. Produced water handling revenue rose to $0.77/bbl from $0.72 a year ago, and the company declared a $0.05 dividend with covenant net leverage of 3.5x against a sub-3x target.

WD reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of -$1.15, driven by a $49M valuation adjustment plus an $8M loss-sharing charge and $7M of REO operating costs tied to accelerated liquidation of legacy GSE loan repurchase assets; adjusted core EPS was $0.92 and adjusted EBITDA $61M. Total transaction volume fell 11% and revenue was $298M, down 12% YoY, as a 58% rise in brokered debt originations was offset by GSE and HUD originations down 55% and 29% and investment sales down 25%. Full-year guidance calls for GAAP diluted EPS of -$0.10 to $0.30, adjusted EBITDA of $260-280M, and adjusted core EPS of $4.00-4.50, implying Q4 core EPS of $0.90-1.40. Management said the GSE fraud investigations are complete with no further buybacks expected, and cost actions initiated in Q4 are expected to improve NOI by roughly $20M annually by mid-2027.

Energy Fuels reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $29.2 million, including $28.7 million and $17.9 million of gross profit (about 63% margin) from uranium, with 320,000 lbs sold at an $88.90/lb realized price versus a ~$34/lb cost. The quarter produced a $52.2 million net loss, or $0.20 per share, driven mainly by $35.3 million of non-cash mark-to-market losses on marketable securities plus $9 million of ASM/VAC transaction costs. Guidance was not raised: the company said it hit the low end of full-year processed-pound guidance, targets the low end of sales guidance (1.5 million lbs), and is only 'hopeful' of reaching the low end of mining guidance after Pinyon Plain grades of 1.04% came in below expectations. Strategic milestones (ASM close, VAC pending, Donald conditional AUD 180 million debt commitment) advanced, but no near-term ASM financial contribution is expected.

Revenue rose 13% to $223 million with PT visits up 8%, adjusted EPS of $0.80 up $0.14, and EBITDA of $28 million up 16%, driven largely by hospital affiliations (revenue share from <5% in Q2 to >13% in Q3) pushing revenue per visit up $5 to $111. Adjusted PT margin expanded 60 bps to 19% despite a ~150 bps drag from self-insured employee health claims, which were $7 million higher year-to-date and $2 million over budget in Q3. Full-year EBITDA guidance of $102-106 million was reaffirmed, not raised, and no 2027 numerical guidance was provided. Management flagged continued elevated benefit costs into Q4 while noting a final CMS rule that follows its IPCI modifier phase-out context as a multi-year tailwind.

US Foods reported Q3 net sales up 2.1% to $10.4 billion on total case volume growth of 1.3%, with adjusted EBITDA up 9.9% to $555 million (margin +38 bps to 5.3%) and adjusted diluted EPS up 17.8% to $1.26. Independent restaurant case growth held at 5% and net new accounts improved to 5.5%, but total volume growth came in below management's expectations as the macro backdrop deteriorated and lower center-of-the-plate inflation cut 100-150 bps from sales. FY2026 guidance was tightened rather than raised (net sales +4-5%, adjusted EBITDA +9-11%, adjusted EPS +18-20%), with Q4 carrying roughly one point of watching-cost headwind and 1-1.5 points of fuel headwind. Management flagged Prime Line ($110 million annual sales), $191 million of Q3 buybacks ($690 million YTD), and AI initiatives now generating over $75 million of adjusted EBITDA, ramping to $110 million next year.

Unusual Machines reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $13.9 million, up 551% year-over-year but down sequentially from $16.7 million in Q2, with a 35.4% gross margin and an adjusted EBITDA loss of roughly $700,000. GAAP net loss was about $25 million ($0.50 per share), driven mainly by $5.5 million in non-cash stock compensation and $18.4 million in unrealized losses on short-term investments. Q4 revenue guidance was maintained at $25 million, matching the target set last quarter, and management said it is nearly fully allocated through Q1 2027. Inventory and prepaid inventory rose to $65.9 million from $42.4 million, and cash stood at $162 million with $98.4 million in short-term investments.

Q3 revenue rose 14% YoY to $284 million with pump shipments up 12% to ~33,000 and gross margin of 57%, up nearly 3 points YoY; U.S. sales grew 9% to $191 million and international hit a record $93 million, up 26%. Adjusted EBITDA reached 6% of sales, the fifth consecutive positive quarter, with operating margin up 8 points and $443 million in cash. Full-year 2026 guidance was maintained at $1.065-1.085 billion with gross margin of 56%-57%, but management said pharmacy adoption is tracking well below earlier plans (10%-12% of the year versus prior assumptions), expects continued sales headwinds into 2027, and framed 2027 growth as mid-to-high single digits versus ~12% consensus. The quarter also included CEO succession, with John Sheridan retiring at end-2026 and Jeannette Bankes named incoming CEO effective November 16.

TPL reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of ~$273 million, up 11% sequentially and 35% YoY, an all-time high, with net income of $167 million ($2.42/diluted share, +38% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of $238 million at an 87% margin, and free cash flow of $170 million (+39% YoY). Oil production of 17.1 Mbbl/d and total production of 42.3 Mboe/d were quarterly records, produced water royalty volumes hit a record 5.5 million bbl/d (+14% sequential, +27% YoY), and SLIM revenue rose 53% sequentially to $36 million. No formal guidance was issued; management flagged a decline in net line-of-sight wells to 16.8 and water sales roughly flat sequentially, but said the Q4 completion schedule is more robust and the next couple of quarters should be stronger. The prior-period change is the third consecutive quarter of record revenue, net income, and free cash flow.

Q3 FY2026 net income was $3.3 million, or $0.12 per share, up from $1.7 million/$0.06, and adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $10.4 million from $5.3 million, but results were heavily aided by $3.9 million of crop insurance proceeds, $2.6 million of pistachio bonus pricing, and an early harvest that pulled wine grape sales forward. Trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA reached $35 million, up 44% from $24.3 million, though management repeatedly flagged that land-sale timing and farming items will not repeat. No formal forward guidance was issued; the CEO instead outlined a multi-part plan to cut costs and CapEx and convert land to recurring income, with details deferred. Shareholder questions centered on negative free cash flow, rising net debt, and the share-price discount to intrinsic value, which management acknowledged while defending the quarter's cash improvement.

Targa reported Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.5B, 6% lower than Q2 as record Permian G&P, NGL transportation (1.17 MMBbl/d) and fractionation (1.26 MMBbl/d) volumes were offset by lower marketing/optimization and LPG exports. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to at least $6B, more than 21% above 2025, and pointed to multiple years of double-digit Permian volume growth. Permian volumes hit a record 7.5 Bcf/d, up 5% sequentially and 14% YoY, with several plants (Copperhead, Yeti, Yeti II, Train 12, Bull Run Extension) starting ahead of schedule and a new Train 14 fractionator announced. Capital returns were reinforced by a $1.25 quarterly dividend (up 25% YoY) and an intended 20% increase to $6/share in 2027, alongside $187M of YTD buybacks.

TripAdvisor reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $436 million, down 11% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $71 million (16% of revenue). Experiences revenue fell 3% with segment EBITDA down 440 bps to 13% of revenue, while Hotels and Other revenue dropped 23% to $152 million and segment EBITDA fell ~650 bps to 22%. Management guided Q4 group revenue to decline in the low teens and group adjusted EBITDA margins to step down to low-to-mid single digits, with Experiences EBITDA roughly break-even. The quarter included a $369 million goodwill impairment in H&O, a global restructuring targeting ~$40 million in group annualized savings, and the announced CEO and CFO departures.

Q3 FY2026 medical-only revenue of $230 million rose 4% YoY and 4% QoQ versus medical-only baselines of $221 million and $222 million, exceeding guidance and outperforming seasonal trends on Georgia and Pennsylvania growth. Gross margin was 64%, up ~1 point YoY and sequentially, adjusted EBITDA was $89 million (39% margin), and operating cash flow was $74 million against $29 million of capex for $45 million free cash flow; net income was only $1 million, or $18 million / $0.09 per share excluding non-recurring items. Q4 revenue guidance is up low single digits sequentially with gross margin comparable to recent quarters but pressured by holiday promotions, and purchase accounting from the Harvest deconsolidation is expected to drive a fourth-quarter net loss; FY2026 operating cash flow is guided to at least $225 million while capex rises to ~$105 million from ~$95 million. Prior framing on 280E is unchanged, with the uncertain tax position covering 2019 to present including $102 million of IRS refunds and interest.

Tronox reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $827 million, up 18% YoY, driven by higher TiO2 volumes (+10%) and prices (+9%), with adjusted EBITDA of $101 million at a 12.2% margin. Adjusted diluted EPS was a loss of $0.34, and net loss attributable to Tronox was $55 million. Q4 guidance calls for adjusted EBITDA of $80–90 million, reflecting $15–20 million of higher raw material costs from the prolonged Middle East conflict, and TiO2 volumes down high-single to low-double digits sequentially. Full-year free cash flow is now expected to be a use of $25–50 million, versus prior expectations, with capex cut by roughly $30 million.

TC Energy reported Q3 FY2026 comparable EBITDA above $3 billion, up 13% YoY, with comparable EPS of $0.94, up 22%, and year-to-date comparable EBITDA of $9 billion, also up 13%. All four segments grew, led by U.S. natural gas pipelines up 17% and Power and Energy Solutions up 35% on 97% Bruce Power availability and a full quarter of Unit 3 contributions. Management raised 2026 comparable EBITDA guidance to $11.8-$12 billion (a $200 million increase) and set 2027 at $12.3-$12.5 billion versus the prior $11.7-$11.9 billion outlook, alongside a new 2031 outlook of 5%-7% annual EBITDA growth, 3%-5% dividend growth, and debt-to-EBITDA exiting 2026 at 4.55x-4.6x. The company announced $3 billion of new projects, bringing sanctioned and pending approval spend to $30 billion, with over $40 billion in origination.

Q3 FY2026 total revenue was $405.6 million, up 11% YoY, with subscription revenue up 14% to $287.9 million and total subscription pets up 6% to 1.145 million. Adjusted operating income hit an all-time high of $47 million (up 15%), subscription AOI was $45.4 million at a 15.8% margin, net income was $9.3 million or $0.21 per share, and free cash flow reached a record $28.5 million. FY2026 revenue guidance was narrowed to $1.59-1.597 billion and total AOI guidance to $179-182 million, with the subscription revenue midpoint rising to 14% YoY growth; Q4 revenue is guided to $407-414 million. Net new pets rose over 28% YoY, retention improved for a seventh consecutive quarter to 98.38%, and the company repurchased roughly $25 million of shares during the quarter.

Q3 FY2026 sales reached $3.1 billion, up 4% YoY and 5% sequentially, with EBITDA up 16% sequentially to $756 million at a 24% margin. Management guided Q4 revenue up close to 10% sequentially with EBITDA margin around 25%, citing higher volumes across most markets and a positive U.S. pricing dynamic from Pipe Logix (+8-9% in Q3, +6% in October). U.S. OCTG demand rose roughly 15% since the start of the conflict and tariffs are now running at $140-150 million per quarter versus the prior $120 million. Free cash flow was $168 million with net cash rising to $3.8 billion, and the company expects further volume growth in Q1 2027 with margins at or above 25%.

Total Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 20% YoY to $50.1 million, with record systems integration revenue up 75% to $16.1 million (32% of revenue vs 22% a year ago) and adjusted EBITDA up 225% to $4.7 million. Gross margin expanded 610 bps to 17.2% and net income swung to $1.1 million ($0.04 per diluted share) from a $1.5 million loss. Management raised the full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $21-$23 million and guided Q4 systems integration revenue above the Q3 level, with growth continuing into 2027. Procurement returned to its $20-$40 million range at $32.4 million (+4%), while facilities management revenue fell 30% YoY to $1.1 million.

10X Genomics reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $150.7 million, up 1% year-over-year, as consumables grew 5% (spatial +16%, single-cell +1%) while total instrument revenue fell 43%. Gross margin expanded to 75% from 67% a year ago on lower inventory write-downs and mix, and the company raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to $625-635 million from $610-630 million. Management also lifted its Atera shipment expectation to ~50 units by year-end from ~40, but guided Q4 gross margin down to the low-to-mid 60s as Atera instrument shipments ramp and flagged lower margins for 2027 amid an instrument-heavy year.

TXRH reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.6 billion, up 9.5% YoY, with same-store sales +4.3% (0.7% traffic) and diluted EPS +8.6% to $1.36; restaurant margin expanded 30 bps to 14.6%. Comps decelerated sharply to 1.0% in September (after 5.9% and 6.8% in July/August) on a social media hoax and softer trends; Q4-to-date comps are +1.5%, with management noting sequential weekly improvement. FY2026 commodity inflation guidance held at ~5% (Q4 improved to ~4.5%), labor narrowed to 3.5%-4%, capex raised to ~$440M, and initial FY2027 guides set at ~4% commodity, ~3% labor, and ~$425M capex.

Unity reported Q3 FY2026 strategic revenue of $597M, up 59% YoY, with Strategic Grow of $432M (+90% YoY) driven by Vector revenue growing 126% YoY and 40% QoQ, roughly double the guided 20% sequential growth. Adjusted EBITDA was $257M at a 41% margin, up 1,800 bps YoY, and the company posted its first GAAP profit since IPO at $122M net income (20% margin), with record free cash flow of $220M and a $2.65B cash balance. Q4 guidance calls for strategic revenue of $683-691M (+65-67% YoY), Grow growth of 105-107% and adjusted EBITDA of $290-295M (42% margin), implying further acceleration from Q3.

Unisys reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $472 million, up 2.5% YoY as reported and 0.6% in constant currency, about $20 million above the prior outlook, with TS&S at $387 million (vs. $370 million expected) and ClearPath at $84 million (vs. ~$80 million expected). Non-GAAP operating margin of 7.2% came in well above the ~4% guided, up 180 bps YoY, and GAAP operating profit was $24 million versus a prior-year loss that included a $55 million goodwill impairment. Full-year revenue guidance was raised for the second time this year to a constant-currency decline of 3% to 1.5% from 5% to 3.5%, while non-GAAP operating margin guidance of 9%-11% and free cash flow of about negative $25 million were reiterated. New business TCV rose 78% YoY and total TCV 43% YoY, but free cash flow was negative $58 million versus positive $20 million a year ago and the GAAP net loss was $201 million on a $151 million non-cash pension settlement charge.

BeOne Medicines reported Q3 FY2026 product revenue of $1.9 billion, a 33% year-over-year increase driven by BRUKINSA sales of $1.4 billion (up 34%) and TEVIMBRA growth of 28%. The company raised its full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to $6.9-$7.0 billion from the prior range of $6.6-$6.8 billion, while narrowing operating expense guidance to $4.9-$5.0 billion. Management highlighted strong commercial execution, broad-based geographic growth, and significant late-stage pipeline progress in both hematology and solid tumors.

Revenue returned to growth at $84.7 million, up 5.3% YoY, but gross margin fell to 34.9% from 37.4% on product mix and higher promotional, tariff and freight costs, and Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $8.1 million from $11 million. GAAP net income rose to $4.4 million ($0.24/diluted share) from $1.7 million ($0.08), helped by $1.9 million of prior-year debt extinguishment and current-quarter insurance recoveries. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed at $335-355 million revenue and $44-48 million Adjusted EBITDA, requiring a substantial Q4 that management ties to retailer holiday replenishment shifted out of Q3, new products and major releases including GTA VI. Retailers bought only to normal seasonal levels in Q3, pushing holiday load-in into Q4, while October watch-through and orders accelerated; inventory rose ~$23.2 million sequentially to $79.8 million and no shares were repurchased after ~$25 million in Q2.

Q3 FY2026 sales were $4.5 billion, down about 2% YoY (up ~2% organically ex-divestitures), with unit volume down ~3% and gross margin down 2 percentage points; segment operating income was $174 million and non-GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.11, which management said was below its prior expectations. Free cash flow was a use of $283 million versus a $181 million use a year ago, and net debt was $6.6 billion. For Q4, management guided to modestly lower global volumes, ~$170 million of raw material headwinds, ~$45 million of higher unabsorbed fixed costs and tax expense of roughly $50 million. Management declined to quantify the newly announced transformation office's financial impact, promising details on the next quarterly call, and said plans assume no volume recovery.

GCI, Liberty Capital's operating business, reported Q3 revenue of $267 million, up 4% YoY, and adjusted OIBDA of $101 million, up 10%, with adjusted OIBDA margin expanding 200 bps to 37.8%. Consumer revenue rose 3% (wireless +4%) and business revenue rose 5%, while broadband subscribers slipped 900 sequentially to 154,500. Management reaffirmed 2026 net capex of approximately $290 million as the peak year, with meaningful declines in 2027-2028, and the Quintillion acquisition is expected to close early and add roughly $50 million of EBITDA. Liberty Capital declared its first quarterly dividend of $0.375 per share (~$15 million/quarter), authorized a $100 million buyback, and retired its 2028 senior notes, pushing nearest maturities to 2030; trailing-twelve-month free cash flow was $37 million, down YoY on higher capex.

Genesis reported Q3 2026 results modestly ahead of internal expectations, but management now expects full-year adjusted EBITDA of roughly $570 million, at or possibly below the low end of original guidance. Offshore volumes were hurt by curtailments at legacy fields, Shenandoah well issues, an early Salamanca turnaround, and a hurricane-related downtime item cited in Q&A; first production from the two Monument wells and both Salamanca wells has slipped into Q1 2027. Onshore and marine came in at or above expectations, with spot marine rates up over 10% and only ~10% of the inland fleet contracted beyond year-end. The distribution was held at $0.20 per unit (up ~21% YoY), no revolver borrowings, ~$41.5 million cash, leverage ~5.03x, and roughly 40% of the 11.24% Series A preferred retired, leaving ~$311 million outstanding.

Genius Sports reported Q3 FY2026 group revenue of $270 million versus guidance of $260 million and adjusted EBITDA of $87 million versus guidance of $85 million, a 32% margin up 12 points year-over-year from 20%. Betting revenue grew 33% and media revenue grew 126%, with gross margin expanding to 34% from 25% and $54 million of free cash flow at 61% conversion. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $1.015-1.035 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $287-297 million, with year-end cash of approximately $260 million and net leverage near two times by year-end 2026. The 2028 targets of 35% adjusted EBITDA margin and over 60% unlevered free cash flow conversion were reaffirmed, and management said the guide does not assume an NFL prediction-market deal.

GEO reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of ~$761.1M (up 12% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of ~$145.3M (up 21%), and adjusted EPS of $0.39 (up from $0.25), the highest quarterly revenue and EBITDA in company history. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $568M-$573M and Q4 adjusted EBITDA to $149M-$154M, with Q4 revenue guided to $777M-$827M. The quarter was driven by new ICE contracts (Big Horn, Rivers, Big Spring adding ~$365M annual revenue) and a reversal of the multi-year decline in electronic monitoring revenue (up 1.6%). The company also completed the $950M sale of the Adelanto complex and expanded its share repurchase authorization by $750M-$1.25B.

Q3 FY2026 attributable production was 605,000 oz, slightly lower quarter-on-quarter, which management attributed to lower grades at Tarkwa and Agnew. Costs were largely flat quarter-on-quarter despite inflation and remain within guidance, with net debt of $981 million ($410 million excluding leases) and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 0.13x. Management expressed high confidence in delivering at the top end of production guidance, citing improved grades expected in Q4 at Gruyere, St. Ives, Agnew, Tarkwa and Salares. Realized gold price was just below $4,300/oz, down 5% quarter-on-quarter, and the five Tarkwa leases expiring in April remain unresolved with no committed government timeframe.

Q3 revenue rose 36% YoY to $361M from $265M, with oncology up 25% to $231M, screening up 180% to $68M on Shield volume of 83,000 tests (+246%), and biopharma/data up 8% to $59M. Non-GAAP gross margin was 67% vs 66%, adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $37M from $46M, and Shield cost per test fell to $330 from $410, ahead of the $350 target. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $1.36-1.37B (38-40% growth) from 36-38%, with screening raised to $233-238M and oncology volume now expected up more than 50%. Free cash flow burn guidance widened to $205-220M from $195-205M on a $10-15M CMS claims timing shift for Guardant360 Liquid CDx.

Gildan reported Q3 FY2026 net sales from continuing operations of $1.47 billion, up 61% YoY on the HanesBrands acquisition but well below guidance of ~$1.65 billion, with adjusted diluted EPS of $1.54 (up 54%). Full-year 2026 guidance was cut sharply: revenue to $5.4-5.5 billion from the low end of $6.0-6.2 billion, adjusted operating margin to ~20% from ~21.8%, and adjusted EPS to $3.70-3.80 from $4.65-4.75; the 2026-2028 outlook was withdrawn. Management attributed the shortfall to softer demand, unfavorable fleece mix, product availability constraints, and lower replenishment, and said soft conditions persist into Q4. Adjusted gross margin of 43.3% benefited from ~$177 million of IEEPA tariff refunds, with underlying margin nearer 37% ex-refunds.

GCI posted Q3 revenue of $267 million, up 4%, and adjusted OIBDA of $101 million, up 10%, with adjusted OIBDA margin expanding 200 bps to 37.8%. Consumer revenue rose 3% on 4% wireless growth, while business revenue grew 5% with gross margin up 30 bps to 78.5%. Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow fell to $37 million as 2026 net CapEx is guided to a peak ~$290 million, with meaningful declines expected in 2027-2028. The company declared a first quarterly dividend of $0.375 per share (~$15 million/quarter), authorized a $100 million buyback, retired the 2028 notes pushing nearest maturity to 2030, and expects Quintillion to close soon adding ~$50 million of EBITDA.

Genmab reported 22% YoY total revenue growth for the first nine months of 2026, with DARZALEX up 19%, EPKINLY sales up 47% to $491 million, TIVDAK up 9% to $131 million, and the remainder of the portfolio up 30%; adjusted operating profit grew 9%. Full-year 2026 guidance was maintained at ~$4.325-4.525 billion revenue (19% growth at midpoint, now expected in the upper part of the range) and adjusted operating profit of $1.065-1.35 billion, with the company guiding operating profit above the midpoint. The key change was three positive phase III readouts announced in October — EPCORE DLBCL-2 (PFS HR 0.49), RAINFOL-02 for Rina-S (PFS HR 0.29 plus OS benefit), and LiGeR-HN1 for petosemtamab (OS HR 0.5 plus ORR) — with prior peak-sales estimates ($3B+ EPKINLY, $2B+ Rina-S, multi-billion petosemtamab, $1B peto in 2029) reaffirmed.

Q3 FY2026 revenue fell to $28 million from $68 million a year earlier on the Q2 decommissioning of U.S. Bitcoin mining and lower average Bitcoin price. Operating loss narrowed to $8 million from $18 million, but the loss from continuing operations widened to $62 million ($0.10 per share) versus $11 million, driven by a $55 million non-cash unrealized loss on capped calls, and adjusted EBITDA swung to negative $27 million from positive $19 million. Management walked back the May goal of signing three leases by year-end, citing Pennsylvania's new GRID executive order and moved permitting/commercial timelines by months, and pushed the Panther Creek/Scrubgrass expansion load-study update from December/January to Q1 2027. Liquidity was roughly $780 million as of November 4, with $380 million of pre-lease capital commitments through 2028 and management stating no external debt or equity is needed before a lease.

Globus Medical reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $763.7 million, down 0.7% as reported and 0.5% constant currency, as base Globus sales grew 3% to $690 million but Nevro fell 25.7% to $73.7 million; non-GAAP EPS rose 4.4% to $1.23 and adjusted gross margin expanded 140 bps to 69.5%. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was cut to $3.09 billion from $3.18-$3.22 billion, while non-GAAP EPS guidance of $4.95-$5.05 was reiterated (24.4%-26.9% growth). Management attributed softness to delayed new product launches (SCRIPT, XLIF Prone), weaker competitive rep recruiting, and a slower-than-expected Nevro recovery, with benefits pushed into 2027. Record free cash flow of $225 million and an added $500 million buyback authorization offset some of the top-line weakness.

Genie reported Q3 FY2026 revenue down 8% YoY to $127.2M, but gross profit rose 37.4% to $41.2M with gross margin expanding to 32.4% from 21.7%. Income from operations jumped 72% to $12.7M and Adjusted EBITDA rose 67% to $13.7M, with diluted EPS of $0.39 versus $0.25 a year earlier. Management said it remains on track to deliver full-year Adjusted EBITDA within its 2026 guidance range, a recovery from what it described as a challenging start to the year. The key change was margin normalization at Genie Retail offsetting a 15% decline in RCEs and 13% decline in meters, with GREW turning positive on Adjusted EBITDA at $1.1M.

Genco reported Q3 2026 net income of $38 million ($0.87 EPS) and adjusted net income of $39.2 million ($0.89 basic), with adjusted EBITDA of $68.1 million, up over 200% YoY, on a TCE rate of $27,539/day (+73% YoY), the highest quarterly TCE since 2022. The company declared a record $1.05/share quarterly dividend, up 31% QoQ and 600% YoY. Management reiterated Q4 guidance for a second consecutive dividend above $1/share, bringing projected full-year dividends to over $3.20/share, with Q4 TCE to date of over $30,000/day on 66% of owned days fixed. The key change is robust sequential and YoY earnings growth driven by Capesize acquisitions and strong freight rates, with operating leverage translating into record shareholder returns.

Q3 2026 revenue was $112.9 million with a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $67.1 million and AFFO of $48.3 million, or $0.22 per share. GNL raised the low end of full-year AFFO per share guidance to $0.83-$0.85 from $0.82 and lifted the low end of gross transaction volume guidance to $750-$800 million, while reaffirming net debt/Adjusted EBITDA of 6.5x-6.9x. Office exposure fell to 23% of straight-line rent from roughly 27% last quarter, and 6.6 million shares were repurchased for $58.5 million in the quarter. Leverage temporarily rose because Modiv closed mid-August, so debt reflects a full quarter while EBITDA includes only a partial quarter.

Genworth reported a Q3 2026 net loss of $41 million and adjusted operating income excluding the closed block of $102 million, with Enact contributing $132 million and the closed block posting a $146 million adjusted operating loss driven by a $111 million pre-tax A/E remeasurement loss. Full-year A/E losses are trending above the prior ~$300 million expectation on lower mortality and higher utilization, and management flagged that the Q4 annual assumption review could be 'materially unfavorable' in aggregate, particularly in LTC. Offsets included Enact's $122 million capital return, a $37 million pre-tax reserve release and a 20% loss ratio, a $500 million buyback authorization, and $80 million of Q3 repurchases, while CareScout match volumes are pacing below the ~7,500 full-year target even as the $25 million services revenue target is retained. CEO Tom McInerney also announced his retirement at year-end, with CFO Jerome Upton succeeding him.

GPGI reported Q3 pro forma adjusted net sales of $509.6 million, up ~5% YoY, adjusted EBITDA of $146.3 million, up ~7%, and 28.7% margins, up ~60 bps, with ~$81 million in adjusted free cash flow. CompoSecure set records at $140.7 million sales (+16%) and $61.2 million EBITDA (+23%) with 43.5% margins, while Husky sales were flat at $368.9 million (+0.5%) and EBITDA fell 0.9% to $88.8 million on 24.1% margins. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance is intact at the high end of the prior range (~$2.03-2.06 billion, +1%), but adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered to $520-550 million (-2% YoY at midpoint) and margins cut ~80 bps due primarily to ~$20 million of delayed Husky cost actions and unfavorable mix.

GPN reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net revenue of $3.18 billion, up over 4% on a constant-currency basis excluding dispositions, with adjusted EPS of $3.58 (+10%) and adjusted operating margin of 42.5%, up 220 bps. All three segments grew: SMB normalized revenue +5% at a 60% contribution margin, Enterprise +8% at 79%, and Platforms +8% at 45%. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed (4-5% normalized revenue growth, ~150 bps margin expansion, EPS $13.60-$13.80), while the Worldpay run-rate expense synergy target was raised to $600 million-$650 million by end-2028. Management declined to discuss reported take-private speculation and deferred a 2027 outlook to the Q4 call.

GigaCloud reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $424 million, up 27% year-over-year (23% organic plus 4% from New Classic), with EPS up 42% to $1.41 and net income of $51 million (36% growth). Total gross margin contracted to 24.9% from 25.6% in Q2, with product gross margin down about 200 bps sequentially on higher logistics costs, 3P competition in Europe, and seasonal discounting, partly offset by service gross margin expansion of 360 bps to 15.3% on favorable ocean freight spreads. Q4 guidance is $425-450 million, with no prior guidance stated in the text for comparison. Europe product revenue grew 46% to $129 million and U.S. product revenue rose 16% to $141 million, while New Classic revenue fell about 30% year-over-year to $14 million amid deliberate portfolio pruning.

Genpact reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.385 billion, up 7.3% year-over-year despite roughly two points of drag from work being transitioned away, with gross margin expanding ~160 bps to 36.9% and adjusted operating margin at 17.7%. Adjusted diluted EPS rose 10.3% to $1.07 and GAAP diluted EPS was $0.89. Advanced Technology Solutions accelerated to 30.3% growth ($405 million, 29% of revenue) from 24.1% in Q2, while Core Business Services was flat at $980 million. Full-year 2026 guidance is at least 7% revenue growth, ATS at least 25%, gross margin raised to 36.9% (~90 bps expansion) and adjusted EPS growth of at least 13%, with 2027 revenue growth expected similar even as the transition-away impact grows modestly.

Liberty Media's Q3 FY2026 was defined by calendar mechanics rather than clean growth: F1 revenue was roughly flat year-to-date despite holding 15 of 23 races (65% of season-based revenue) versus 17 of 24 (71%) last year, and F1 adjusted EBITDA fell 5% with primary revenue down on lower race promotion and media rights (lapping last year's one-time F1 movie revenue). MotoGP revenue and adjusted EBITDA also declined year-to-date on two fewer races, lower contractual media rights, and a net-basis hospitality change with Quint. Management repeatedly steered investors to full-year framing, cited 18 consecutive sold-out F1 events, 5.8 million season-to-date attendance, 16% social growth and record Sepang attendance of 261,000, and touted Las Vegas pacing ahead of 2025; no explicit numerical guidance was given beyond an expected return to a 24-race calendar in 2027 and roughly 200 bps of full-year team-payment leverage improvement. The key change versus prior periods is the rescheduled Bahrain race in Malaysia (bringing expected count to 23) plus the Malone high-vote share conversion reducing his voting power to about 3%, with management flagging ongoing geopolitical contingency planning.

Liberty Media's Q3 2026 results were uneven: F1 year-to-date revenue was roughly flat despite two fewer races (15 vs 17), and F1 adjusted EBITDA fell 5% due to calendar variance and the prior-year one-time F1 movie revenue. MotoGP revenue and adjusted EBITDA also declined year to date on two fewer races, net-basis hospitality accounting, and lower media rights. Management kept its full-year team payments leverage target (~200 bps improvement), expects a return to a 24-race calendar in 2027, and emphasized demand outpacing supply in hospitality and sponsorship. Corporate net leverage was 3.0x, with $2.3B cash and $5.5B debt.

First Advantage reported Q3 revenue of $466M, up 14% YoY, above its stated expectations and long-term growth algorithm. Adjusted EBITDA was $136.5M with 29.3% margin (up 70 bps sequentially), and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.38, up 27% YoY. It raised FY2026 guidance across all metrics, with the low end of the revised ranges exceeding the high end of prior ranges (revenue $1.72-1.745B, adjusted EBITDA $488-498M, adjusted EPS $1.30-1.33). The company also announced the $125M tuck-in acquisition of Data Diver (approximately $20M in annual revenue). Q4 is guided to more modest growth against a year-ago 12% comparable, with base expected neutral to slightly positive.

FIGS reported Q3 net revenue of $190.7 million, up 26% YoY, well ahead of its ~20% outlook, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 410 bps to 16.5% and operating margin up 520 bps to 11.6%. International grew 51% and non-scrubwear 35%, while gross margin contracted 60 bps to 69.3%, still above expectations. Management raised full-year 2026 net revenue growth guidance to ~23.5% from ~20%, adjusted EBITDA margin to ~15.8% from 14.8–15%, and operating margin to ~12% from ~10.8%, with Q4 revenue guided to ~15% growth. The quarter was strong across the board but tempered by Jordan supplier-transition stockouts that persist into Q2 2027 and a mid-60s% gross margin normalization outlook for 2027 versus the tariff-refund-boosted 69.9% in 2026.

Q3 revenue of $323M came in above the high end of guidance, up 13% YoY, with subscription revenue +16%, CCaaS +8%, and AI revenue accelerating to 91% growth (~$45M, 17% of subscription vs 10% a year ago). Non-GAAP EPS was $0.82 vs $0.78, adjusted gross margin slipped to 62% from 63%, and LTM subscription dollar-based retention rose to 109% from 107%. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to a $1.272B midpoint (up $6M), but FY EPS guidance was cut $0.07 to $3.19 on timing of org changes and a higher share count. The company announced a $325M cash acquisition of Level AI (~$20M ARR, +50% YoY, ~11x forward ARR), expected to dilute 2027 adjusted EBITDA margin by ~1 point.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $90.4M, up 8% YoY and 6% sequentially, with $21.8M from Bako and StrataDx acquisitions; GAAP gross margin was 35.3% and non-GAAP gross margin 36.3%, both improving sequentially on better collection rates. GAAP loss was $13.2M (-$0.48/share) and non-GAAP loss $0.09/share, with Adjusted EBITDA of -$7.5M versus -$17.1M in Q2. Full-year revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $330-340M (2.3%-5.4% growth), while non-GAAP operating margin guidance improved to low negative-20% from mid negative-20% and non-GAAP loss per share guidance improved to $1.65-$1.75 from $2.22-$2.35. Precision Diagnostics fell 18% YoY to $41.8M, offset by Anatomic Pathology growing 57% YoY to $40.9M.

Net sales rose 3% with core collectibles up 5% and Europe up 12%; gross margin reached 45%, a five-point improvement YoY, and adjusted EBITDA was $32 million (12% margin). Full-year guidance was reiterated at sales flat to up 3% and adjusted EBITDA of $100-110 million. Offsetting this, Q3 reported POS units fell 4% globally, down 10% in the U.S. and down 13% in D2C, while EMEA POS grew 16%; year-to-date POS remained up 3%. Net debt fell to $155 million from just over $200 million a year earlier.

HIFU revenue was $9.8 million, up 26% YoY, but management said revenue fell short of internal expectations because three anticipated U.S. capital system sales slipped on hospital committee timing. Gross margin expanded 482 bps to 51.4% on better standard cost and higher ASPs, while operating loss widened to $7.8 million from $6.7 million on higher opex; net loss narrowed to $4.5 million ($0.10/share) on a $2.6 million warrant fair-value gain. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was narrowed to $50-52 million (34-39% growth) from $50-54 million, with the three slipped systems now expected to revenue in Q4. U.S. procedure volumes grew 32% YoY versus 15% a year ago, and the install base reached 192 systems.

Q3 FY2026 results were in line with guidance: gross revenue $1.3B (+12% YoY), GRLNF $648M (+10%, +9% organic constant currency), Adjusted EBITDA $310M (+6%, 48% margin), non-GAAP EPS $1.49, and a record $200M Adjusted Free Cash Flow (+42%) that included ~$20M of working capital timing pulled from Q4. Q4 guidance was lowered to GRLNF of $625-640M and Adjusted EBITDA of $285-300M, reflecting $20-25M of travel disruption, ~$6M of FX, and $25-30M from deprecating non-core revenue and deferring European commercial initiatives; full-year Adjusted EBITDA margin is now 45-46% versus 46-47% originally guided, while full-year Adjusted Free Cash Flow guidance of $465-475M was reaffirmed. Management introduced a 2027 framework of mid-to-high single-digit organic GRLNF growth and cited softer restaurant same-store sales and intensified travel disruption as reasons for more deliberate caution. The company repurchased ~4.2M Class A shares for $190M at an average ~$45.62 and announced a new $1B repurchase authorization starting January 1, 2027.

Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS was $0.54 versus $0.23 last year, but consolidated sales fell 10.1% to $338.4M and adjusted EBITDA was only ~$38M excluding $12M of IEEPA tariff refunds — the low end of the preliminary range set on October 16. Management said results were below expectations, driven by a spring supplier disruption and higher costs in Powered Vehicles, upfit operational challenges, softer bike sales, and Marucci weakness ahead of closing. Q4 sales guidance of $287-313M was maintained and FY2026 adjusted EBITDA was narrowed to $143-148M ex-tariff refunds; 2027 guidance and CEO search details were deferred. Marucci was divested for $225M EV, cutting net leverage from 3.7x to ~2.4x.

JFrog reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $179.2M, up 31% YoY and above the high end of guidance, with cloud revenue of $101.5M up 60% YoY and 57% of total revenue. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 22.7% from 18.7%, free cash flow margin reached 37% versus 21%, RPO totaled $812M up 60% YoY, and trailing-four-quarter NRR rose to 124% from 118% YoY. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $680–682M (28% growth at midpoint), lifted baseline cloud growth to 52–54%, and set Q4 revenue guidance of $183–185M with non-GAAP EPS of $0.28–$0.30. A $76M multi-year SaaS agreement with a leading telecom, representing 167% growth in that customer's cloud consumption, anchored the quarter, while on-prem revenue grew only 6% YoY.

FRP reported a net loss of $0.06 per share for the nine months versus a $0.16 profit a year ago, driven by roughly $3M lower interest income, $3M higher G&A post-Altman, $1.5M D.C. multifamily underperformance, and $1M industrial weakness partly offset by $1.3M mining and $2.3M development improvement. Full-year 2026 guidance is approximately $35.8M pro-rata NOI and $15.6M FFO, down from $37.9M NOI in 2025. Management guided to roughly $2.1M of 2027 property costs on new deliveries and a $7.1M total FFO drag, with only about $2.5M offset by leasing and mining, and deferred buybacks citing about $70M of cash against $70M of commitments plus $20.5M OZ tax due in 2027. The quarter's tangible positive was leasing activity of about 127,000 sq ft, the strongest since Q2 2021, though multifamily NOI fell 12%.

FSK reported Q3 2026 net investment income of $0.46 per share, aided by a $25 million ($0.08/share) one-time Belk dividend and a $12 million benefit from KKR's incentive fee waiver. Total investment income rose $4 million quarter-over-quarter to $294 million, but interest income fell $11 million on portfolio shrinkage and non-accruals, and NAV per share slipped to $18.28 from $18.30 on $0.19 of portfolio depreciation. Q4 GAAP NII guidance is 8%-9% of NAV annualized, with management flagging the Belk dividend as non-recurring and offsetting it with an expected ~$17 million JW Aluminum dividend. Non-accruals improved to 6.4% of cost (3.4% fair value) from 7.1% (3.8%), though two new software/IT names (3Pillar, New Era) were added at $142 million cost.

Fortuna produced 69,665 gold equivalent ounces in Q3 FY2026, with adjusted EBITDA of $165 million and adjusted attributable net income of $51.2 million ($0.17 per share), down 47% from the $75.5 million in Q2. A Séguéla stoppage from an artisanal-miner blockade and contractor equipment availability cut production; Séguéla now tracks the low end of its 2026 guidance while annual production guidance of 281,000-305,000 oz GEO is maintained. Cash costs rose to $1,244/GEO from $1,034 and AISC to $2,286/GEO from $2,157, with FY AISC now expected 8-10% above the top end of guidance on diesel, royalties and Argentina macro; share buybacks are paused during the ~$750 million two-year growth program. Free cash flow from ongoing operations was $90.8 million, and net cash fell roughly $160 million to $260 million largely on the $206 million Bambadji acquisition.

Frontdoor reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $655 million, up 6%, with adjusted EBITDA up 5% to $205 million and adjusted EPS up 15% to $1.81. Results exceeded the top end of the revenue outlook and adjusted EBITDA came in above the midpoint despite $9 million of unfavorable weather that drove a 200 bps gross margin decline to 55%. Full-year revenue guidance was raised by $10 million at the midpoint to $2.205-$2.215 billion, with adjusted EBITDA of $590-$600 million, while real estate channel member count expectations were lowered to flat for 2026. The board approved a new three-year $1 billion share repurchase authorization after completing the prior $650 million authorization roughly a year early.

Q3 FY2026 same-park revenue rose 1.4% to $1.17 billion and adjusted EBITDA grew 1.1% to $493.2 million, with margin essentially flat at 42% (down 13 bps) despite weather and smoke headwinds; reported net loss was $366 million (-$3.59/share) on a $688 million non-cash impairment. For Q4, management guided same-park adjusted EBITDA to roughly $140-150 million versus $166.9 million last year, citing October attendance down 9% (weather plus the fatal Georgia incident and related ride closures), but still expects full-year same-park EBITDA to grow. The prior-period picture included 11% YTD EBITDA growth, ~200 bps margin expansion, and $257 million of free cash flow, while the key change versus the prior outlook is the softer October-driven Q4 guidance.

FrontView reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted cash revenue up 4.4% to $17.1 million (5.6% excluding other income), with adjusted cash NOI of $17.4 million and an exiting run-rate of about $17.2 million, reflecting percentage rent and loan-repayment items. Full-year 2026 AFFO guidance was maintained at $1.32-$1.34 per share (~7% growth at midpoint, up from an initial $1.28), implying $0.33 in Q4. Occupancy was 99.4% with only two vacancies and no new watch-list additions; acquisitions totaled 16 properties for $50.6 million at a 7.56% cap rate, and leverage fell to 5.0x, or 4.5x pro forma including the final preferred draw. The quarter was largely in-line with steady guidance; the notable changes were higher cap rates on new acquisitions and the appointment of Pierre Revol as President alongside his CFO role.

Gulfport reported Q3 2026 results where production, capital, and operating costs all landed in line with guidance, with liquids at 13% of total production on the strength of wet gas Utica TILs and EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow both up meaningfully from Q2. Management reaffirmed it remains on track to execute within original 2026 guidance ranges and expects adjusted free cash flow to grow more than 15% over 2025 at $3 gas. The quarter's key strategic changes are a move to a continuous two-rig program in Appalachia with an electric frac fleet contracted from mid-2027, a target to cut D&C cost per foot by more than 20% by 2028, a reduction in SCOOP activity in 2027, and a 33% increase in the buyback authorization to $2 billion. Formal 2027 guidance was deferred to the Q4 call in February.

Green Plains reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $496 million, down 2.5% YoY on the Obion plant sale, but net income jumped to $85 million ($1.03/diluted share) from $12 million ($0.17), and adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to a record $118 million from $53 million.
