The quarter included $65 million of 45Z tax credit value net of discounts and expenses, with the base business contributing $53 million; consolidated ethanol crush margin rose to $0.70 per gallon from $0.30. Management raised its full-year carbon-adjusted EBITDA outlook to roughly $230-$250 million from the ~$188 million expected entering 2026, and set a 2027 target of at least $250 million of carbon-related EBITDA; it also executed a 45Z monetization agreement covering $250-$325 million of gross face value, with ~$140 million of receivables to convert to cash this quarter. Q4 margins are guided below Q3 levels on seasonality, though expected to remain above historical averages.

Reported revenue fell 1.7% YoY to $371M from $377M, but management said sales would have risen high single digits absent IRA-related drug price reductions. Gross profit rose 14% to $85.2M with margin up sequentially to 23%, Adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to $33.9M (9.1% margin), and net income doubled to $19M from $9.6M. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised: revenue to $1.44-1.46B from $1.43-1.45B and Adjusted EBITDA to $136-138M from $129-131M. Prescription volumes rose 10% and residents served grew high single digits to ~218,000.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $556M, up 5% organic/4% reported, with adjusted gross margin of 42% (up ~1pt sequentially from 41%), adjusted EBITDA of $114M (20.5% margin, +8% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $2.44 vs $2.03 last year (+20%). Infusion Systems grew 11% to a record and Consumables grew 5% to a record, while Vital Care fell 10% organic/12% reported on a logistics consolidation that management said was largely a mix issue with no net revenue impact. Full-year guidance now points to the higher end of the prior $415-435M EBITDA and $8.60-9.00 EPS ranges (no change to the ranges themselves), CapEx guidance was cut to $75M from $85M, and net leverage was brought to ~2x after $80M of debt paydown.

Revenue of $70.2 million came in $0.2 million above the guidance midpoint, up 31% year-over-year and 10% sequentially, with core business up ~14% quarter-over-quarter to $40.7 million and Wuxi up ~5% to $29.5 million. Non-GAAP operating loss narrowed to $7.2 million from $11.3 million a year ago, and non-GAAP net loss per share improved $0.02 to $0.05. Q4 guidance of $73-81 million ($77 million midpoint) implies ~33% year-over-year growth, and management said its 2027 revenue outlook is in line with current analyst estimates. Gross margin ticked down sequentially to 41.6% on Wuxi mix pressure, with a modest Q4 uptick expected and blended margins moving to the low 50s after the Wuxi divestiture.

Total revenue of $77.2 million fell 2.4% YoY (-3.2% constant currency), with U.S. sales up 3.8% to $42.2 million on distributor demand and ~250 bps of new-product contribution, offset by a 9% international decline tied to softer European capital spending. Adjusted gross margin contracted to 44.2% from 45.9%, adjusted net loss from continuing operations was $0.4 million versus $1.2 million of income a year ago, and adjusted diluted loss per share was $0.02 versus $0.04 of earnings. Q4 guidance of $65-68 million implies continued international softness, full-year revenue is guided to $298-301 million, and full-year adjusted net loss from continuing operations to $7-8 million. Management announced a $20 million annualized cost savings program and closed the U.S. rental divestiture for up to $24.8 million, but declined to take live Q&A on the new CEO's first call.

Ingredion reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.8 billion, down 1% YoY (up 2% excluding the Pakistan divestiture), with adjusted operating income down 19% to $206 million and adjusted EPS down $0.47 YoY. Management lowered its full-year outlook, now guiding flat net sales, adjusted operating income down mid-teens, and adjusted EPS of $9.25-$9.70, driven by Argo operational headwinds, record-high tapioca costs (up ~65% YoY), a stronger Mexican peso, and softer than expected consumer demand. Cash from operations guidance was cut to $650-$750 million. The Tate & Lyle acquisition remains on track to close in the second half of 2027, with integration planning underway.

Innodata reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $95.6 million, up 53% YoY and 4% QoQ, beating consensus of $83.3 million by 15%. EPS was $0.29 versus $0.17 consensus (a 70% beat), and adjusted EBITDA of $17.7 million exceeded consensus by ~15%. Guidance for 2026 was raised to 42%+ growth from 40%-42%, but the raise was limited by a program termination at the historically largest customer expected to cost ~$12 million in Q4 revenue, which management expects to replace by Q1. The quarter was a clear beat-and-raise despite the Q4 air gap, with strong new program wins across physical AI, RL environments, trust and safety, and federal.

Q3 FY2026 EBITDA came in below consensus, which management attributed primarily to the Brazil online gaming shutdown; the low end of full-year guidance was cut to $109 million. EBITDA margin reached 46%, up roughly 900 bps YoY, aided by divesting the holiday park business, restructuring the pub business, and growing the higher-margin digital segment. Like-for-like revenue rose 9% adjusting for the U.K. tax impact, with interactive segment EBITDA up 20% pre-tax and U.S. GGR up over 30% YoY. Management pushed its multi-year growth targets out by a year, now expecting 2027 only modestly above 2026, and lowered the 2026 free cash flow conversion target from the prior 20%.

INSW reported Q3 net income of $344 million ($6.90 per share), adjusted net income of ~$291 million ($5.84/diluted share), and adjusted EBITDA of $345 million, in line with a solid prior quarter. Blended spot TCEs were $67,700/day versus $29,400/day a year ago, and crude tanker revenue hit a record $321 million including ~$77 million of dual-fuel VLCC profit sharing. For Q4, management has booked more than half of expected revenue days at a blended spot TCE above $172,000/day, more than double the record Q3 rate, and declared a $5.05/share dividend while maintaining an 85% payout commitment.

IonQ reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $173.8 million, up 336% year-over-year, split between $90.3 million in the IonQ Platform segment (+127% YoY) and $83.5 million from SkyWater, which closed at the end of July and contributed two months. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $505-515 million from the prior $450-460 million range, with quantum computing revenue growth now expected above 110% versus 100% previously. Adjusted EBITDA was -$133.6 million, and management called the -$127 million Q4 consensus estimate reasonable while noting an improving trajectory. GAAP net income of $564 million was driven by an $896 million non-cash warrant mark-to-market gain, not operations.

Iovance reported record Q3 FY2026 total revenue of ~$122M, up 80% YoY and 22% sequentially, with AMTAGVI sales of ~$102M (+77% YoY, +12% QoQ) and Proleukin ~$20M. Margin hit an all-time high of ~60% (up from 56% prior quarter), R&D fell ~16% sequentially to ~$49M, and cash of ~$382M supports runway into 2029. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $410M-$420M (issued five weeks earlier) and set no new raise, while highlighting pipeline progress (IOV-LUN-202, POSITILITY, SARATOGA) and an sBLA planned for 2027.

Q3 sales were flat at $430 million and up 1% for the first nine months; European ops grew 4% while U.S. ops fell 7% on roughly $10 million of gift-set shipments delayed into Q4 (excluding which U.S. would have been flat). Q3 gross margin expanded 360 bps to 67.1% (boosted by tariff refunds and mix), operating margin rose to 27.4% from 25.3%, and nine-month net income was $142 million or $4.43 per diluted share versus $4.36. Full-year 2026 sales guidance was raised modestly to about EUR 1.49 billion from EUR 1.48 billion with diluted EPS maintained at $4.85; formal 2027 guidance is due November 18, and management flagged external pressures including geopolitical risk, a weakening euro, and moderating consumer demand.

Clinical-stage business update with no revenue or EPS figures disclosed; the key financial datapoint is cash of EUR 96.8 million at September 30, 2026, with runway guided to end of Q1 2028. The Sobi lacutamab partnership closed, bringing a $75 million upfront plus up to $40 million in near-term Sezary milestones and $465 million in further milestones with tiered double-digit royalties; TELLOMAK-3 is initiated with first patient dosing expected Q1 2027. The PACIFIC-9 monalizumab readout slipped to H1 2027 from prior expectations, which management attributed to event-driven timing and declined to interpret. CFO Frederic Lombard will depart at end of December and a successor search has begun.

Q3 revenue was EUR 8.9M against EUR 17.7M for 9M 2026 versus EUR 11.9M for 9M 2025 (+49% YoY), with gross margin of 47% (up from 46% in Q2). Order intake was EUR 42.2M, led by a EUR 33M LUMI-IQ Halocene contract with CSC, lifting backlog to EUR 102.5M from EUR 69.1M at June end. Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated at EUR 65-75M order intake and EUR 42-47M revenue, structurally Q4-heavy and dependent on acceptance of the first two 150-qubit systems already being installed. Operating loss was EUR 171M, including EUR 13.5M of one-time listing transaction costs and a EUR 127M non-cash share-based listing expense; cash stands at EUR 260M with runway into Q2 2028.

Iron Mountain reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.99 billion, up 13% reported and organic and ahead of prior guidance, with adjusted EBITDA of $748 million (up 13%, 37.6% margin) and AFFO per share of $1.53 (up 16%, $0.06 ahead of the prior projection). Data center revenue rose 34% to $274 million with segment EBITDA margin up 370 bps to 56.3%, ALM revenue grew 43% (38% organic), and Global RIM grew 7%. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to revenue of $7.95-8.02 billion (16% growth at midpoint, nearly $300 million above initial guidance), EBITDA of $2.948-2.978 billion and AFFO of $5.94-6.00 per share, with the board raising the quarterly dividend 15% to $0.993. The raise absorbs a $5-10 million Q4 FX headwind from a stronger dollar, and management guided to 25%+ ALM organic growth and another 20%+ data center year in 2027 on flat memory pricing.

Q3 revenue was $221.6M, up 14.9% YoY with Zio monitor ahead of expectations but Zio AT flat versus prior expectations of growth, and adjusted EBITDA margin hit a record 23.1% (gross margin 74.2%, up 310 bps with ~140 bps from ~$3M one-time tariff refunds). Adjusted EPS was $0.82 versus a $0.06 loss a year ago, though GAAP net loss was $29.9M ($0.90/share) on a $50M IP litigation settlement charge. Management raised FY26 revenue guidance to $890-895M (19-20% growth) and adjusted EBITDA margin to 15.5-16%, incorporating the earlier-closed VitalConnect acquisition (~$16M Q4 revenue, $65M run rate), while pushing the Zio MCT FDA submission to 2027. The key change versus prior periods is the Zio AT slowdown and the shift to VitalConnect as the near-term MCT platform alongside a fresh 2027 framework of ~$1B organic revenue, organic mid-teens growth, and at least 15% adjusted EBITDA margin.

Ironwood reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $133 million with LINZESS U.S. net sales of $325 million, GAAP net income of $60 million and record adjusted EBITDA of $98 million; YTD LINZESS sales of $880 million already exceed full-year 2025. Management raised full-year 2026 LINZESS net sales guidance to $1.2-1.25 billion (up $50 million at the midpoint, >35% YoY growth) as the second raise this year, with total revenue guidance of $485-510 million and adjusted EBITDA above $350 million. The company paid down $60 million of its revolver to $325 million outstanding and expects to end 2026 with under $300 million debt and gross leverage below 1X. STARS-2 site activation remains on track with primary completion estimated October 2028 and NDA submission in 2029.

ITT reported Q3 FY2026 revenue over $1.4 billion, up 44% reported and 8% organically, with orders up 58% (20% organic) at a 1.08x book-to-bill and adjusted EPS of $2.26, up 20%. Adjusted operating margin expanded 140 bps to 21%, aided by 100 bps of CCT margin expansion to a record 22%. Management raised full-year organic revenue guidance to 7%-9% and lifted adjusted EPS to a midpoint of $8.58, a $0.36 increase with the low end of the new range now exceeding the prior high end; free cash flow guidance midpoint was raised to $610 million. SPX FLOW cost synergies now project over $20 million for 2026 versus a $15 million target, an annual run rate above $30 million against an original $80 million multi-year target.

IMAX reported record Q3 revenue of $175M (up 64% YoY), record adjusted EBITDA of $121M at a 69% margin (up ~2,040 bps YoY), and adjusted EPS of $2.21 (up $1.74 YoY), with global box office of $712M nearly double the prior record. Company now expects to significantly exceed its $1.4B 2026 full-year box office guidance and to deliver ~50% adjusted EBITDA margin versus prior mid-40s guidance, while maintaining install guidance of 160-175 systems despite a slower 32 installs in the quarter. Signings reached 105 year-to-date with a pipeline of ~150 potential new and upgraded locations, though 2027 box office guidance was deferred to early next year.

ICF reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $470.5 million, up 1.1% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS up 18.6% to $1.98 and GAAP EPS up 37.5% to $1.76. However, full-year revenue guidance was cut to approximately $1.87 billion, roughly flat versus FY2025, as commercial energy add-on work was paused due to utility affordability pressure, costing about $15 million in Q3 and a similar amount expected in Q4. The non-GAAP EPS midpoint of $7.10 and operating cash flow guidance of $135-150 million were maintained, aided by gross margin expansion of 50 bps to 38.1%, a lower 15% tax rate, and reduced interest expense. Management cited Q4 commercial energy growth of mid-to-high single digits and a second-half exit rate near 4%, but deferred 2027 guidance pending federal budget clarity and resolution of the utility add-on pause.

Grindr reported Q3 FY2026 revenue up 22% YoY to $141 million with Adjusted EBITDA of $62 million (44% margin, down from 47% a year ago on higher capitalized product development last year); app revenue rose 22% to $118 million and advertising 23% to $24 million. GAAP net loss was $7 million, driven by a $33 million one-time U.K. litigation settlement charge and $3 million Freddie transaction costs; excluding those, net income was $21 million and operating income $40 million (28% of revenue). Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to at least $560 million revenue (from ~$540 million) and at least $236 million Adjusted EBITDA (from ~$232 million), and initial 2027 guidance calls for at least $705 million revenue (~26% growth) and at least $275 million Adjusted EBITDA (~39% margin) including the Freddie acquisition and Edge launch. Management flagged moderated ad growth back toward 15%-16% of revenue and the loss of ~$10 million of telehealth direct ad revenue, with Edge ($120/month, ~400,000 early-access registrations in 72 hours) and Freddie integration (expects ~12,000 U.S. patients at year-end) as the 2027 drivers.

IBP reported record Q3 revenue of $808 million, up 4% YoY, but same-branch installation sales rose only 0.3% as a 5% decline in new single-family was offset by 10% commercial and 8% multifamily growth. Adjusted gross margin fell to 32.0%, with roughly 180 bps of the decline tied to aluminum (100 bps), fuel (40 bps), freight (20 bps) and other-segment mix (20 bps); adjusted EBITDA was $128 million (15.9% margin) and adjusted EPS $2.76. Management guided full-year gross margin to the low end of the 32%-34% range and said 2027 could sit at the low end too, with Q4 facing record prior-year comps, continued fuel/freight headwinds, and only partial aluminum recovery. The company completed four acquisitions (~$22 million annual revenue), reaffirmed at least $100 million of acquired annual revenue for the year, and raised the quarterly dividend to $0.39, while leverage stays at 1.3x after a $250 million Term Loan B add-on.

Gold Royalty reported record Q3 FY2026 results with total revenue, land agreement proceeds and interest of $11.5 million (2,689 GEOs), adjusted revenue up over 40% and GEOs up over 50% sequentially, and Adjusted EBITDA of $9 million versus $2.5 million a year ago and up ~60% from Q2. Year-to-date production of 6,366 GEOs is 76% of the midpoint of the 7,500-9,300 GEO full-year guidance, which was reiterated; management said the high end could be reached depending on gold prices. The balance sheet has ~$21 million cash (up from $12 million at the start of the year), no debt, and an undrawn $125 million revolver. A capital return policy is under board consideration, and the 2030 target of 28,000-34,000 GEOs remains in place.

Total revenue for Q3 FY2026 was $26 million, down from $46.3 million in the prior year period, primarily due to the absence of a $7 million Amazon Prime Day event in 2025. The company reported a net loss of $18.7 million and an adjusted EBITDA of -$4.8 million following a workforce reduction that generated one-time restructuring expenses of $7.1 million. Management deferred financial guidance as they integrate the Allen Family Digital transaction and restructuring changes.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 5% to $16.3M, but net income fell to $1.0M ($0.03 diluted) from $1.7M ($0.06), driven by a $1.1M increase in depreciation and higher net interest expense; operating expenses rose 10.4% to $13.9M. Adjusted EBITDA was roughly flat at $7.8M, and G&A held near $4.8M. The GW-Santa Cruz rate case was unanimously approved, adding $2.3M of annual revenue effective December 1, 2026, partly offset by a $0.4M GW-Palo Verde reduction; the larger Palo Verde case is now deferred, with four new rate filings planned for the first half of 2027 and new rates estimated in 2028. Active connections grew 2.4% to 69,797, while Phoenix MSA building permits fell 10% year-to-date.

HALO reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $493 million (+39% YoY) and record royalty revenue of $341 million (+44% YoY), with adjusted EBITDA of $336.2 million (35% growth, 68% margin) and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.39 vs $1.72 prior year. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised: total revenue to $1.86-$1.925 billion (up $20 million at midpoint), royalties to $1.235-$1.255 billion, adjusted EBITDA to $1.24-$1.29 billion, and non-GAAP EPS to $8.75-$9.05 (up $0.08 at midpoint). Royalty growth broadened across DARZALEX (+20% to $153.5 million), VYVGART (+89% to $88.1 million), Phesgo (+23% to $34.3 million), and other royalties (+92% to $65.1 million). Separately, the Dutch Patent Court ruled KEYTRUDA QLEX infringes EP622 and barred Merck from marketing it across eight European markets, while U.S. patent validity rulings have gone against HALO with appeal expected into 2028.

rows.company_name: Hannon Armstrong Sustainable Infrastructure Capital, Inc.
rows.key_quote: HASI reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.82, helped by a fair value gain on the SunStrong Management affiliate; year-to-date adjusted EPS reached $2.34 (up 15%) and adjusted ROE rose to 15.6% from 13.4%. Adjusted recurring net investment income grew 23% YoY to $330 million and managed assets rose 26% to $19 billion, with $2.8 billion of transactions closed YTD at yields above 11%. Management reiterated 2028 guidance of $3.55-$3.65 adjusted EPS and at least 17% ROE, and expects 2026 adjusted EPS in line with the 10% long-term growth target, while taking a $21 million RNG impairment charge (offsetting part of the $35 million SunStrong gain) that moved about 1% of the portfolio to category three.

Health Catalyst reported Q3 revenue of $56.3 million versus a $55-56 million guide and adjusted EBITDA of $779,000 versus a $0-500,000 range, both above the high end. However, adjusted gross margin fell sharply to 44.3% from 52.6% a year ago, with professional services margin at just 1.7%, and Q4 is guided to an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.3-1.8 million as Vitalware's full removal and higher medical claims hit results. Full-year revenue ($246-249M) and EBITDA ($18-18.5M) guidance was reaffirmed, not raised, and bookings are now expected to exceed the high end of the $22-26M target. New CEO Simeon Kohl flagged elevated churn as the top priority, offsetting the modest top-line beat.

Q3 revenue was $246.8M, up 8.5% sequentially, with gross margin of 34.2% (in line with ~34% guidance, up from 33.1%) and EPS of $0.107, above the $0.080-$0.100 guidance range on lower opex. Q4 guidance calls for revenue down 22%-26% sequentially and EPS of $0.045-$0.065, excluding an expected $19-20M after-tax divestiture gain, driven by an abrupt correction in automotive driver IC orders from Chinese-export-exposed panel makers. Management still expects full-year 2026 automotive IC revenue to grow about 10% and guided to double-digit 2027 revenue growth (excluding CPO), while flagging foundry/backend price increases as a gross margin challenge it expects to largely offset.

Holley reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $141.6 million, up 2.3% (core sales +6.7% vs +4.9% in Q2), with gross margin up 73 bps to 44%, adjusted EBITDA up 8.6% to $29.4 million (20.8% margin, +120 bps), and GAAP net income of $7.8 million or $0.06 per share versus a $0.8 million loss a year ago. American Performance returned to growth (+9% core) and leverage fell to 3.5x a quarter early, but Euro & Import declined 12.2% on self-inflicted in-stock and marketing timing issues. Full-year guidance was tightened by cutting the top end only: net sales now $610-$625 million and adjusted EBITDA $127-$132 million, with management citing tariffs, freight, product launch delays, Middle East-driven consumer caution, and a more cautious consumer. The midpoint implies roughly 21% adjusted EBITDA margin, essentially unchanged from prior guidance.

Q3 FY2026 orders were $191 million (up 12% YoY, down 7% QoQ), revenue $171 million (flat QoQ), adjusted EBITDA $38 million (down 3% YoY at a 22.3% margin), and free cash flow was negative $12 million. Product revenue collapsed 69% YoY to $17 million on pushed-out equipment orders, and full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was revised down to $135-$140 million with Q4 roughly flat to slightly below Q3. Management framed the weakness as timing (rig reactivation delays, Middle East disruption, equipment order slippage) and guided to 10-25% YoY growth in key floater activity for 2027, with ~85% of base-case 2027 activity supported by backlog or options. Lower Middle East activity is estimated to cut 2026 order intake by $50-$60 million, partly offset by 16% YoY service order growth and an expanding North American land business.

Reported revenue fell 8.6% to $84.6M on Powering Honest Growth exits and weaker diapers, but organic revenue rose 9.2% to $79.3M; underlying adjusted gross margin hit a record 48.9% (up ~1,160 bps) and underlying adjusted EBITDA was $6.3M at a 7.9% margin, up 300 bps. Net income of $91.3M was almost entirely an $89.4M deferred-tax valuation-allowance release; adjusted net income was $3.1M. FY2026 guidance was raised on all lines: revenue $322-325M (from $319-325M), organic growth 6-7% (from 5-7%), adjusted gross margin 45.5-46.5% (from mid-40s), and adjusted EBITDA $25-26M (from $23-25M). The key negative versus prior periods: total consumption growth moderated to 1% and diaper consumption fell 27%, partly attributed to the Prime Day timing shift.

Hornbeck's Q3 FY2026 was a transitional quarter: as-adjusted (full-quarter combined) revenue was $503 million, Adjusted EBITDA $155 million (31% margin), and adjusted free cash flow $99 million (64% conversion), though as-reported results include only one month of Legacy Helix and $79 million of merger/integration costs plus $41 million of accelerated stock comp. Management issued initial guidance of $90-100 million Adjusted EBITDA for Q4 2026 and $500-550 million for full year 2027, with Q4 and 2027 headwinds from heavy regulatory dry docking (223 days in Q4 vs 50 in Q3; 407 days in Q1 2027 alone). Backlog stood at approximately $1.9 billion at September 30, and the newly announced five-year Shell service agreements (spanning all three segments) were not yet added to backlog. Management highlighted roughly $20 million of implemented annualized cost synergies toward a $30 million three-year target.

HPP reported Q3 FY2026 core FFO of $18.6M ($0.28/diluted share), up ~8% per share YoY, and same-store cash NOI growth of 8.3% to $85.2M, while total revenue fell to $180.9M from $186.6M on asset dispositions. The GAAP net loss widened to $218.1M (-$3.38/share) from $136.5M on non-cash impairments of Skyport Plaza and Hill7 and a loss on the 875/899 Howard sale. Management raised and narrowed full-year core FFO guidance to $1.15-$1.21 from $1.12-$1.20, citing ~$0.01 Q3 outperformance and ~$0.01 from improved Q4 expectations, while excluding Weil Gotshal rent and after dispositions/remove of Fourth & Traction the prior outlook would likely have been maintained. In-service office occupancy rose 310 bps sequentially to 85.6% (fifth straight quarter of gains) and the leasing pipeline stands at 2.1M sq ft with 1.1M in advanced stages.

Horizon reported Q3 FY2026 NII of $0.19/share, up from $0.11 in Q2 but well below $0.32 a year ago, while total investment income fell to $24.1 million from $26.3 million. NAV per share dropped $0.67 to $5.56, driven primarily by write-downs of stressed investments, and the portfolio yield fell to 14.7% from 18.6% in the prior-year quarter. Management emphasized a record backlog of $351 million (up over $42 million QoQ) and declared unchanged monthly distributions of $0.06 for January-March 2027, but declined to give a timeline for credit stabilization and guided to lower Q4 prepayment activity.

HST reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDAre of $347 million, up 8.8% YoY, and adjusted FFO per share of $0.39, up 11.4%. Comparable hotel RevPAR rose 8.8% and total RevPAR 7.3%, with comparable hotel EBITDA margin expanding 90 bps to 25.2%. Management raised full-year 2026 comparable RevPAR guidance to approximately 6.75% and adjusted EBITDAre guidance to $1.865 billion, a $35 million or 2% increase over the prior midpoint, with two-thirds of the raise from Q3 outperformance and one-third from improved Q4 expectations. The company also announced two acquisitions (1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge and Renaissance Dallas at Plano Legacy West) at a blended 10.7x EBITDA multiple and noted 2027 group revenue pace of 6% ahead of the same time last year.

Hertz reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.6 billion, up 5.6%, with global RPD up 5.4% (U.S. RPD up more than 8%), GAAP diluted EPS of $0.20 and adjusted EPS of $0.14. Adjusted corporate EBITDA was $233 million, up $30 million year-over-year and the best quarterly result in three years, but more than $40 million below the low end of guidance. Q4 adjusted EBITDA is guided to negative $50 million to negative $100 million, lower than prior expectations on international softness, lower TSA volumes, and elevated collision/maintenance costs ($15-20 million over plan), and year-end liquidity is now seen at roughly $800 million versus a prior ~$1 billion. Management introduced 2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $500-800 million that excludes any franchise-conversion impact, with fleet and transaction days expected to shrink in Q4 and into 2027.

Q3 revenue was $33 million with average paid members of 630,000, and management acknowledged continued top-line pressure; GAAP net loss was $3.3 million while adjusted EBITDA was $6.1 million. Free cash flow of $3.3 million rose 170% year-over-year and full-year 2026 FCF guidance was raised to $13.5-15.5 million from $12-14 million, though no revenue or EPS guidance was given. New Expensify ARR grew 30% from Q2 and 212% year-over-year to over $13 million, card interchange rose 8% to $5.8 million, and travel bookings rose 40% year-over-year, but management said the crossover point where new-customer growth outpaces Classic attrition likely comes next year. October paid members were 636,000, and the company repurchased 722,121 shares for about $1.3 million.

Evergy reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.58 vs $2.03 a year ago, with adjusted earnings of $610M vs $475M, driven by warmer weather (CDDs 31% above prior year), 4.5% weather-normalized demand growth, and large customer revenues. Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $4.35-$4.50 from $4.14-$4.34, and the long-term 6%-8%+ growth target through 2030 was reaffirmed. Management also announced a 4% dividend increase to $2.89 annualized, three ESA amendments adding ~250 MW, a 1.4 GW Digital Realty LOI, and a planned ~$4B capital investment for that expansion. The key change versus prior periods is the acceleration in large-load contracted demand, with 3.1 GW of tier 1 load supporting 7%-8% annual retail demand growth through 2030.

Q3 revenue was EUR 164.9 million, broadly flat year-on-year (163.9 million), with D&PD down 2.3% to 120.1 million and JEB up 9.4% to 44.8 million; adjusted EBITDA improved to -1.6 million from -15 million. Nine-month revenue fell 13.1% to 465 million and adjusted EBITDA swung to -44.3 million from -16.9 million due to a weak first half and the prior-year Sandoz license. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed (revenue 570-610 million, adjusted EBITDA -105 to -70 million), with management expecting both toward the upper end; Q3 included about 30 million of strategic milestones that will not repeat in Q4. Vertex selected JEB for commercial povetacicept manufacturing, and Horizon cost savings are ahead of plan (>20% delivered).

Cigna reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted revenue of $73.8 billion, adjusted after-tax earnings of $2.1 billion and adjusted EPS of $7.98, led by Evernorth revenue growth of 6% to $63.8 billion and Cigna Healthcare revenue growth of 9% to $11.7 billion. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $30.60 and tightened its MCR range around a maintained 84.2% midpoint while raising the Cigna Healthcare segment earnings guide to at least $4.6 billion. Forward commentary was two-sided: Specialty and Care Services earnings grew 15% to $1.1 billion, but management guided Evernorth to low single-digit earnings growth in 2027, with Pharmacy Benefit Services down single digits on gross rebate compression, lower employer GLP-1 coverage, fewer specialty/biologics launches and the ACA exchange exit (roughly $200 million headwind, or about $0.60 of run-rate EPS).

Q3 net investment income fell to $12.3 million, or $0.25 per share, from $14.2 million, or $0.29, in Q2, on total investment income of $48.3 million (down about 3% from $49.8 million). NAV declined 2.7% to $13.20 per share from $13.57, driven mostly by unrealized mark-to-market decreases and distribution under-earning. Management completed a deleveraging plan, cutting total debt to $897 million from $1.17 billion and net debt-to-equity to 1.3x from 1.52x, with several one-time items (JPMorgan early repayment, JV formation costs, Thrill One exchange) reducing NII by roughly $0.15 per share. Q4 base distribution is unchanged at $0.30, but Q1 2027 base distributions are set at $0.25 per share, 17% lower, reflecting the smaller earning portfolio.

Q3 2026 RevPAR rose 8.3% (above expectations) to an all-time-high $161, with GOP margin of 44.7% (+110 bps) and hotel EBITDA margin of 38.7% (+190 bps); hotel EBITDA was $35 million, adjusted EBITDA $31.9 million, and adjusted FFO $0.46 per share, up 31% YoY. Management raised full-year adjusted FFO per share guidance roughly 28% from an original $1.09 midpoint to $1.38-$1.40, with FY RevPAR growth of 4%-4.5% and adjusted EBITDA of $104.2-$105.3 million. Silicon Valley RevPAR surged 23%, portfolio occupancy hit 83% (highest since 2019), and October RevPAR rose 7.9%, though management guided Q4 RevPAR growth to a more conservative 3.5%-4%. Leverage was 29.3% with approximately $25 million of expected 2026 free cash flow after dividends and capex.

Clean Energy reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $112 million, 66.8 million gallons of RNG distributed (up 9% YoY), Adjusted EBITDA of $27.2 million versus $17.3 million a year ago, and a GAAP net loss of $5.7 million versus a $23.8 million loss in Q3 FY2025. Guidance for 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was raised by $5 million to $75-80 million, driven by improved 45Z values under the DOE's updated GREET model. Results included an $8.3 million catch-up from applying new 45Z values to first-half production plus $5.8 million from third-party producers; management flagged possible one-time Q4 charges tied to organizational changes and will give its 2027 outlook in February.

Cummins reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $9.4B, up 13% YoY, with record EBITDA of $1.8B (18.9% of sales, up ~170 bps ex-items) and record gross margin of 27.7%; net earnings were $1.1B, or $8.25 per diluted share. Revenue came in below management's own expectations, roughly half from a Power Systems supplier constraint (~$200M pushed to Q4) and half from weaker North America pickup truck demand. Full-year guidance was narrowed to the low end: revenue growth of approximately 10% (prior 10%-13%) and EBITDA margin of approximately 18.2% (prior 18%-18.5%), with pickup truck shipment guidance cut to 118,000-122,000 units from 125,000-140,000 and medium-duty truck market forecast lowered. Power generation demand remains exceptionally strong with orders extending into the second half of 2028, and most delayed shipments are expected to recover in Q4.

Q3 revenue of $84.2 million landed in line with the $82.5-$85.5 million guide, while non-GAAP operating income of $8 million (9.5% margin) beat the $3.3-$5.3 million range, aided by roughly $3 million of savings pulled forward from Q4. Full-year revenue guidance was maintained at $339-$342 million and non-GAAP operating income was raised $2.3 million at the midpoint to $35.3-$37.3 million, with roughly $5 million of in-year operating-plan savings versus $3 million previously. Offsets included total ARR down $2.9 million sequentially to $357.6 million, net revenue retention falling to 94.7% from 95.8%, and non-GAAP gross margin down about 110 bps sequentially to 74.5% on AI infrastructure costs. A $50 million buyback was authorized, and CFO/COO Daniel Lentz is departing effective November 13 with Tyler Duncan as interim CFO.

Q3 FY2026 revenue from continuing operations was $534 million versus $605 million in Q3 2025 (down ~12% YoY) but up sequentially from Q2. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $36 million from $31 million, with margin up 160 bps YoY to 6.7%, while commercial revenue fell 16% on contract losses including the largest commercial client rolling off, and government revenue fell to $226 million from $238 million. New business ACV was $61 million versus $70 million in the prior-year quarter, with the $2.9 billion qualified pipeline up modestly from the start of the year. Full-year 2026 guidance ($2.15-2.25 billion revenue, $140-170 million Adjusted EBITDA) was unchanged, and Q3 free cash flow was negative $117 million, attributed to a paused factoring facility.

Canadian Natural reported Q3 2026 total production of ~1.65 million BOE/d, up ~31,000 BOE/d YoY, with thermal in situ at a record ~300,000 bbl/d (+9% YoY) and North American conventional liquids at a record ~358,000 bbl/d (+16% YoY), despite a planned Horizon turnaround. Adjusted funds flow was ~CAD 5.5 billion (CAD 2.68/share), adjusted net earnings CAD 3.4 billion (CAD 1.67/share), and net debt ended at ~CAD 12.1 billion, hitting the CAD 13 billion target ahead of schedule and moving the buyback to 100% of free cash flow. Management guided to a very strong Q4, with the Horizon turnaround completed 7 days early (adding ~23,000 bbl/d in Q4), extended turnaround intervals to three years (+~5,000 bbl/d average capacity), and targeted buybacks of CAD 800 million per month in November and December. No formal financial guidance ranges or comparisons to prior guidance/consensus were provided in the transcript.

Q3 2026 net income fell to $9M ($0.18/diluted share) and adjusted EBITDA to $165M from $126M net income and $324M EBITDA in Q2; excluding Q2's $125M Leer South insurance benefit, EBITDA was $33M lower, partly on a $17M 401(k) profit-sharing accrual. Cash costs were raised for High CV Thermal ($40-$41/ton from $39-$40.50) and PRB ($13.75-$14/ton) on persistent inflation and diesel, while the met range was tightened to $88-$90/ton. Guidance for High CV Thermal pricing implies a Q4 step-up to $62-$63/ton, and management cited 29.4M tons newly contracted through 2031 and weather-delayed high-priced vessels shifting into Q4.

Americold reported Q3 FY2026 same-store warehouse revenue up 4.9% YoY with NOI up 5.5%, handling margin at a record 15.9% (up 230 bps), physical occupancy of 70% (up 460 bps YoY) and economic occupancy of 78.5% (up 210 bps YoY). AFFO of $0.35 per share beat expectations, and management raised FY2026 AFFO guidance to $1.31-$1.33 and same-store NOI to $680-$700 million (about $13 million higher at the midpoint), the second consecutive raise. The $1.3 billion EQT JV closed August 31, repaying $1.15 billion of debt, eliminating 2026-2028 maturities, cutting leverage a full turn to 6.2x and saving nearly $50 million in annual interest, but adding about $0.03 of Q4 dilution and $0.07-$0.08 in 2027. Management characterized demand as stabilizing but not inflecting, guiding Q4 pricing up about 100 bps and warning of Q1 2027 pressure from retail customer rationalizations and seasonality, with AFFO lowest in Q1 and building through the year.

Bob's Discount Furniture reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue of $680 million, a 10% increase year-over-year, driven by 3.8% comparable sales growth and contributions from 11 new store openings. Adjusted EBITDA grew 18% to $75.5 million with an 11.1% margin, though gross margin decreased 30 basis points to 45.7% due to higher fuel and inventory costs. Management maintained full-year guidance for net revenue of $2.6 billion-$2.63 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $255 million-$265 million despite expecting a full-year gross margin decline of 20-30 basis points.

Collegium reported record net product revenue of $216.3 million, up 3% year-over-year, with JORNAY PM up 24% to $51.9 million and AZSTARYS contributing $26.5 million in its first full quarter. Offsetting gains were in the pain portfolio: XTAMPZA fell 9% and NUCYNTA dropped 44% year-over-year, driving adjusted EBITDA down 9% to $121.6 million and non-GAAP EPS to $1.96 from $2.25. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed at $825-855 million product revenue and $445-470 million adjusted EBITDA (essentially flat versus 2025), and management disclosed no signals yet of a Teva generic BELBUCA launch after the January 23, 2027 settlement date.

Compass reported record Q3 revenue of $3.9 billion and record Q3 Adjusted EBITDA of $306 million, above the high end of guidance, with GAAP net income of $62 million (first positive Q3 net income) and record free cash flow of $240 million on $841 million of cash. Organic brokerage transactions fell 0.3% YoY but outperformed the market by 150 bps, while organic GTV rose 7.5%. Cost synergies were actioned ahead of plan at $360 million versus the $330 million target, lifting 2026 realization to about $245 million. However, Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $3.15-3.35 billion, down 4.5% organically at the midpoint, with pending home sales down 15% in October and Q4 cited as tougher than current forecasts contemplate.

ConocoPhillips reported Q3 FY2026 production of 2,302 Mboe/d, adjusted EPS of $3.27 and CFO of $7.2 billion, with $3.1 billion capex yielding roughly $4 billion of free cash flow. The company returned $3.4 billion to shareholders ($2.4 billion buybacks, $1 billion dividends) and announced an 11% increase in the quarterly dividend. Full-year guidance items were unchanged, with Q4 production guided to 2,320-2,360 Mboe/d and 45% CFO return on track; preliminary 2027 calls for modestly lower capex, low single-digit underlying production growth, lower unit costs and continued 45% distributions. Net debt-to-CFO improved to 0.5x and the $5 billion divestment program was completed, though Qatar volumes remain below pre-conflict levels.

Core Scientific reported GAAP colocation revenue of $215 million, up nearly 60% sequentially, with Adjusted EBITDA more than tripling to $134 million from $41 million and EBITDA margin expanding to 57% from 25%. The company expects a double-digit sequential revenue increase in Q4 and reaffirmed its contracted portfolio of ~1.1 GW across CoreWeave and AMD, which it expects to generate $1.8 billion in average annual run-rate revenue and $1.6 billion in NOI once fully delivered. Management did not provide formal EBITDA or SG&A guidance, citing a clean 2027 P&L after exiting Bitcoin mining, but called the low $30 million range a reasonable quarterly SG&A baseline. Liquidity fell roughly $1 billion to $1.7 billion on $540 million of CapEx and $440 million for the Polaris acquisition.

Q3 2026 sales rose 1.9% to $708.6 million, but adjusted EBITDA slipped to $52.8 million from $53.3 million and the GAAP net loss widened to $20.4 million from $7.6 million (adjusted loss $0.11/share vs $0.24 prior year). Management cut full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance by roughly $40 million at the midpoint, citing $30 million of added commodity cost and recovery delays plus $10 million less lean savings ($80 million vs original plan). Material costs ran $15 million higher and wages/inflation $12 million higher in the quarter, partly offset by $13 million in lower gross profit, gross tariffs and duties and $9 million of lean savings. Liquidity exceeded $300 million after an ABL amendment raising capacity to $200 million and extending maturity to 2031.

Chimera reported a GAAP net loss of $193.6 million and a 16.5% decline in book value to $14.82, with economic return of negative 13.98% for the quarter, though EAD of $0.38 per share covered the $1.45 of dividends paid and nine-month EAD of $1.38 exceeded $1.35 of dividends. HomeXpress originated a record $1.12 billion of loans (+27% YoY) but net origination margin was negative 7 bps with EBITDA of only $0.4 million. Management guided to roughly flat HomeXpress profitability in Q4 plus an expected hit to investment portfolio financials from loans held for securitization, with a return to origination profitability expected in Q1 2027. Book value was up about 5% quarter-to-date as rates and spreads tightened, and PRISM 2026-HX1 priced with AAA spreads at 160 bps.

Chord reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted free cash flow of approximately $442 million, with the majority returned to shareholders via buybacks on top of a $1.30/share base dividend; shares outstanding are down ~10.8 million (17%) since the Enerplus combination. Q4 volume guidance was set well above both August expectations and consensus, oil guidance was raised twice in 2026 (159 to 162.5 mboe/d), and management sees holding 162.5 flat into 2027. Capital guidance rose to about $146 million on more operated and non-operated activity plus $20 million of incremental midstream investment, and new marketing savings of $35-$55 million bring total annual savings to roughly $85 million. Prior guidance had not included the Q4 volume raise or the incremental marketing savings.

Q3 2026 production averaged 1.3 BCFE/d, up 8% QoQ and 9% YoY, on oil and gas sales after hedging of $359 million, EBITDAX of $266 million, and cash flow of $208 million ($0.71/share). GAAP profit was $22 million ($0.08/share), but adjusted net income was only $6 million ($0.02/share) excluding a $35 million pre-tax mark-to-market hedge gain. Management announced a $1.65 billion divestiture of 20% Legacy Haynesville / 15% Western Haynesville / 15% Pinnacle interests to SOCAR, which pro forma cuts net debt from $3.4 billion to about $1.7 billion and leverage from 3.2x to 2x, plus a Jerry Jones drilling venture funding 85%/80% of 27 wells. No explicit updated production or capex guidance was given beyond restating 2026 drilling plans and noting Q4 free cash flow.

Cognex reported record Q3 revenue of $313 million, up 19% YoY, with adjusted EPS of $0.53 (+89%) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 35.5% (+1,240 bps). Adjusted gross margin expanded 360 bps to 71.3% on favorable mix, volume, and pricing. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.14-1.16 billion (~16-17% growth) and adjusted EBITDA margin of 31-32% (~1,000 bps expansion), with adjusted EPS of $1.68-1.72 (+67-75%). Q4 guidance was initiated at revenue of $270-290 million (~11% growth) and adjusted EPS of $0.37-0.41 (+44% at midpoint), with the comparison noted as more challenging against a strong Q4 2025.

Q3 revenue was $437 million, down 6% year-over-year due to strategic launch timing and lower tariffs, but exceeding expectations. Adjusted EBITDA of $36 million rose 17% year-over-year, driven by gross margin expansion of approximately 520 basis points to 45.0%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance by approximately $14 million at the midpoint and increased Adjusted EBITDA guidance by $23 million at the midpoint.

B2Gold reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $836 million and adjusted net income of $183 million ($0.14/share), driven by 195,000 ounces of gold sold at an average price of $4,287/oz. Management lowered full-year all-in sustaining cost guidance to a range of $2,230-$2,410/oz (down from the prior midpoint) and free cash flow for the quarter was $48 million. The company remains on track for full-year production targets despite lower Q3 grades at Fekola due to waste stripping.

Bentley Systems reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues of $422 million, a 12.2% year-over-year increase driven by strong subscription growth and asset analytics expansions. The company raised its full-year ARR growth outlook to 12.5%-13.5%, excluding the impact of the recent Cohesive divestiture which reduced Q4 revenue guidance by approximately $12 million. Management highlighted that ARR growth accelerated to 13% YoY, surpassing the high end of the original annual range.

CarGurus reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $258 million, a 12% year-over-year increase at the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA of $89.7 million and a margin of 35%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $1.0115 billion-$1.0165 billion (up 11.5%-12.1% YoY) and provided Q4 guidance of $258.5 million-$263.5 million. The company highlighted strong adoption of new products like StockVantage and VINMax, though it noted that dealer enthusiasm has not yet returned to 2025 levels due to margin pressure.

Q3 revenue of $182 million was within guidance and up slightly year-over-year, while adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 30.7%, outperforming the high end of guidance by 120 basis points. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for flat to 2% revenue growth and a 29%-30% adjusted EBITDA margin, expecting year-end performance toward the lower end of the revenue range due to OEM spending trends. The company highlighted strong free cash flow generation enabling a $74 million share buyback year-to-date against a $90 million target.

Total revenue declined sequentially by 1.8% to $231.2 million and decreased year-over-year, driven primarily by a 19.5% drop in off-net revenues ($76.6M) as the company rotates away from lower-margin acquired Sprint customers. Adjusted EBITDA grew sequentially by $2.8 million to $73.9 million with margins expanding 150 bps to 32%, supported by cost reductions and a shift toward higher-margin on-net services which now comprise 67% of total revenue. Management suspended its dividend program while addressing the maturity of $700 million in 2027 notes, citing a deliberate evaluation process for refinancing options.

Consensus reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $91.0 million, up 3.7% YoY, with corporate revenue at a record $61.4 million (+9.1% YoY) and SoHo at $29.6 million (-6% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA was $47.6 million (52.3% margin, +2.7% YoY) and adjusted EPS was $1.50 (+8.7% YoY). Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $6.00-$6.10 while revenue ($360-364M) and adjusted EBITDA ($188-192M) were narrowed to the above-midpoint/high end of the prior range; Q4 guidance was provided with revenue midpoint of $90.9 million and EPS midpoint of $1.53. Net revenue retention improved to 104.5% from 103.1% last quarter, and free cash flow of $38.6 million was down 13.2% YoY on tax and interest timing but ahead of forecast.

Coeur reported Q3 revenue up 77% YoY and gold production up 45% YoY, largely from the New Afton and Rainy River acquisitions, but the quarter came in lighter than expected on lower realized metals prices (gold -4%, silver -13% QoQ) and operational setbacks. Adjusted EBITDA was $448 million (~46% margin, up 2% from Q2), GAAP net income ~$109 million or $0.11/share, free cash flow ~$240 million, with $111 million of buybacks (46% of FCF). Management kept full-year guidance ranges but now points to the low end of gold, silver and copper production and the upper end of cost guidance, requiring Q4 gold up 29% and silver up 36% QoQ; costs were adjusted lower for capex, taxes, exploration and G&A. Dilution from wet weather at Rainy River and Palmarejo and a New Afton conveyor failure hit the quarter, partly offset by record Rochester crushing and a Wharf rebound.

Cadre reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $202.9 million, up 30% year over year and 10% organically excluding distribution, with net income up 46% and Adjusted EBITDA of $41 million (margin up 110 bps to 20.2%) — both ahead of guidance. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised for the second consecutive quarter to $756-769 million in sales and $140-144 million in Adjusted EBITDA, implying ~18.6% margins and ~$197 million of Q4 revenue. The beat was driven largely by the NGABS EOD R&D program shipping a quarter early, partially offset by lower distribution revenue, while backlog fell ~$29 million sequentially on the NGABS shipment and TYR timing. Management also announced a first-ever $100 million buyback and a small precision-fabrication bolt-on (~$4-5 million revenue).

Celcuity reported Q3 FY2026 with no product revenue recognized since REVTORPYK shipments only began September 30, 2026, and product was not delivered to any treatment location until after quarter-end. Net loss widened to $73.3M ($1.33/share) from $43.8M ($0.92/share) a year ago, with opex up to $77.3M from $42.8M, driven by $25.3M of commercialization-related SG&A. Cash was $642.7M, expected to fund operations through 2029. Early launch metrics: 78% of top 36 strategic accounts ordered, 91% of commercial/Medicare lives covered, and NCCN category 1 context within two weeks; no formal guidance was issued, with a Q4 sales flash report expected mid-January.

Q3 revenue of ~$847M rose ~17% YoY, aided by roughly $20-25M of shipments pulled forward from Q4, with Alani Nu net sales ~$410M (+24%, scans +58%) while brand CELSIUS net sales fell ~6%. Gross margin contracted to 46.8% from 48.1% in Q2 and 51.3% a year ago on higher aluminum and diesel, though adjusted EBITDA rose sequentially to ~$199M (23.4% margin) on SG&A leverage. Management guided Q4 reported growth below the year-to-date pace, citing a ~$25M non-recurring prior-year DSD build, the shipment pull-forward, and higher trade investment, and said commodity-driven gross margin recovery to the low 50s will take longer than previously expected.

Century Aluminum reported Q3 net sales of nearly $1 billion, up $209 million sequentially, with net income of $303 million ($2.89 per share) and adjusted EBITDA of $332 million, driven by record shipments of ~173,500 tons (+33% QoQ) as Mt. Holly and Grundartangi returned to full capacity. Q4 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $275-$300 million implies a $35-$45 million sequential decline due to lower lagged LME ($3,150/ton) and premiums. Cash rose to $755 million against $486 million of debt, with $365 million of quarterly cash flow, and management said Oklahoma financing terms are largely agreed with FID pending.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $94.9M, up 4% YoY on a continuing operations basis, with software up 11% to $48.8M (first double-digit organic software growth in two years) and services down 2% to $46.1M but up 3.5% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA rose 6% to $30.2M at a 31.8% margin, up from 31.5% a year ago and 28.1% in Q2, while adjusted diluted EPS was flat at $0.09 and GAAP net loss from continuing operations narrowed to $3.6M. Full-year revenue growth guidance was narrowed to 2%-3% (from the prior range), with the 29%-31% adjusted EBITDA margin outlook maintained for Q4 and adjusted EPS updated to $0.31-$0.34. Management declined to give 2027 guidance and said the services transition and APAC expansion are 2027 impacts.

CF reported Q3 2026 net earnings of $436 million ($2.87/diluted share), EBITDA of $822 million and adjusted EBITDA of $833 million, with nine-month adjusted EBITDA near $3 billion already above the company's $2.9 billion mid-cycle estimate. Management flagged fall ammonia volumes among the highest in 10 years, Q3 UAN shipments near two million tons (largest this decade), and a constructive global S&D balance into 2027 on roughly 9 million tons of lost Middle East urea supply and over 35% of European ammonia capacity curtailed. Growth projects (Blue Point One, Yazoo City, Donaldsonville CCS) are expected to add $400 million to mid-cycle EBITDA by 2030, lifting it to $3.3 billion, while the company repurchased 3 million shares for ~$367 million in Q3 and returned $1.3 billion over 12 months.

Carlyle reported Q3 FY2026 distributable earnings of $433 million, or $1.12 per share, up 17% year-over-year, driven by a fivefold increase in net realized performance revenues to $100 million. Fee-related earnings were $293 million at a 47% margin, with year-to-date FRE a record $950 million and full-year FRE expected to be the highest in firm history. Inflows were $11 billion in the quarter and $41 billion year-to-date, with at least $20 billion expected in Q4 to bring the full year to about $60 billion, over 10% above last year. Pending fee-earning AUM rose nearly 50% year-over-year to $28 billion, representing more than $230 million of annualized management fees, though management noted full-year FRE growth may fall slightly short of the mid-single-digit target.

CRA reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $214.9 million, up 15.6% year over year and its highest quarterly revenue ever, with record Q3 net income, EPS, and EBITDA; seven practices representing ~95% of revenue grew, and Forensic Services, Life Sciences, and Risk, Investigations & Analytics each posted double-digit growth. Full-year FY2026 constant-currency revenue guidance was raised to $830-840 million from $805-820 million, while non-GAAP EBITDA margin guidance was narrowed to 12.2%-12.8% from 12.0%-13.0%. Consultant headcount rose 6.2% to 1,028, utilization ticked up to 78% from 77%, and project lead flow and new originations each grew more than 20% year over year. The company also announced a 17.5% dividend increase to $0.67 per quarter, its 10th consecutive annual raise.

Ceragon reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $95.5 million, up 11.7% YoY, with non-GAAP operating margin expanding to 8.5% from 6.2% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.07 versus $0.02 a year ago. North America revenue reached $37.8 million on the anticipated rebound at the key Tier 1 carrier plus higher software mix, while India came in at $33.6 million. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance is $365-375 million with non-GAAP gross margin of 33.5%-34.5% and non-GAAP operating margin of 5%-6% at the midpoint, which the CFO said is maintained from prior guidance. The wide revenue range for Q4 was attributed solely to component supply turbulence rather than demand, with cost pressures and supplier delays expected to persist into 2027.

Evolent reported Q3 revenue of $725 million, up 11% sequentially, and Adjusted EBITDA of $34.3 million, up roughly 22% QoQ and slightly above the $4-7 million step-up guided last quarter. MER improved to 93% from 95%, a ~220 bp sequential gain driven by favorable in-year claims development. Full-year revenue guidance of $2.6-2.7 billion was reiterated while Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $130-135 million from $120-135 million; Q4 EBITDA step-up is now $11-16 million versus $7-15 million prior. Management reiterated confidence in a 2027 Adjusted EBITDA midpoint of $150 million or higher but deferred specific 2027 revenue guidance to February, citing Medicaid work-requirement attrition, renewal scope adjustments, and higher AI capex.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $28M, down 6% YoY, with the sequential increase driven largely by a cumulative catch-up on a modified long-term contract; nine-month revenue fell 37% YoY (about 32% ex the prior-year $7.5M BiomEdit non-cash item). Net loss from continuing operations narrowed 44% to $41M and Adjusted EBITDA improved 58% to negative $22M on R&D down 48% and G&A down 32% from restructuring. Full-year 2026 cash burn guidance of $125M-$150M was reaffirmed, but management declined to give revenue guidance or 2027 guidance, deferring to February. Management emphasized new autonomous-lab customers (Novo Nordisk, MIT, Caltech, Maryland, Northwestern, ARPA-H), but revenue is contracting and system revenue is only recognized on installation with a six- to twelve-month lag.

Q3 net revenue of $329M fell 12% (organic roughly flat) and GAAP-adjusted EBITDA of $35.3M dropped 13.1%, but both declines were driven by refranchising and lapping the prior-year $9.3M cyber insurance recovery; excluding that recovery, adjusted EBITDA rose 13% and margin expanded 240 bps. U.S. organic revenue grew 0.9% with U.S. adjusted EBITDA up 18% (ex-cyber) and margin up 320 bps, while international organic revenue fell 5.4% on U.K. weakness. Management raised and narrowed FY net revenue guidance to $1.35-1.4B and lowered CapEx to $40-45M, but held the adjusted EBITDA range at $140-150M despite commodity and fuel inflation. Adjusted EPS of $0.06 improved $0.05 year-over-year.

DTE reported Q3 2026 operating earnings of $481 million, or $2.30 per share, with DTE Electric earnings down $73 million YoY on tax timing, higher rate base and storm costs, partly offset by rate implementation and warmer weather. Management said it remains positioned for the high end of 2026 EPS guidance (6%-8% growth off the 2025 midpoint), supported by RNG tax credits and Vantage earnings above its guidance range. The company announced the ~$3 billion sale of DTE Vantage to J.P. Morgan Asset Management infrastructure investors (expected close H1 2027) and raised its five-year utility capex plan to ~$44 billion, up nearly $10 billion, alongside a 2027 pro forma operating EPS baseline of $7.59-$7.73 and >9% annual EPS CAGR thereafter. Vantage results included a $69 million YoY increase to $110 million on higher RNG and investment tax credits, and a 7% dividend increase was cited for 2027.

Duke Energy reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted and reported EPS of $1.99 versus $1.81 a year ago, with electric utilities up $0.20 on rate cases, riders, higher volumes, and hot summer weather. Management narrowed 2026 EPS guidance to $6.70-$6.80 and expects to finish near the top end, while reaffirming 5%-7% long-term EPS growth through 2030 and top-half delivery beginning in 2028. Q3 load growth of 2% was the strongest quarterly growth since 2022, and 5.2 GW of data centers under construction remain on schedule for late 2027 into 2028, though a Florida large-load tariff was delayed by the PSC and requires refiling and the Smith CT CPCN was denied.

DXP reported record Q3 sales of $587.2 million, up 14.3% YoY, with 8.7% organic growth and $48.8 million from acquisitions. Adjusted EBITDA rose 19% to $67.3 million (11.5% margin), operating income grew 20.1% to $52.5 million (8.9% margin), and diluted EPS increased 25.2% to $1.64 from $1.31. Gross margin fell 70 bps to 30.7% on mix shifts in Service Centers and IPS, partly offset by 108 bps of SG&A leverage. No formal guidance was issued; management cited unchanged priorities (organic growth, margin expansion, DXP Water, acquisitions, cash generation) and noted October average daily sales of $9.03 million versus $9.60 million in September.

Q3 sales of $309 million rose 51% YoY, including ~$67 million of sulfur cost pass-through, and Adjusted EBITDA of $61 million was up over 6% and above the high end of guidance. Management raised FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $208-$212 million (a 4.5% midpoint increase from $195-$207 million), sales to $1.05-$1.07 billion, and Adjusted Free Cash Flow to $50-$60 million, with a $3 million turnaround deferral into early 2027 aiding the raise. Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 19.8% from 28.1%, though management said it would have been ~550 bps higher excluding the sulfur pass-through. Q4 Adjusted EBITDA is guided to $54-$58 million.

Excelerate reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $60 million, up $10 million sequentially, and record adjusted EBITDA of roughly $133 million, up $13 million QoQ on the new Jordan charter and higher LNG/gas/power direct margins. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was narrowed to $495-515 million, maintenance capex lowered to $65-75 million on deferred work, and committed growth capex raised to $400-410 million for the FSRU conversion timing, with total capex broadly unchanged. The company announced an 11-year AxDo LNG supply agreement underpinning a Bahamas LNG Hub ($85-95 million FSU, ~$6 million 2027 EBITDA rising to ~$15 million), extended the Sequoia charter through 2038 adding over $400 million of backlog, and reiterated $250-300 million of incremental EBITDA growth by 2029 from Iraq, Colombia, Caribbean, and reliquefaction projects. Net debt was $871 million at 1.8x trailing leverage with $357 million of cash and a $0.09 quarterly dividend targeting low-double-digit annual growth through 2028.

Ellington Financial reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP net income of $0.31 per share and adjusted distributable earnings of $0.45 per share, exceeding the $0.39 quarterly dividend, with an annualized economic return of 9.4%. Book value per share declined 0.6% to $13.53 after dividends, while net interest margin rose to 3.55% from 3.36% and the investment portfolio grew 4.5% to $4.7 billion. Longbridge's ADE contribution fell to $0.07 from $0.23 in Q2 on narrower origination margins and fewer proprietary reverse securitizations, partially offset by a smaller corporate drag. Management guided to approximately $0.45 per share of quarterly ADE going forward, assuming roughly one proprietary reverse securitization per quarter, and affirmed the $0.13 monthly dividend as appropriate.

Enovis reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $559M, up 2% reported and 5% organic, with Recon +6% organic (extremities +8%, hips/knees +3%, international Recon +8%) and P&R +3% organic. Adjusted gross margin was 60.9% (+60 bps, including $8M tariff refunds), adjusted EBITDA margin 18.5% (+120 bps), and adjusted EPS $0.88, up 17%; free cash flow was $35M in the quarter. Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $2.32-2.35B (~5% organic), while adjusted EBITDA was raised to $428-438M and adjusted EPS to $3.58-3.79, partly offset by a $4M enabling-tech R&D investment and $1M FX headwind in Q4. Management characterized the quarter as in line with August expectations in a choppy market, announced a new $200M buyback authorization, and declined to discuss 2027 beyond prior September commentary.

Revenue hit a record $82.7 million, up 171% year-over-year and 20% sequentially on a 23% sequential rise in cube shipments. Adjusted gross margin improved 18 points sequentially and 58 points year-over-year on a GAAP basis, with Adjusted EBITDA of -$63.8 million (a 27-point sequential improvement), but net income of $125 million was driven by non-cash mark-to-market gains on warrants and debt, not operations. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $300 million to $325 million, with Q4 Adjusted gross margin guided to -25% to -20% (another 19-24 points of improvement), while 2027 guidance was deferred to the Q4 call. Backlog fell sequentially to $765 million (about 3.2 GWh) from $807 million in Q2 because shipments exceeded bookings, though it was up 19% year-over-year and the company cited 3.5 GWh of late-stage opportunity.

EPAM reported Q3 revenue of $1.426 billion, up 2.3% year-over-year (2.5% organic constant currency), beating the high end of guidance; non-GAAP EPS rose 14% to $3.51 and GAAP EPS rose 32.5% to $2.53, with non-GAAP gross margin expanding to 32.8% from 31% and GAAP operating margin up to 12.3% from 10.4%. The company raised its AI-native revenue target for 2026 to at least $650 million from $600 million and lifted full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to $13.23–$13.31, but Q4 revenue guidance of $1.405–$1.420 billion implies roughly -0.2% to 0.9% year-over-year growth (0.5%–1.6% organic CC), a sharp deceleration. Management also flagged that 2027 gross margin may be modestly lower as the Poland R&D tax benefit falls from about $40 million in 2026 to about $20 million in 2027, and that 2027 non-GAAP operating margin is expected in the 15%–16% range versus 16% guidance for Q4. Growth remains concentrated: financial services rose 13.7%, life sciences and healthcare rose 9.9%, while software and high tech fell 6.1% and consumer goods, retail, and travel fell 2.5%, with Americas up only 0.2%.

Q3 2026 GAAP and non-GAAP recurring EPS were both $0.92, down from GAAP $0.99 and non-GAAP $1.19 in Q3 2025. Management attributed the decline to the March 19 FERC decision cutting transmission ROE to 9.57%, the roughly $40 million CL&P storm cost disallowance in PURA's July decision, the absence of water segment earnings after the Aquarion sale, and a higher effective tax rate, partly offset by PBR rate increases. Full-year 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance was narrowed to $4.62-$4.70, lifting the midpoint to $4.66, while the $26.5 billion five-year capital plan was reaffirmed and the 5%-7% long-term growth target through 2028 was reiterated. Management flagged that the FERC ROE refund process, spanning 154 months of load data, will be challenging to complete by the May 2027 deadline, and that GAAP accounting may require recognizing the refund before the D.C. Circuit appeal concludes.

Eton reported Q3 2026 revenue of $57.9 million, up 158% year-over-year, with adjusted gross margin expanding to 80% from 45% and adjusted EBITDA margin at 49% versus 13% a year ago. Non-GAAP net income was $16.5 million ($0.50 diluted) versus $1.5 million ($0.04) in the prior-year period, and the company generated $35 million in operating cash flow, ending with $55.6 million in cash. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to more than $175 million from more than $145 million and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to above 40% from above 35%. The quarter was driven by a full quarter of HEMANGEOL revenue plus growth across all key promoted products, and management highlighted a pipeline of nine programs, including LIBERVANT and ASN-001, with multiple potential launches starting in 2027.

Entravision reported Q3 2026 consolidated revenue of $226.3 million, up 88% YoY, with operating income of $28.3 million versus a $9.1 million loss a year ago, driven by ATS revenue up 133% to $177.2 million and ATS operating profit up 261% to $35.2 million. However, ATS revenue fell 3% sequentially and ATS operating profit fell 12% QoQ on newly onboarded staff and temporary multi-cloud migration costs, while media revenue rose 10% to $49.1 million on $6 million of political ads and swung to a $0.1 million profit from a $3.5 million loss. Management reaffirmed Q4 ATS revenue growth of more than 100% YoY, extended the Univision affiliation to March 31, 2027 while exploring strategic alternatives for the TV business without Univision, and agreed to watch Tampa TV stations for $30 million. 2026 political revenue of approximately $25 million came in at the low end of the internal range, well below $34 million in 2024 and $32 million in 2022.

Q3 revenue of $151.4 million grew 2.7% YoY but came in just below the low end of guidance, while adjusted EBITDA of $45 million met the midpoint at a 29.7% margin versus 31.5% a year ago. Full-year 2026 guidance was set at approximately $600 million revenue and $170 million adjusted EBITDA, incorporating flat vendor rebates, top-of-funnel lead generation pressure, healthcare claims costs, and incremental Q4 paid-media investment. NRR slipped to 93.3% on declining third-party partner revenue, though payments in the top six solutions grew 15-16% and multi-solution customer counts rose 27%. New CEO Alex Goor disclosed decelerating revenue supported mainly by price actions and flagged that growth investments could weigh on near-term results.

Eve Holding reported a Q3 FY2026 net loss of $58 million and R&D of $48 million, with SG&A down to $6 million from $7 million a year ago. Cash burn for the first nine months was $174 million, tracking toward the low end of the $225-275 million full-year guidance, and management said $356 million in cash plus $114 million in undrawn credit supports operations through 2028. Development milestones advanced, with 170 of 185 engineering test points (91%) validated and a first full transition flight targeted before year-end; no financial guidance was raised, but capex and burn guidance were tightened favorably. The commercial backlog stayed roughly flat at about 2,500 aircraft ($12.6 billion list) with a new 12-aircraft FlyBIS agreement (2 firm, 10 options).

DNOW reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.34 billion, up $30 million or 2.3% sequentially and within the guided range, with adjusted gross margin up 40 bps sequentially to 21.2% and adjusted EBITDA of $76 million (5.7% of revenue), up $16 million sequentially. Adjusted EPS was $0.18 and GAAP EPS $0.14; cash from operations was $120 million, the best third quarter since 2015, bringing year-to-date CFO to $158 million with full-year now expected to approach $200 million. Q4 revenue is guided down high single digits sequentially with EBITDA targeted at 4.5%, and management framed 2027 EBITDA scenarios of $300 million to $350 million off the annualized Q3 figure. International growth was muted by about $15 million of project delays pushed into future periods, and rising inbound and outbound freight costs pressured margins.

Diodes reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $532.6M, up 35.8% YoY and 19.5% QoQ, exceeding the midpoint of guidance, with GAAP gross margin of 36.1% (up 540 bps YoY from 30.7%) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.18 versus $0.37 a year ago and $0.70 last quarter. Q4 guidance calls for revenue of ~$550M (±3%), a 3.2% sequential increase versus typical 5%-6% Q4 seasonal decline, non-GAAP gross margin of 37% (±1%), and non-GAAP EPS of $1.35 (±$0.10). Automotive revenue rose ~60% YoY to a record and industrial rose 50% YoY, while computing rose 33% YoY; management said full-year revenue would grow ~30% and noted its three-year targets are now out of date and will be revisited next quarter.

Cronos reported record Q3 FY2026 net revenue of $63.5 million, up 75% year-over-year, with gross profit of $32.3 million (up 76%) and record Adjusted EBITDA of $17.1 million, an $11.4 million year-over-year improvement. Israel grew 33% year-over-year (19% constant currency), Canada retail sales grew 41% versus 1% industry growth, and other international markets rose 7x to $13.2 million on German demand. Operating expenses rose 23% while OPEX fell to 37% of revenue from 52%, and cash and investments reached $841 million, up $14 million sequentially. Management gave no numeric forward guidance, citing Q4 Canadian provincial purchasing softness and lumpy international export timing, and closed the CanAdelaar acquisition in the Netherlands at under 3x trailing Adjusted EBITDA.

Q3 FY2026 GMV grew 4% to $92.6 million (above guidance midpoint), revenue rose 5% to $23.1 million (above high end), and adjusted EBITDA margin hit 4.5%, up 560 bps YoY and above the high end. Orders returned to growth at +1%, the first YoY increase since Q4 2024, but active buyers fell 8% YoY to about 58,200 and sellers declined 3% to about 5,600. Q4 guidance calls for GMV of -1% to +5% and revenue of -3% to +2%, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 1%-4%, reflecting lower take rates from reduced commissions on ~7% of GMV (jewelry, watches, handbags) plus a low-single-digit AOV decline. The call also announced Bradford Shellhammer succeeding David Rosenblatt as CEO effective January 1, 2027, and an additional $5 million buyback authorization.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $367 million, up 6% YoY and $17 million above the high end of the $320-350 million guide; non-GAAP EPS was $0.13 versus $0.06 a year ago and adjusted EBITDA rose 38% to $22.4 million, both above the high end of guidance. Memory revenue hit a Q3 record of $167.3 million, up 43%, while peripherals grew only 3% to $116.5 million due to $6-8 million of logistics and hub-transition timing that pushed revenue into Q4. Full-year guidance was raised: revenue midpoint up $36 million to $1.456-1.486 billion and adjusted EBITDA midpoint up $3 million to $127-131 million. Q4 revenue is guided to $420-450 million, but Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $38-42 million is expected below last year as memory gross margin normalizes to 18-20% from an unusually high ~35% in the prior-year quarter.

Pre-revenue clinical-stage quarter: Q3 2026 R&D expense rose to $17.8 million from $8.5 million a year earlier on soquelitinib trial costs, and net loss widened to $20.3 million from $10.2 million. Cash and marketable securities totaled $202.9 million at September 30, 2026 (including ~$189.4 million of Q1 follow-on net proceeds), with runway guided into Q2 2028. Management said the Phase III PTCL trial is on track with an event-driven futility analysis due Q1 2027, SIERRA1 atopic dermatitis top-line data are anticipated Q3 2027, and the Angel China cohort one data moved to March 2027 (about a quarter later, attributed to requiring 12 weeks of dosing plus 30-day follow-up while remaining blinded). The HS Phase I-B trial is ahead of its enrollment plan with data possibly in H1 2027, and the asthma trial start shifted from late December to Q1 2027, which management called immaterial.

Castle Biosciences reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $102.9 million, up 24% YoY, driven by TissueCypher test report volume growth of 47% to 15,574 reports. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $385-395 million from $365-375 million, a $20 million increase at the midpoint, primarily on anticipated TissueCypher volume growth and, to a lesser extent, ASP improvement. GAAP net loss widened to $4.1 million ($0.13 diluted loss per share) from $0.5 million a year ago, though Adjusted EBITDA rose to $12.7 million from $9.2 million. Management reiterated full-year TissueCypher volume growth of 50%-52% and refined DecisionDx-Melanoma growth to mid-single-digit; positive Adjusted EBITDA is still expected for Q4, FY2026 and FY2027.

Q3 revenue fell 2.4% to $100.3M as cemetery comparable revenue dropped 7.8% to $32.5M, offsetting funeral comparable revenue growth of 3.6%. Adjusted EBITDA fell 16% to $27.7M (27.6% margin vs 32.1%) and adjusted diluted EPS came in at $0.59 vs $0.75, partly due to trust taxes; excluding those, EPS would have been $0.70. Management cut full-year guidance: revenue to $415-420M from $435-445M, adjusted EBITDA to $125-130M from $135-140M, and adjusted EPS to $2.90-3.05 from $3.35-3.55. Cemetery preneed weakness (concentrated in California) is the largest driver of the reduction, partially offset by a return to positive funeral contract growth (+2.3% same-store) and a pipeline of five pending acquisitions representing over $14M in annual revenue.

CytomX reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.7 million versus $6 million in Q3 2025, with the decline attributed to the conclusion of the Astellas collaboration; operating expenses rose to $25.2 million from $21.7 million. Cash and investments were $348 million at September 30 versus $330 million at June 30, including $37 million received from Regeneron for two additional targets, with runway projected into H2 2028. Management did not provide a revenue or EPS guide; the key forward item is the Varseta-M update moved from year-end 2026 to January, when the company expects a first look at overall survival plus an integrated Phase 1 update and potential registrational strategy, with a first registrational study targeted for H1 2027. No new clinical data was disclosed on the call; initiation of the bevacizumab/5-FU/leucovorin Phase I/II study remains on track for year-end.

Centuri reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.2 billion, up 40% YoY, with gross margin of 9.5% (vs 7.2% in Q2), adjusted net income of $42 million ($0.42/share) versus $17 million ($0.19) a year ago, and Adjusted EBITDA of $108 million, up 44%. Full-year 2026 guidance was updated to revenue of $3.8-3.9 billion, Adjusted EBITDA of $290-300 million, and adjusted net income of $80-90 million, assuming no Q4 storm work, though free cash flow guidance was cut to $25-50 million on higher working capital. Management introduced a 2027 outlook of mid-teens revenue growth to above $4.4 billion with gross margin of 8.5%-9%, and noted the preliminary 2027 view outpaces the 2029 targets set earlier this year. Outstanding bids more than doubled to $4.8 billion and the opportunity pipeline rose 46% to $19 billion, while backlog grew 5% to roughly $6.2 billion.

CVRx reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $13.8 million, down 6.1% YoY and within guidance, with U.S. revenue down 4% to $13 million and Europe down 27% to $0.9 million; gross margin held at 87% and net loss widened to $14.2 million ($0.52/share) from $12.9 million ($0.49). Full-year guidance was cut to $56-57 million from a prior $58-60 million, and Q4 is guided to $11.7-12.7 million, reflecting continued degradation at the largest Medicare Advantage payer (30-day approval rate down to ~12% from 83% in 2025), physician champion turnover, and slower recovery in four less-tenured regions. Operating expenses were held at $99-101 million via cost actions including severance, cash stood at $58.7 million with at least 18 months of stated runway, and $6 million was raised through the ATM. Two written Medicare Advantage coverage policies (21% of MA lives) and a raised national inpatient rate to $45,000 were cited as offsets.

Curtiss-Wright reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $953M (+10% YoY), operating margin of 19.9% (+30 bps), and diluted EPS of $3.94 (+16%), slightly ahead of expectations, with free cash flow near $160M (108% conversion). Orders rose 15% for a 1.1x book-to-bill and backlog reached a record ~$4.6B, up 12% YTD. Management raised full-year guidance across all major metrics: sales growth to 8%-10%, record operating margin of 19.2%-19.4%, EPS of $15.40-$15.50 (+16%-18%), and FCF raised $10M to $595M-$615M. Defense Electronics sales grew only 2% with margin down YoY on unfavorable mix, while Aerospace & Industrial (+14%) and Naval & Power (+12%, +200 bps margin) led growth.

Q3 sales were $497M, up 12% YoY, but organic growth was only 1%; adjusted EBITDA rose 4% to $127M with margin down 190 bps to 25.6% on Antares Vision dilution, and adjusted EPS was flat at $1.28. SAT grew organically 7% with margin up 60 bps to 29.2% and backlog up 8% to ~$482M, while DTT organic sales fell 5% and margin contracted 430 bps. Management raised the midpoint and narrowed FY adjusted EPS guidance to $4.32-$4.42, but lowered DTT on CPI hardware/retail pushouts and slower life sciences project conversion at Antares.
