Adjusted free cash flow was $98M, up 15%, with ~132% conversion.

CoreCivic reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $0.49 vs $0.24 a year ago (+104%), normalized FFO per share of $0.75 vs $0.48 (+56%), and adjusted EBITDA of $117.8 million vs $88.8 million (+33%), beating consensus by $0.06 on adjusted EPS and $2.7 million on EBITDA. Residential occupancy rose to 84% from 76.7%, the highest since the pandemic, with federal partner revenue up 22.2% and ICE revenue up $75.2 million (+34.8%). Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $1.74-$1.80 from $1.64-$1.73 and adjusted EBITDA to $442.5-$445.5 million from $434.5-$439.5 million. The quarter was dominated by the $2.2 billion gross sale of four facilities to DHS ($1.6 billion net), over $700 million of debt repayment, and a $500 million accelerated share repurchase plus a $500 million authorization increase.

Cryoport reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $50.2 million, up 14% YoY, with Life Sciences Services up 18% and commercial cell and gene therapy client revenue up 20%; products grew 8%. Adjusted EBITDA was positive $1.1 million, a $1.8 million YoY improvement and the second consecutive positive quarter. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $197-199 million, implying ~12% growth and Q4 of roughly $50-52 million, though management called the range prudent and excluded new approvals from the outlook. The clinical pipeline reached a record 788 trials (99 in Phase III), but four expected 2026 application filings slipped into 2027 and the filing outlook was trimmed versus Q2 commentary.

Dropbox reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $637.3M, up 0.5% YoY (1% ex-FormSwift, vs guidance implying roughly flat), with operating margin of 42.2% versus guidance of ~38.5%. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.88 versus $0.74 a year ago, and the company raised FY2026 revenue midpoint by $12M to $2.528-2.531B and operating margin guidance to 40.5%. Q4 revenue guidance of $630-633M implies only 0.2% YoY growth ex-FormSwift, and the early 2027 view is roughly flat revenue with ~150 bps of margin expansion; management also announced a ~9% workforce reduction and the planned acquisition of Tigris Data.

Ducommun reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $227M, up 6% YoY, a record, with commercial aerospace up 28% to $97M offsetting a 7% decline in military and space to $119M. Gross margin set a record at 28.9% (up 140 bps from 27.5%), while adjusted operating margin slipped to 12.3% from 12.7% on stock-based comp timing and adjusted EPS was $1.21 versus $1.22. Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $885-890M from $880-890M, essentially intact, with no EPS guide. Bookings were a record $354M at 1.6 book-to-bill and defense RPO hit a record $1.3B, though missile framework order conversion is not expected until late Q1/Q2 2027.

Revenue rose 10.9% YoY to $99.3M on an adjusted basis, with all four strategic markets growing nearly 30% collectively; non-GAAP gross margin expanded 420 bps to 35.5% and Adjusted EBITDA improved $13.1M YoY to +$3.1M. Non-GAAP diluted loss per share was $0.06, a $0.02 improvement. Q4 guidance is revenue of $100-103M with Adjusted EBITDA of -$2M to break-even, reflecting customer order timing variability and less year-end concentration. The company launched an ATM equity program and plans to exchange its 2030 secured notes for new unsecured notes due 2031.

Diversified reported Q3 FY2026 production of ~1.2 BCFE/d, commodity revenue of $470 million (~$4.29/Mcfe), adjusted EBITDA of $256 million at a 56% margin, and adjusted free cash flow of $153 million. Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated at ~$1 billion adjusted EBITDA and ~$440 million adjusted free cash flow, excluding the Birch acquisition expected to close before year-end. Year-to-date the company repaid ~$313 million of debt principal and returned ~$157 million to shareholders, and the credit facility was upsized to $1 billion after quarter-end. The quarter was in-line with no guidance change, with the main swing factor being the pending Birch deal (pro forma production +~35%, EBITDA +~55%).

Revenue was $3 million, up 286% YoY, including a one-time $0.5 million defense contribution; GAAP operating loss was $50.4 million and non-GAAP operating loss $41.6 million. Q3 free cash flow was -$38 million, better than the low end of guidance, and full-year 2026 FCF burn guidance was improved to -$153M to -$155M from -$155M to -$162M. Q4 deployment count is guided to the mid-40s from 37 delivered at quarter end, with no formal 2027 revenue or FCF guidance; management reiterated 200 trucks and over $50M annualized run-rate revenue exiting 2027 and 5,000 trucks with over $1B run-rate and FCF breakeven exiting 2029. The key change is commercial — a 75-truck definitive DaaS agreement with DTL Transport, IKEA as first unsupervised launch partner, and a third OEM platform (International LT) — while the core P&L remains deeply loss-making at roughly $3M quarterly revenue.

Cable One reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues of $332.2 million, a decrease of approximately $44 million year-over-year compared to $376 million in the prior year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $159.8 million from $201.9 million, driven by declines in residential data and video revenues alongside lower advertising sales due to a third-party transition. While net subscriber losses narrowed significantly to approximately 7,500 (best in seven quarters), the company explicitly acknowledged that ARPU declined $2 sequentially and business services revenue was impacted by divested assets.

Q3 revenue was $927M, down 0.8% YoY but within the flat-to-down-2% guidance, while underlying revenue grew 2.3% versus the 1%-2% guide; adjusted EBITDA rose 29% to $21.3M and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps to 2.3%, at the top of the range. Adjusted EPS fell to $0.07 from $0.17 on discrete tax items, and Education revenue declined 6.4%, below expectations on K-12 enrollment pressure. Management guided Q4 revenue to flat to up 1% (including a ~3-point extra fiscal week) with 180-200 bps of EBITDA margin expansion, and revised down its prior Q4 view on a slower Education recovery plus incremental pressure from one large ETM client, while reaffirming the full-year revenue and margin plan.

Novavax reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $68 million, a decrease from $70 million in the prior year, driven by reduced R&D reimbursement offset by product sales growth and a $125 million milestone. The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted revenue guidance to a midpoint of $400 million (range $385M-$415M) and improved expense guidance to a midpoint of $385 million. Management highlighted strong execution, including the initiation of Sanofi's Phase III trial in Europe and continued commercial momentum for Nuvaxovid.

Q3 revenues of $426 million rose 13% YoY, driven by M&A revenue up 40% and a record quarter in capital structure advisory, partly offset by softer capital markets after a record H1; first nine months revenue hit a record $1.15 billion, up 10%. Adjusted comp ratio improved to 65.8% from 66.2%, but adjusted pre-tax margin slipped to 21.4% from 22.2% as non-comp expenses rose, with full-year non-comp growth guided to approximately 19%. Management cited new business origination and announced pipeline up roughly 20% YoY with total pipeline at a record, while flagging macro and AI-financing volatility and a softer capital markets quarter. No formal revenue or EPS guidance was given, though management reiterated an expectation of some full-year comp leverage and flagged a few points of tax-rate headwind from Section 162(m) in 2027.

MBIA reported a consolidated GAAP net loss of $24 million (negative $0.49 per share) for Q3 2026, versus a $8 million net loss (negative $0.17) in Q3 2025, driven by a smaller loss and LAE benefit of $12 million versus $50 million a year ago. Adjusted net loss was $3 million (negative $0.06 per share) versus adjusted net income of $51 million ($1.03 per share) in the prior year, with the variance from a $54 million prior-year PREPA-driven benefit versus $3 million of current-quarter LAE and reserve accretion. National statutory net income fell to $18 million from $73 million; book value per share was negative $46.87, down $2.60 from year-end. Management gave no explicit earnings guidance, declined to discuss PREPA negotiation offers, pricing on claim sales, or transaction price, but said it continues to pursue reducing $390 million of gross PREPA par and an eventual sale of the company.

MasterBrand reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.04 billion (incl. $356 million from American Woodmark), with legacy MasterBrand sales down 2.5% YoY, adjusted EBITDA of $86 million at an 8.3% margin (down 470 bps), gross margin down 660 bps to 24.6%, and a GAAP net loss of $9.2 million (-$0.05/share; adjusted EPS $0.10 vs $0.33 prior year). Q4 guidance implies net sales of $958-$988 million and adjusted EBITDA of $38-$48 million (4.0%-4.9% margin), with second-half revenue below the prior August range and adjusted EBITDA midpoint at the low end of the prior range; the FY2026 end-market outlook was cut to down high-single digits from mid-single digits. Management lowered its net leverage target of below 2x to end-2029 from end-2028 and expects Q4 adjusted diluted loss per share of -$0.12 to -$0.08. Positives include roughly $9 million in realized synergies, IEEPA duty refunds, and market outperformance, offset against lower volume, unfavorable mix, and cost inflation outpacing pricing.

Q3 net sales were $500 million, down ~2% organically and ~3% as reported, with adjusted EBITDA of $62 million down 7% and margin contracting 50 bps to 12.5%. FAM delivered record organic growth of over 11% and EBITDA up 20% with 150 bps margin expansion to 18.1%, while SAS sales fell more than 10% and EBITDA dropped 25% on the Wisconsin tornado (a $20-25 million sales hit), healthcare destocking, and 50% Canadian tariffs. Q4 adjusted EBITDA is guided to a low single-digit percent decline year-over-year on temporary storm and tariff costs, even as both segments are expected to grow volume; full-year revenue, earnings, and cash are still expected ahead of 2025. Management framed the headwinds as transitory, citing YTD EBITDA up 8%, margins up 100 bps, free cash flow up 5%, and net leverage improving to 3.8x.

Insight Enterprises reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue of $2.4 billion (up 22% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.59 (up 34%). Gross profit grew 20%, driven by strong infrastructure hardware growth (>50%) and cloud services, while management raised its full-year 2026 gross profit growth guidance to 12.5%-14% and adjusted EPS midpoint to $13.75.

Mattel reported Q3 net sales up 4% as reported (3% constant currency) to $1.81 billion, with adjusted gross margin up 480 bps to 55% — though $88 million of tariff refunds contributed 490 bps — adjusted operating income of $502 million and adjusted EPS of $1.30 versus $0.91. However, full-year guidance was cut to 1-4% constant-currency net sales growth, roughly 48% adjusted gross margin, adjusted operating income of $500-570 million and EPS of $1.05-$1.20, citing softer-than-expected POS that decelerated late in Q3 and continued into Q4 across major markets. Management deferred 2027 guidance and any updated strategic plan to the February call, and declined to detail drivers of the POS slowdown or whether it was Mattel-specific or industry-wide.

Q3 FY2026 net sales grew 25% YoY to $1.127 billion on strong commercial volume, with adjusted EBITDA up 19% to 26.5% margin. The margin decline was driven by data center mix, as Nortek Data Center Cooling growth compressed commercial margins to 26% from 28% prior year. Orders grew 26% combined and 37% in commercial, with record backlog of $3.2 billion, up 119% YoY, and book-to-bill of 1.26x. Full-year guidance was raised to net sales of $4.05-$4.125 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $1.04-$1.07 billion, implying approximately 26% margins.

Live Nation reported Q3 FY2026 Concerts attendance above 60 million fans, up nearly 20% YoY, with international up 29% and every region up at least 15%; stadiums drove over half of global fan growth. Ticketmaster AOI guidance was raised to high single-digit growth for the full year, supported by 20 million-plus net new tickets and large Q3 on-sales (Harry Styles, Bruno Mars, Oasis, Metallica). Full-year fan count was guided toward close to 180 million, roughly 3% above prior expectations, while Concerts full-year AOI growth was reiterated at double digits with no change. Management repeatedly deferred Venue Nation, capital deployment, and pre-opening cost detail to next week's Investor Day.

Lyft reported Q3 FY2026 gross bookings up 17% YoY to $5.6 billion, adjusted EBITDA up 47% to $204 million (3.6% of bookings, a company record), and 273.5 million rides, up 10% YoY with North American rides accelerating for a second straight quarter. 31.6 million active riders marked the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, driver hours hit an all-time high, and trailing 12-month free cash flow exceeded $1 billion for a fifth consecutive quarter. Management said Q4 guidance absorbs near-term costs of the new Lyft Go/DoorDash membership and pointed to a third straight quarter of North American rides acceleration, but did not restate specific Q4 bookings or EBITDA figures on the call; the October 1 insurance renewal carried very modest growth. Repurchases were about $50 million in Q3 with roughly $500 million expected for the full year, and the company introduced new CFO Michael Brous, who framed the outlook as continuity rather than a reset.

Total Q3 2026 revenue fell to $11.3 million from $14.2 million a year ago, driven by lower Novo licensing revenue ($10.0 million vs $13.2 million), while INPEFA net sales rose to $1.2 million from $1.0 million. Net loss widened to $14.0 million ($0.03/share) from $12.8 million, with R&D down to $16.2 million and SG&A up to $9.5 million; 2026 opex guidance was reiterated at $100-110 million. Both key catalysts slipped: ZYNQUISTA NDA resubmission, delayed by STENO1 data formatting and FDA alignment, and SONATA-HCM top-line are now both expected in Q1 2027 (resubmission previously guided earlier). Q3 included a third $10 million Novo milestone, and cash rose to $183.2 million from $125.2 million at year-end 2025.

El Pollo Loco reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $126.3 million, up from $121.5 million, with systemwide same-store sales up 5% (company comps +4.4%, franchise +5.3%) and restaurant contribution margin of 18.4% versus 18.3% a year ago. GAAP EPS fell to $0.23 from $0.25 and adjusted EPS to $0.24 from $0.27, while adjusted EBITDA slipped to $17.1 million from $17.4 million on higher G&A ($14 million, 11.1% of sales). Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated for adjusted EBITDA of $68-$70 million (near the middle) with comps of approximately 4.5%, and Q4-to-date system comps were +3.6% through October 28. Management expects to accelerate new-unit openings to 25-30 in 2027 from 18-20 in 2026, and noted the consumer is stretched and that pricing versus inflation will be balanced carefully next year.

Lincoln reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted operating income available to common stockholders of $339 million, or $1.72 per diluted share, including a $95 million ($0.48/share) after-tax hit from the annual assumption review; adjusted operating income excluding that review rose 10% year-over-year on strong alternative investment returns (16.5% annualized vs. a 10% target, $55 million above target after tax). Life operating income excluding the review jumped to $130 million from $54 million on favorable mortality and alternatives, and RPS rose to $55 million from $46 million, while Group Protection earnings fell to $77 million from $110 million with the margin down 260 bps to 5.5% on a 670 bps rise in the disability loss ratio to 83.4%. Management guided Q4 annuities earnings roughly flat sequentially, life up $12-17 million from Talcott, RPS in line with the prior-year quarter on ~$3 billion of net outflows, and now expects Group to finish the year at or modestly below the low end of the prior 8%-9% margin range; the company also retired over 40% of preferred, closed the Talcott transaction, and resumed buybacks, with a 2027 outlook due in February.

Q3 FY2026 IFP reached $1.55 billion, up 34% YoY (12th straight quarter of accelerating growth), revenue rose 73% to $336 million, and gross profit rose 48% to a record $118 million. Adjusted EBITDA loss was $20 million, improved from $26 million, and adjusted free cash flow was positive for a sixth consecutive quarter at $27 million. Guidance calls for ~33% IFP growth and ~52% Q4 revenue growth with positive Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $5-9 million; full-year revenue guidance rose by $16 million but the EBITDA range was unchanged, which management attributed to a modest pet loss-ratio headwind. GAAP net loss widened to $44 million ($0.56 per share) from $38 million ($0.51), driven by higher stock-based compensation and interest expense, and Europe's loss ratio was elevated with 29 points from catastrophes and large losses.

Q3 2026 revenue was $1.1 billion, broadly flat reported and down 2% rebased, with residential fixed and B2B declines, while adjusted OIBDA rose 3% rebased to $454 million and consolidated adjusted OIBDA margin expanded 160 bps to ~41%. Revenue and OIBDA both grew sequentially over Q2. Segment results were mixed: Panama revenue fell 5% on government project phasing though residential fixed grew 3% and mobile subscription revenue 6%; Liberty Networks OIBDA fell 16% rebased on an El Salvador build cost/revenue timing mismatch; Costa Rica margin expanded ~300 bps to ~40% and Puerto Rico OIBDA rose 8% rebased despite a 3% revenue decline. Guidance was qualitative rather than numeric: management expects a strong Q4 with improved results and full-year adjusted FCF comfortably ahead of 2025, and now expects Jamaica FCF headwind comfortably below the prior $100 million estimate; buybacks exceeded $150 million year-to-date, nearly 10% of year-end 2025 shares.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $1.1 billion, broadly flat reported and down 2% rebased, with declines in residential fixed and B2B partly offset by mobile service growth. Adjusted OIBDA rose 3% rebased to $454 million and consolidated margin expanded 160 bps to about 41%. Management gave no explicit numeric guidance but said it expects a strong Q4 with improved results, full-year free cash flow comfortably ahead of 2025, and Jamaica free cash flow headwinds below the prior $100 million estimate. Year-to-date adjusted free cash flow before partner distributions was slightly positive, about $140 million above the first nine months of 2025, and roughly $150 million of buybacks so far in 2026 represent about 10% of year-end 2025 shares.

Nutrien reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.31 billion and raised full-year guidance for both potash sales volumes (to 14.3-14.8 million tons) and nitrogen sales volumes (to 9.3-9.7 million tons). Retail adjusted EBITDA was revised down to a range of $1.72-$1.85 billion due to intentional volume reductions in Brazil and weather impacts, though the company reiterated mid-single-digit annual growth expectations for the business. Management highlighted record potash volumes, strong proprietary product margins, and a disciplined capital allocation strategy including increased share repurchases.

AEye reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $506,000, up roughly 2.5x sequentially and about 10x year-over-year, marking a fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth. Gross margin improved by 45 percentage points though remained negative, GAAP net loss was $11.2 million ($0.24 per share) versus $10 million ($0.22) in Q2, and non-GAAP net loss improved to $7.2 million ($0.15) from $7.6 million ($0.17). Management issued first-ever revenue guidance of approximately $1 million for Q4, framed as a new quarterly baseline with meaningful growth into 2027, and targeted about 15% lower cash consumption in 2027 against an expected $35 million of FY2026 burn, with runway into 2028 on $63.1 million of cash. The key changes versus prior periods were the first STRATOS revenue shipment, the binding multi-million-dollar Lunar Outpost agreement now contributing revenue, and paid POC customers rising 28% sequentially to 32.

LifeStance reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $456 million, up 25% and ahead of expectations, with visit volumes up 17% to 2.7 million and revenue per visit up 7% to $170. Adjusted EBITDA rose 70% to $68 million (15% margin, second straight quarter at that level), Center Margin was 35.4% of revenue, and net income was $22 million versus $1 million a year ago. Management raised full-year guidance across all metrics, lifting revenue by $46 million at the midpoint to $1.741-1.761 billion, Center Margin to $599-613 million, and Adjusted EBITDA to $242-250 million. For 2027 management flagged a temporary 1-2 point revenue growth headwind from the new EHR rollout, putting growth toward the low end of the mid-teens long-term range, while still expecting margin expansion.

Natera reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $794 million, up approximately 34% year-over-year (north of 40% excluding true-ups), driven by a record 1.1 million tests processed and strong growth in oncology MRD volumes which rose 56%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $3.005-$3.035 billion, increasing the midpoint by approximately $140 million compared to prior guidance. The company also set a long-term goal to double revenues to $6 billion by 2029.

Nu Skin reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $311 million and adjusted EPS of $0.10, both within the previously issued guidance range. Gross margin contracted to 65% from 70.5% in the prior year due to revenue mix shifts between core and Rhyz businesses. Management reiterated full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $0.55-$0.65 while noting ongoing pressures in the core business.

Centrus reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $55.5 million, down 26% YoY, with LEU segment revenue down 29% and Technical Solutions down 21% on a $10.2 million drop in HALEU Operation Contract revenue. Normalized results swung to a net loss of $10.2 million (adjusted loss of $9.4 million, $0.46/share) versus adjusted net income of $5.2 million a year ago; GAAP figures included a $46.4 million non-cash warrant gain. Full-year revenue guidance of $450-500 million and capital spend of $350-500 million were reaffirmed, not raised, and the Q4 implied revenue of roughly $142-192 million carries the year. Backlog grew to $7 billion ($5.4 billion contingent enrichment commitments, $5.1 billion definitive) and cash stood at $2.2 billion after a ~$500 million equity offering, while a $116 million Westerman acquisition closed after quarter-end.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was CAD 498 million, up 22% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of CAD 96 million (19.3% margin, down from 20.2%) and adjusted diluted EPS flat at CAD 0.37 as a higher share count offset 26% higher adjusted net income. Satellite Systems rose 26% and Geointelligence rose 25%, while Robotics grew only 2%. MDA raised FY2026 revenue guidance to CAD 1.9-1.95 billion (from CAD 1.8-1.9 billion) and adjusted EBITDA guidance to CAD 355-375 million (from CAD 330-370 million), while maintaining the 18-20% margin, CAD 225-275 million CapEx, and neutral-to-negative free cash flow outlook. Backlog was just under CAD 4 billion, down CAD 444 million YoY but roughly flat QoQ, and year-to-date free cash flow swung to negative CAD 116 million from positive CAD 185 million a year earlier.

NREF reported a net loss of $0.65 per diluted share and earnings available for distribution of $0.52 per diluted share in Q3 FY2026, compared to $1.14 and $0.51 respectively in the prior year period. Cash available for distribution was $0.60 per share, exceeding the regular dividend of $0.50 per share. Management noted that both Earnings Available for Distribution (EAD) and Cash Available for Distribution (CAD) came in ahead of guidance.

NerdWallet reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $240 million (up 11% YoY) and non-GAAP operating income of $30 million, both missing the company's guidance range due to a $17 million decline in auto insurance revenue. Management lowered full-year expectations for NGOI to $85-$91 million, citing continued negative impact from vertical integration investments and AI projects. While consumer revenue grew 12% YoY, organic search traffic has stabilized after severe declines, and the company expects Q4 revenue of $191-$203 million.

Third quarter revenue was $212.2 million, up 18.8% year-over-year, with diluted EPS of $0.53 compared to $0.27 in the prior year. Management maintained full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $850 million-$900 million and expects gross margins to be approximately 14%, slightly higher than previously anticipated due to a decrease in chassis sales. The company returned $5.1 million to shareholders via dividends and share repurchases.

MP Materials reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $155.8 million (including PPA income), a 23.6% sequential increase driven by NdPr sales volumes up 94% year-over-year and higher realized prices. Adjusted EBITDA rose significantly to $53.7 million year-over-year, supported by the commercial launch of dysprosium and terbium separation circuits and the qualification of magnets for GM. Management raised full-year capital expenditure guidance to $500-$600 million due to heavy rare earth expansion and Chlor-Alkali startup, while maintaining strong liquidity of $1.34 billion.

Third quarter EBITDA was $2 billion, up 34% year-on-year, driven by structural margin improvements and the new European trade framework (TRQ). Management expects shipment growth to accelerate in Q4 with double-digit year-on-year improvement as destocking normalizes. The full benefits of the TRQ and capacity restarts are expected to materialize fully in 2027.
